1490120d-3b46-47d4-8eec-3c76ccfbb104.title: Remediate ActiveMQ Queue Saturation and Broker Memory Exhaustion
steps: Inspect the ActiveMQ broker memory configuration and calculate total potential queue usage by multiplying the per-queue memory limit by the number of active queues, comparing this value against total broker memory capacity.
Back up the ActiveMQ configuration file <ActiveMQ_Install_Dir>\bin\win64\wrapper.conf to a secure location before making changes.

Open <ActiveMQ_Install_Dir>\bin\win64\wrapper.conf in a text editor and set wrapper.java.maxmemory=2048 (or 4096 depending on workload requirements). Ensure per-queue limits adhere to the rule: Per-Queue Memory × Number of Queues ≤ Broker Memory (70% of JVM heap).
If queues remain locked or saturated preventing recovery, manually purge saturated queues and update stale database workflow records.
Restart the ActiveMQ service to apply the JVM heap and memory configuration changes.
Verify that agents polling the server resume receiving workflow assignments and that messages are actively drained from the queues without stalling.

103c28f3-8e70-4e53-9583-7fdded11966d.title: Workflow Operation Failure Due to Plugin or Environment Configuration Issues
steps: Verify folder permissions on the Process Studio installation directory and target destination directories. Ensure the operating system user running Process Studio has Full Access permissions to read, write, and modify files.

In Process Studio, click Tools > Sync plugins. In the AutomationEdge connection details window, enter the username and password, then click Connect. Once synchronization completes, reopen the .psw workflow file.
Close Process Studio. Navigate to the Process Studio installation directory. Delete the psplugins and .process-studio folders. Launch Process Studio by executing process-studio.bat.

Compare the plugin JAR versions and core libraries (such as GUI Plugin, Model Builder Plugin, ARC JAR, and SLF4J in the lib folder) installed in Process Studio against those installed on the AutomationEdge Server and Agent. Ensure all environments use identical versions.

For workflows utilizing Python-dependent plugins (such as Model Builder), verify the Python runtime path. Remove conflicting standalone Python installations and configure the plugin to point exclusively to the bundled Python distribution.
If encountering NoClassDefFoundError or unassigned plugin errors during execution, reassign the workflow to the target agent on the AutomationEdge platform, then restart the Agent service.

Inspect the project for orphan or unused workflows if publishing is blocked by project inspection rules (such as 'No Unused Workflows/Processes in a Project'). Remove or link unreferenced workflow files before re-publishing.

3b43efd6-edd1-42c1-9e20-d758a333286e.title: Office 365 Plugin Communication Protocol & Authentication Clarification
steps: Identify the specific plugin and operation referenced in the client inquiry (for example, Office 365 Send Mail, Office 365 Email Message Input, or legacy Out-of-the-Box Email Message Input).
Verify whether the client is using legacy Out-of-the-Box (OOTB) email steps relying on Basic Authentication (POP3/IMAP) or the dedicated Office 365 plugin steps.

Provide technical specifications to the client: confirm that Office 365 plugin steps (such as Send Mail and Email Message Input) are exclusively developed using Microsoft Graph APIs and use OAuth2 authentication (Password Grant and Refresh Token). If legacy OOTB steps are used, advise migrating to the Office 365 plugin steps.
Document the provided architecture clarification in the client ticket and verify if additional firewall, proxy, or Azure Entra ID permissions (Graph API permissions) are required.

2b39038a-93d7-48b7-95fb-cb37e9dc1d07.title: AutomationEdge Browser Driver Configuration and Compatibility Troubleshooting
steps: Identify the exact error message from the Agent or Process Studio execution logs to determine whether the failure is a driver deployment issue, a browser compatibility/instantiation issue, or a Chrome renderer crash.

Deploy or update the required browser driver (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or IE) through the AutomationEdge server. For on-premise instances, log in to the AutomationEdge UI as sysadmin, navigate to File Management, select GUI Automation Plugin, and upload the driver obtained from EPD. Do not place driver files directly into agent storage directories. For T3 cloud instances, sync the plugin directly.

If encountering 'Can not instantiate browser due to compatibility issue', update the Web GUI plugin based on the AutomationEdge version: update to web-gui-3.24.jar for AE 7.x, or web-gui-4.2.jar for AE 8.x. Open process-studio.bat and add the JVM flag: -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true

Configure the JVM flag on the Agent. For AE 7.x: go to the Agent installation directory, navigate to the bin folder, edit startup.bat, and add -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true. For AE 8.x: log in to the AutomationEdge UI, go to the Agents tab, select Edit Agent, and add -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true.

If running Chrome and receiving 'Unable to get web driver' or renderer errors on the agent machine, add --disable-features=RendererCodeIntegrity to the Chrome shortcut target properties. Apply the setting for all users by navigating to Compatibility > Change settings for all users.
Trigger a test execution of the Web-GUI automation workflow both from Process Studio and through the AutomationEdge Agent to verify browser launch and driver initialization.

15720699-c5ac-4581-9844-62dc090208d9.title: Chrome Extension Installation Blocked by Network Proxy
steps: Confirm that the extension installation failure is caused by network proxy restrictions blocking the Chrome Web Store.
Provide the client with the offline extension installation files and standard offline installation instructions.
Recommend that the client deploy and test the offline extension in a User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment prior to production rollout.
Coordinate with the client to finalize their deployment approach, confirming whether they will proceed with offline distribution or adjust network proxy allowlists.

2851114a-d353-4ec9-9793-07f870faf4e9.title: Investigation and Resolution Triage for Unidentified Intermittent or Critical Issues
steps: Request comprehensive diagnostic log bundles from the client and establish a scheduled window for direct technical availability to capture live diagnostics if recurrence happens.
Cross-reference observed failure symptoms and environment version metadata against internal engineering bug trackers, ongoing defect investigations, and upcoming software or plugin release notes.
Check if a matching bug record or target plugin/software release version (such as a 4.5 patch) has been identified by engineering.
Link the support case to the target engineering release ticket, inform the client of the planned fix version schedule, and close or defer the operational ticket pending release deployment.
Engage internal tier-3/core engineering for active investigation while maintaining enhanced monitoring on the affected environment to capture reproduction traces.

366dc902-4b9a-4151-886d-cecadfcdd442.title: OneDrive Plugin Refresh Token Generation Failure Due to Browser Encoding
steps: Verify that your Azure Active Directory application registration has a valid Custom redirect URI configured under Mobile and desktop applications (e.g., https://automationedge.com) and that delegated OneDrive permissions are granted.

Request an authorization code using Mozilla Firefox or a dedicated REST client instead of Google Chrome to prevent URL encoding corruption. Load the URL request: GET https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?client_id={client_id}&scope={scope}&response_type=code (replace 'common' with your Tenant ID if applicable).
Redeem the authorization code using the grant flow request to obtain the refresh token and access token.
Open the OneDrive Plugin Connection Configuration in the application, enter the generated token into the 'Refresh Token' field, and click 'Test Connection'.

43110cad-56e7-43be-a79a-acc79314fc0d.title: Client-Side Network and Firewall Restrictions Troubleshooting for AutomationEdge
steps: Test network socket reachability to your designated AutomationEdge endpoint (such as ondemand.automationedge.com or your tenant instance like t4.automationedge.com) on port 443 using a network tool like telnet.
Verify the configured server URLs by checking AEServerURL and Process Studio login URL inside the .psrc configuration file located under PS Home/.process-studio/.psrc.
Test connection from an alternate network (such as a mobile hotspot or non-corporate network) to isolate corporate network controls from external ISP blocks.

Check client proxy configuration. If an automatic proxy script is used, copy the script address from system proxy settings, download the .pac file in a browser, and verify IP range routing. Alternatively, test by temporarily removing the system-level proxy if direct access is allowed.

Engage the client IT network team or Internet Service Provider (ISP) to whitelist the AutomationEdge domain (e.g., ondemand.automationedge.com) and permit outbound traffic on port 443 for the affected client IP addresses.

4507acc0-f2f0-4160-97d9-553ca571b6dd.title: ML Plugin Compatibility and Input/Output Format Troubleshooting
steps: Inspect the AutomationEdge Agent logs and CPU capabilities. Verify that the agent machine processor supports the AVX (Advanced Vector Extensions) instruction set required by TensorFlow, and check logs for ProcessStudioException errors such as 'Cannot run program "python"' or missing package errors.

Verify the installed Python version and system environment variables on the Agent machine. For Machine Learning plugins (such as Model Builder), verify that Python 3.10 is installed rather than unsupported versions like Python 3.12, and ensure the Python installation path and Scripts directory are present in the system PATH environment variable.

Install required Python packages (such as scikit-learn, matplotlib, and TensorFlow dependencies) inside the designated Python 3.10 environment and ensure the service account running the Agent has full read/write permissions to the specified output directory.

Deploy the updated ML plugin JAR file if running Python 3.10 with tar.gz model outputs. In Process Studio, select 'Sync plugins' from the Tools menu to sync and restart Process Studio, then restart the AutomationEdge Agent service.

Validate the training input JSON structure and model path formatting. For Intent Entity Model Builder, ensure the input JSON syntax matches the validated sample schema for utterances, intents, and entities. For Intent Entity Prediction, ensure the model path parameter matches the output artifact type (either directory path or tar.gz archive).
Execute an end-to-end test execution of the workflow in Process Studio and on the Agent to verify model training and prediction inference.

023cc1ae-1168-4a0d-a5ae-1547db331edd.title: Process Studio Browser Launch Failure Due to Timeout/Delay
steps: Inspect the Start Browser stage properties in Process Studio and check the configured page load timeout and delay settings.
Increase the page load timeout value in the Start Browser stage parameters and add explicit delay handling for the target URL navigation.
Run the Start Browser stage in Process Studio to confirm the browser launches and successfully loads the target URL.

49877f87-6fe1-4e7e-939d-8e6e42bfe824.title: AutomationEdge Plugin and Library Compatibility Troubleshooting
steps: Inspect the error logs across Process Studio, Agent logs, or Server logs to identify whether the issue is a portal upload incompatibility, missing runtime dependency, version mismatch across environments, or corrupted plugin cache.

If uploading plugin JAR files on the AutomationEdge portal fails with 'No step or entry found in a plugin jar', open the Resource tab on the portal, review the plugin compatibility section in the plugin reference guide, and ensure the plugin release version matches the running AutomationEdge server version (for example, plugin release version 2.0 for AutomationEdge version 6.0) before uploading via the sysadmin login.

If the Agent fails with 'Cannot run program "python": CreateProcess error=2' or third-party dependency conflicts such as NoSuchMethodError, install the required Python runtime as administrator, set system environment variables, remove conflicting external Python packages or duplicate third-party JARs from the Agent external library directory, and restart the AutomationEdge Agent and Apache Tomcat services.

Remove any manually pasted JAR files from the Process Studio psplugins folder. Launch Process Studio, open the Tools menu, click sync plugins, provide the username and password in the AutomationEdge connection details window, and click Connect to synchronize plugins with the server.

If missing plugin errors or ClassNotFoundException persist after syncing, close Process Studio. Navigate to the Process Studio installation directory, delete the psplugins and .process-studio directories, then launch the application by running process-studio.bat.

Open the .psw workflow file in Process Studio and verify that all workflow steps load without error. Export or import the workflow onto the AutomationEdge server to verify version parity between Process Studio and the server.

4ad47337-d421-4408-b46d-0a590e66813f.title: License Invalidation Due to Server Hardware Replacement or MAC Address Change
steps: Check the License-Details tab in the AutomationEdge UI (AEUI) to inspect the expiry date and status of the latest uploaded license.
Open CMD and execute the command "getmac" on the host machine to obtain the current system MAC address.
Compare the host's current MAC address against the MAC address specified in the uploaded AE license file and the database table: check database vae > ae_license (or ae_license_details) > Mac_Address.
Evaluate whether the system MAC address matches the license MAC address or has changed.

If the MAC address has not changed or logs report blank/null MAC addresses, restart the PostgreSQL, ActiveMQ, and Tomcat services, or reboot the host machine, then attempt to re-upload the license file.
If the MAC address changed, coordinate with the internal IT team to determine if the change was unintentional and attempt to roll back the MAC address to its previous value.
If rollback is not possible or the hardware was permanently replaced, request an updated license file from the licensing team reflecting the new host MAC address.
Apply and upload the new license file via the AutomationEdge portal.
Verify that license details display properly in AEUI and confirm that Process Studio launches without license invalidation errors.

289aa11e-5147-4566-b24b-be0304aed712.title: BOT Login Failure Due to Application-Specific Error
steps: Inspect the BOT execution logs and capture the exact application response and error message received immediately after credential submission.
Escalate the incident to the application development team, providing the BOT identifier, timestamp, and captured error logs from the login failure.
Trigger a test execution of the BOT login workflow once the application team confirms the fix is deployed.

4e0c8d37-6dd7-4b1d-9143-027c55bbf361.title: Advanced REST Client Plugin Defects and Configuration-Related Data Inconsistencies
steps: Identify the primary symptom: check whether the issue is a data inconsistency (such as duplicate staging records created during update operations) or an API execution failure (such as URL encoding errors, S3 upload failures, or log download bugs).
For duplicate staging record creation, check the global system property 'Create Staging request on every update operation' in ServiceNow.
Set the global property 'Create Staging request on every update operation' to 'No' in ServiceNow.

For API request execution failures (such as 'Illegal character in path', S3 upload errors, or log download failures), test the target URL in Postman and compare behavior against AutomationEdge REST Client / Advanced REST Client execution. Check whether query strings contain explicit '%20' or unhandled special characters.
If URL encoding issues occur (e.g., '%20' handling), temporarily remove manual URL encoding like '%20' from the query parameters and use unencoded values in the request configuration.
Deploy the updated Advanced REST Client plugin JAR (version 4.5 / advanced-rest-client-6.3-R4.5 or latest approved patch) to the AutomationEdge environment.
Run a test execution of the affected workflow (e.g., S3 upload, log download, or REST API query) and verify that no duplicate staging records are created.

4535b427-35c1-4034-85ea-36d8d0054918.title: Recurring Sweet32 Cipher Vulnerability in VAPT Scans
steps: Review the Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) report to identify the target hostnames, IP addresses, and ports flagged for the Sweet32 cipher vulnerability (CVE-2016-2183).
Create a backup copy of the target service or load balancer TLS configuration file before making cipher modifications.
Update the TLS cipher suite settings on the target server or load balancer to disable all 64-bit block ciphers, specifically 3DES and DES, and reload the service.
Scan or probe the modified endpoint to confirm 3DES ciphers are rejected and application traffic functions normally over TLS.
Notify the customer to run revalidation scans or User Acceptance Testing (UAT) against the updated endpoints.
Evaluate the UAT and revalidation results provided by the customer.

59cf37a5-341a-4af3-8d56-30459ef786dd.title: AutomationEdge Workflow Unassignment Management and Remediation
steps: Open the AutomationEdge UI (AEUI) and verify the target workflow's agent assignment status and scheduler status.
Determine if the workflow should remain scheduled for execution or be retired/paused.
If scheduled execution is required, assign the workflow to an active agent in AEUI, ensuring the agent does not exceed the 200-workflow limit.
If the workflow is intentionally being unassigned or decommissioned, disable or delete the active schedule in AEUI before completing unassignment.

In High Availability (HA) environments, clear the engine cache by executing a PUT request to http://localhost:8080/aeengine/rest/cache/clear with the header X-session-token set to the System Administrator authentication token.
Check the next scheduled run or trigger a test run in AEUI to confirm the assigned agent picks up and completes the workflow execution.

4f2d122d-54c2-47d2-a329-f0c5b1e7ddcf.title: Troubleshooting Advanced REST Client (ARC) Plugin Limitations and Failures
steps: Replicate the exact REST call outside Process Studio using an external tool (such as Postman) with identical headers, query parameters, and body to confirm whether the endpoint and credentials are valid.
Inspect the error log and request configuration for URL encoding and parameter issues, such as 'Illegal character in path' or unexpectedly empty response bodies.

When encountering malformed URLs, special characters in query strings, or empty responses from valid endpoints, construct the full request URL with all encoded query parameters upstream in a scripting step, and pass the complete URL string directly into the Advanced REST Client plugin URL field.
Check if the HTTP method is GET while a body payload is attached, resulting in 'The Input payload cannot be null' or execution rejections.

Remove the request body from HTTP GET steps. If the target API requires a request payload, convert the step method to POST or PUT, or use an external script step if a non-standard GET-with-body is strictly mandatory.
Check the execution log for 'SSLHandshakeException' or 'No subject alternative names matching IP address' errors.

To resolve SSL certificate SAN mismatch errors, switch the target URL from an IP address to the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) listed in the certificate SAN. If testing in non-production environments or accessing internal hosts without valid certificates, enable the 'Option to ignore SSL certificate validation' checkbox in the Advanced REST Client configuration.
Check if the API returns an HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect status code (or check ArcRespStatus) and fails to complete the transaction.

Bypass redirect limitations by either pointing the workflow directly to the final destination URL (obtained from the initial response Location header), executing the request via a curl/script step, or updating to a plugin JAR version containing redirect-handling enhancements.
Verify whether the workflow encounters port validation errors or receives null field values when routing through an error hop out of the Advanced REST Client step.

Upgrade the Advanced REST Client plugin to Release 4.8 or later to resolve port validation bugs. For error hop null fields, verify incoming fields prior to the error hop or handle error routing via status code inspection (checking the ArcRespStatus field) instead of relying solely on the plugin error hop.

500a36b6-cf6b-422c-8973-199c424bb352.title: AutomationEdge Component Startup, Connectivity, and Configuration Troubleshooting
steps: Check network reachability and port availability for the Agent Controller, AutomationEdge Server, and Tomcat management services, ensuring port 8081 has no port conflicts.

Verify the installed Java runtime environment path and version for AutomationEdge components, Tomcat, ActiveMQ, and the Agent runtime (confirm compatibility, such as using Java 11 where Java 8 is unsupported).

Inspect the AEHOME directory, `ae.properties` file, and agent folders for correct file permissions and verify binary integrity (confirm `javaw.exe` is present in the agent folder and has not been removed).

Review and update configuration parameters in `ae.properties` and Tomcat Java options. Verify the database key is set to `database.username` (not `database.user`), verify the `ae.properties` file path in Tomcat Java options, and ensure Tomcat log directory paths exist.
Inspect and update SSL/TLS certificates and URL bindings for Tomcat and the AutomationEdge Server.
Enable the Agent Controller tab in the AutomationEdge administration portal, ensure required workflow plugins are assigned, and start ActiveMQ, Tomcat, and the Agent Controller services.
Start the AutomationEdge Agent, assign it to the active Agent Controller, and verify user login and workflow execution (including Remote Desktop Protocol sessions).

0a6fa103-8cde-4b5c-9991-e362cbfe97a5.title: Process Studio Publishing Failure: vfsFilename is null
steps: Check the Process Studio error logs and publishing output to confirm the failure is caused by the 'vfsFilename is null' error during project upload.
Back up the existing Process Studio library directory and current JAR files to a rollback location.
Replace the existing publishing library with the updated Process Studio patch JAR file.
Update project field mappings in the publishing configuration and JSON request body to use lowercase field names.
Restart Process Studio, open the project, and attempt to publish to the OnDemand server.

50633763-da67-45c3-a164-3f1f65a5ffd7.title: AutomationEdge Redshift Connectivity Failure Due to JDBC Driver Incompatibility
steps: Check that the latest Redshift JDBC driver file (such as RedshiftJDBC42-*.jar) is present in the <Process Studio>\lib\ directory.
Restart AutomationEdge Process Studio to ensure the newly added driver JAR file is loaded into the Java classpath.
Open the database connection settings in AutomationEdge Process Studio and change the Connection Type to Generic Database instead of the native Redshift option.

Configure the Generic Database connection parameters:
- Set Driver Class to: com.amazon.redshift.jdbc.Driver
- Set JDBC URL to: jdbc:redshift://<host>:5439/<database>
- Enter the database Username and Password.
Click Test Connection in AutomationEdge Process Studio to validate database connectivity.

51f59d9e-6e04-4444-b804-9d6d53777ea3.title: AutomationEdge ActiveMQ Configuration and Performance Remediation
steps: Inspect <ActiveMQ_Install_Dir>\bin\win64\wrapper.conf to verify JVM heap allocation. If memory is insufficient or default, set wrapper.java.maxmemory=2048.

Open activemq.xml in <ACTIVEMQ_HOME>\conf\ (or C:/ActiveMQ/conf/activemq.xml). Check for syntax errors such as an extra '/' in <policyEntry topic="> /" > within the destinationPolicy section. Remove the invalid '/' if present, and confirm the broker configuration includes <broker useJmx="true" ...>.

Open the ae.properties file located in <AE_HOME> (the AutomationEdge installation directory). Locate activemq.broker.url and configure it with reconnect parameters, ensuring maxReconnectAttempts=10 (e.g., activemq.broker.url=tcp://localhost:61616 or failover URL with maxReconnectAttempts=10). Verify mq.username and credentials are set.
If queues are saturated with backlog requests that are not processing, purge stuck messages from the ActiveMQ queue and update any stale database records associated with stalled workflow executions.

Restart services in the exact required sequence: run 'net stop AutomationEdge', then 'net stop ActiveMQ', then 'net start ActiveMQ', and finally 'net start AutomationEdge'. Ensure only one ActiveMQ instance is running and bound to port 61616.
Log in to the ActiveMQ Console and check the AutomationEdge application logs to confirm successful broker connection and verify agent workflow assignment resumes.

6307b7a0-ae02-45bf-a925-3a5223b63d93.title: GUI Automation and Spy Troubleshooting in Process Studio
steps: Inspect system resource utilization (CPU and memory) on the workstation running Process Studio and check whether the required browser extension (such as the Chrome extension) is installed and enabled.

Check the Process Studio logs for error signatures. Identify whether the failure is a javassist bytecode error during plugin sync, a browser instantiation compatibility error, or a missing GUI Automation plugin JAR.

If encountering javassist/sync errors: Take a backup of the existing javassist JAR file from the Process Studio/Agent lib directory. Copy the latest javassist JAR file into the lib folder, replacing the existing file.

If encountering browser compatibility issues: Update to web-gui-3.24.jar (for 7.x) or web-gui-4.2.jar (for 8.x). Add the JVM flag -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true to process-studio.bat. For Agent execution, add the flag to startup.bat (in 7.x) or configure it via AE UI -> Agents tab -> Edit Agent (in 8.x).

If GUI Spy fails to load or capture elements: Verify the GUI Automation plugin directory. Ensure gui-automation-4.0-complete-custom.jar (or GUI Automation 4.0 JAR) is placed directly inside the Process Studio GUI Automation plugin folder.
Restart Process Studio, trigger a Web GUI plugin sync if prompted, and verify that GUI Spy successfully launches and captures target UI elements.

5526511a-5281-4565-822c-331fcf8e2d73.title: Intermittent Connection and Resource Exhaustion for Automation Services
steps: Inspect agent and server logs for the specific failure signature: look for socket timeouts, 'Connection refused' (org.apache.http.conn.HttpHostConnectException), 'Connection reset', or JDBC errors such as org.postgresql.core.v3.ConnectionFactoryImpl.enableSSL.

If database connection drops are suspected on PostgreSQL, enable diagnostic logging in postgresql.conf:
logging_collector = on
log_connections = on
log_disconnections = on
log_min_messages = info
log_hostname = on
Verify active connections via pg_stat_activity and compare against SHOW max_connections;.

If the agent encounters socket timeouts or enters an 'Unknown' state due to busy backend services, edit agent_home/conf/application.properties and add:
ae.connect.timeout=60
ae.socket.timeout=120

If PostgreSQL JDBC connections intermittently drop due to SSL negotiation failure when SSL is off on the database server, update the JDBC connection string to:
jdbc:postgresql://<servername>/<database_name>?currentSchema=public&sslmode=disable
Execute workflows multiple times under normal and elevated load to verify that database and agent-server connections remain stable without connection resets, socket timeouts, or SSL errors.

6356e42e-57ab-4a91-aab7-839e41934cd6.title: AutomationEdge Agent Registration Failure Due to Conflicting Host Details
steps: Inspect the agent startup log files on the host machine to confirm whether registration failed due to duplicate host details.
Check for any running AutomationEdge Agent processes on the local machine and stop them.
Log in to the AutomationEdge UI (AEUI) and search the registered agents list for any existing entries matching the target hostname and username across all machines.
Delete the conflicting or unused agent entry from the AutomationEdge UI.
Start the new agent on the target machine and verify in the AutomationEdge UI that the agent registers successfully and reports an online status.

661d1a34-b8bd-4910-93b2-b0b17af073e4.title: Process Studio Web GUI Synchronization Failure Due to JAR Mismatch
steps: Inspect the Process Studio or Agent 'lib' directory for the current 'javassist' JAR file version and review the error logs for 'Tampered Error' or 'JAR might be corrupted' messages.
Take a backup of the existing 'javassist' JAR file from the Process Studio or Agent 'lib' directory to a separate backup location.
Replace the existing 'javassist' JAR file in the Process Studio or Agent 'lib' directory with the latest compatible version.
Restart Process Studio.
Sync the Web GUI plugin again from Process Studio or Agent.

81359e7a-a5da-4881-80a6-b237b20a1e78.title: Remediating RPA Browser Compatibility Failures Post-OS Upgrade
steps: Identify the installed AutomationEdge version (7.x or 8.x) and inspect the execution logs for the error string 'Can not instantiate browser due to compatibility issue'.
Update the Web GUI plugin JAR file to the appropriate version for your platform: use web-gui-3.24.jar for AutomationEdge 7.x or web-gui-4.2.jar for AutomationEdge 8.x.
Open the process-studio.bat file in a text editor and add the JVM flag -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true to the execution command.
For AutomationEdge 7.x, navigate to the Agent installation directory, open the bin folder, edit startup.bat, and add the JVM flag -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true.
For AutomationEdge 8.x, open the AutomationEdge UI, navigate to the Agents tab, select Edit Agent, and add the JVM flag -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true.
Restart the AutomationEdge Agent and Process Studio, then trigger a test automation workflow that performs browser actions.

c87b0565-6935-41e4-9e0b-79fa078acf0b.title: AutomationEdge Job Processing Failures Due to Architectural Limitations
steps: Inspect the AutomationEdge (AE) server and agent versions, and identify active jobs stuck in 'Updating' state or failing termination.
Upgrade the AutomationEdge server and agents to version 8.4.0 or higher during an approved maintenance window.
Submit test workloads across agents to verify that job states transition out of 'Updating', manual job terminations complete cleanly, and concurrency constraints function as expected.

1dd2e1c3-d792-4860-9119-d9a87b4d282f.title: Application Startup Failure: Missing Dependencies or DB Migration Lock
steps: Inspect the application startup logs for missing dependency errors (such as ClassNotFoundException or NoClassDefFoundError) and query the database changelog lock table (DATABASECHANGELOGLOCK) to check if a migration lock is active.
Clear the stuck Liquibase database migration lock by resetting the lock status in the DATABASECHANGELOGLOCK table or executing the Liquibase unlock command.
Place the missing JAR file into the application classpath or shared library directory.
Synchronize the disaster recovery (DR) environment configuration, application artifacts, and database state to match the primary environment.
Restart the application server and send a test HTTP request to the application health check endpoint.

133bff80-bc4d-4bda-a0ba-26d9cb92be63.title: Environmental Restrictions on Preferred Technology Workaround
steps: Inspect execution logs and environment policy constraints to verify why the preferred technology (such as a Python script) was blocked or unsupported.
Export a backup copy of the existing pipeline or transformation configuration before introducing custom code.
Implement the approved custom alternative (such as a User Defined Java Class for Exchange Web Services) to replace the blocked script.
Run a test execution against a test mailbox to verify email fetching, unread email processing, marking processed emails as read, and storage of subject, body, and attachments.
Inspect the parsed output fields specifically for sender information and reply email identification to ensure no null values or missing metadata.

e3d27999-7af7-4ca3-9341-06811450ba6c.title: Plugin Enhancement for Dynamic Configuration Support
steps: Inspect the affected plugin configuration to confirm whether the field strictly expects static values and fails to parse dynamic expressions or runtime variables.
Assess the technical feasibility of dynamic evaluation for the target plugin parameter and identify whether temporary workflow workarounds exist.
Submit a formal feature enhancement request to the plugin development team with use cases, target fields, and request scheduling into an upcoming plugin release.

8cd6785d-0b28-4b77-ac10-8277c8f43345.title: Python Script Plugin Failure Due to Incorrect Parameters
steps: Inspect the plugin invocation logs and configuration to capture the exact parameter values and command-line arguments passed to the Python script during the failed execution.
Inspect the Python script's argument parsing logic (such as argparse, click, or sys.argv handling) and compare the script's required parameter schema against the values captured in step 1.
Update the plugin configuration or execution template to supply the correct parameter names, formats, and required values matching the Python script's specification.
Trigger the plugin execution with the updated parameters and monitor the output.

5effbe08-2e7b-4e50-aa21-64dd997a6467.title: Ambiguous Initial Component Setup and Configuration
steps: Review the environment architecture and gather required prerequisites for the Agent Controller and target Virtual Machines.
Inspect the local and domain Group Policy settings on the client machine to confirm whether 'Save Credentials' for Remote Desktop (RDP) is permitted.
Engage domain administrators to lift the Group Policy restriction on 'Save Credentials' for the RDP Controller host, as RDP Controller requires stored credentials to function.
Run the initial installation and configuration procedure for the Agent Controller and connect the target Virtual Machines.
Initiate an automated session from the Agent Controller to the target VM using the RDP Controller to verify end-to-end connectivity and credential handling.

79b4b410-204a-461a-bde1-e7e027742941.title: Web Automation 'Start Browser' Failure Troubleshooting
steps: Verify that the target web browser (such as Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge) is installed on the machine running Process Studio or the Agent.

Check the 'web-gui' directory and verify that the correct, compatible browser driver executable matching the installed browser version is present. If missing or incompatible, place the required browser driver in the 'web-gui' folder.
Update the Web GUI plugin to the version matching the AutomationEdge release: use 'web-gui-4.2.jar' for AutomationEdge 8.x, or 'web-gui-3.24.jar' for AutomationEdge 7.x.
Open the 'process-studio.bat' file in a text editor and add the JVM flag: -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true

Configure the JVM flag for the Agent: For AutomationEdge 8.x, open AutomationEdge UI, navigate to the Agents tab, click Edit Agent, and add '-DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true'. For AutomationEdge 7.x, navigate to the Agent installation directory, open the 'bin' folder, edit 'startup.bat', and append '-DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true'.
Restart Process Studio or the Agent service and execute the workflow containing the 'Start Browser' step to verify successful browser session initialization.

b8228a84-2824-463b-ac1e-f6658f6bde16.title: DocEdge Azure OCR Plugin Error Handling Failure
steps: Check the failed workflow instance to confirm that execution halted abruptly at the DocEdge Azure OCR Configuration step without triggering configured exception-handling or recovery paths.
Reconfigure the workflow execution path to route OCR processing through the Workflow Executor as a workaround instead of direct invocation by the plugin.
Trigger a test execution of the reconfigured workflow with sample OCR documents to verify that errors are trapped and normal recovery logic executes.
Check plugin repository availability for Plugins release 4.5 or later. When available, schedule and apply the update to permanently resolve the plugin error-handling bug.

8eba3ed9-f9c0-4e0b-b4ea-9b355b81ced6.title: DocEdge PDF Extraction Failure Due to Plugin Incompatibility
steps: Inspect DocEdge application and plugin logs for extraction failures, checking specifically for HTTP 410 Gone errors or API deprecation responses from external OCR endpoints.
Create a backup copy of the current DocEdge OCR plugin JAR file and related configuration settings before making changes.
Deploy the updated DocEdge OCR plugin JAR package to the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment.
Execute a test PDF extraction job in the UAT environment to validate compatibility with the active OCR API.
Deploy the verified DocEdge OCR plugin JAR package to the production environment during an approved maintenance window and restart the DocEdge service if necessary.
Process a test PDF extraction in production and verify end-to-end extraction results.

02582e53-c0e8-4f29-b80b-e21238d5a8fd.title: Missing Application Dependency JAR After Deployment
steps: Inspect the application startup logs to identify missing class errors and confirm if required dependency JAR files, such as snakeyaml-1.33.jar, are absent from the WEB-INF/lib directory.
Copy the required missing dependency JAR file (such as snakeyaml-1.33.jar) into the application's WEB-INF/lib directory.
Restart the Tomcat application server to load the added dependency.
Verify that the application initializes successfully and responds to standard health check requests.

5afb9e0c-d908-42e9-a779-ccd60172447b.title: Automated Browser Instability Post Chrome Update in Virtualized Environments
steps: Inspect the automation agent logs and Chrome crash reports to confirm the failure is a 'tab crashed' error during page rendering following a recent Chrome update.

Update the browser launch configuration or automation runner parameters to disable GPU hardware acceleration and force software rendering (for example, passing flags such as --disable-gpu and --disable-software-rasterizer or deploying an updated runner configuration JAR).
Execute a test automated browser workflow on the affected agent and observe page rendering stability.

f1ac9510-558b-4a74-ad99-95b486ee2640.title: Customer Inquiry for Non-Existent Out-of-the-Box Feature
steps: Verify whether the requested out-of-the-box functionality exists in the current platform release or is currently listed on the product development roadmap.
Send a response informing the customer that the requested capability is not currently available out-of-the-box in the platform.
Communicate planned development milestones (such as an upcoming feature marketplace or future release) and note the customer's account for follow-up updates upon release.

409b55a7-6503-4abb-a6db-6585ee551a64.title: Stored Procedure Call Failure Due to Extraneous 'result' Parameter
steps: Inspect the database procedure invocation syntax in your application code or query interface. Check if an extra 'result' parameter is passed or if a redundant 'find' or lookup step is executed prior to calling the procedure.
Remove the extraneous 'result' parameter from the call definition and remove any redundant lookup steps that query for the procedure name.
Execute the stored procedure call from the application or client interface and verify that data returns without parameter mismatch errors.

cf597e4e-52aa-4566-9f22-6bb7e9783ce5.title: Concurrent Database Row Update Conflicts
steps: Inspect the executing workflow definitions and identify parallel steps targeting the same database rows (for example, an Insert/Update step running concurrently with a SQL Script plugin on the referral_documents table).
Move the conflicting Insert/Update step into a separate, sequential workflow to eliminate concurrent write operations against the target records.
Execute the separated workflows and check database lock monitoring and execution logs to ensure updates complete without transaction errors.

feb3bac5-9af5-4722-8583-45a363675ff4.title: AEUI Access and Functionality Impairment Troubleshooting
steps: Inspect the failure symptom at the client tier. Check if the error is a client-side network error popup, a browser rendering issue, or an HTTP error returned by the server.
Check client browser compatibility, verify the Web GUI plugin version, and ensure any required client or server Java Virtual Machine (JVM) flags are enabled.
Create a timestamped backup copy of web.xml and any related web server configuration files before editing them.
Inspect the web.xml configuration file for XML syntax errors, malformed tags, or invalid comment blocks (such as unclosed or nested XML comment tags).

Review and update the HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) header definitions in the AEUI web server configuration to ensure all required header parameters and directives are correctly formatted.
Restart the AEUI application service to apply changes made to web.xml and security header configurations.
Open AEUI in a supported browser, access the login portal, and perform a test sign-in.

If the AEUI configuration is verified valid but access remains blocked in the specific environment, request the customer IT and security teams to inspect internal firewall rules, endpoint protection policies, proxy configurations, or group policies blocking the AEUI traffic.

1ce75db6-f702-4104-a62f-5918246b3152.title: Routine User Account and License Administration
steps: Identify the specific request type from the ticket: dormant account reactivation, license renewal, or additional license provisioning.
If the ticket is for account access, unblock and enable the dormant user account in the user directory.
If the ticket is for licensing, approve the renewal or assign the requested license seats to the user account.
Verify that the account displays as active and all requested license entitlements are correctly reflected in the administrative console.

e0ed8dd9-147f-44c7-8bb6-af42b40f708b.title: Get File Name Plugin Functionality Issues: Environmental & Configuration Related
steps: Inspect the file path configured in the 'Files Exist plugin' or 'Get file name plugin' against the actual target location on the SFTP or local server.
Update the target file path in the plugin configuration to point to the correct SFTP or shared directory.
Check network reachability, shared folder accessibility, and file system permissions from the agent host to the target directory or SFTP location.
Restart the agent service with administrative rights (elevated privileges).
Rerun the workflow and monitor the application, system, and event logs for successful plugin execution.

b89259ed-960d-4610-bab2-0f9558dcec86.title: Copilot User Agent Visibility Misunderstanding in T3
steps: Determine whether the ticket involves unassigned Copilot plugins or an inquiry regarding missing agent assignments in the T3 instance.
Assign the required Copilot plugin to the requested user account.
Inform the user that the system architecture in the T3 instance does not assign agents to Copilot users by design.

124c3503-0428-4b58-8d1d-ddd71ee455fc.title: Copilot Workflow Overwrite and Data Loss Recovery
steps: Inspect the Copilot environment, file system, and revision history to check whether any platform snapshot, export archive, or version backup of the overwritten workflow file exists.
Make a copy of the current truncated workflow file to preserve any valid parameters, then re-develop the missing workflow steps manually based on the original operational specifications.
Run a test execution of the rebuilt workflow in a non-production or staging scope to verify all steps complete without errors.
Export a backup copy of the verified workflow file and store it in an external version-controlled repository to prevent unrecoverable data loss from future overwrites.

7a63ba42-cead-4525-bb51-ff470341718d.title: Process Studio Unicode Character Conversion Failure Remediation
steps: Inspect the input string retrieved from the database in Process Studio to identify non-ASCII Unicode homoglyph characters (such as Cyrillic letters resembling Latin characters like Р, Т, or В).
Add a Modified Java Script Value (MJSV) step into the Process Studio workflow pipeline immediately following the database retrieval step and prior to the Surface Automation Plugin.
Import or paste the script from unicode_to_ascii_converter.txt into the MJSV step, map the database input string field to the conversion script, and assign the output to a cleaned string field.
Run a test execution passing the cleaned output field into the Surface Automation Plugin and verify that the target application receives standard ASCII text without garbage characters.

7d5d6db1-21a1-4417-a781-5c69656bc76b.title: Troubleshooting Automation Tool Incompatibility with Canvas-Rendered Web Applications
steps: Inspect the web page structure using browser developer tools to verify whether the target interface is rendered inside an HTML5 canvas element or Flutter framework wrapper rather than accessible HTML DOM nodes.
Test direct DOM click actions using the web automation plugin to confirm whether pointer events are captured or ignored by the canvas layer.
Attempt coordinate-based or OS-level pointer click actions at the target element's absolute screen coordinates, ensuring the browser window maintains focus and standard display scaling.

Escalate the automation design to the development team to evaluate framework-specific automation drivers (such as Flutter Driver), enabling semantic/accessibility trees in the target application, or switching to backend API integration.

a6d92da3-d988-4cd4-a3da-8a9551757201.title: Workflow Import Failure Due to Missing Tenant Plugin Assignment
steps: Inspect the workflow requirements and check the tenant's active plugin list to identify which required plugin is unassigned.
Assign and enable the missing plugin for the target tenant.
Retry the workflow import in the tenant environment.

d68c99db-f072-4b36-89e4-c5b1c6d9f06f.title: Active Directory/LDAP Integration Troubleshooting and Plugin Upgrade
steps: Inspect the application LDAP/AD configuration parameters, including hostnames, ports, bind DNs, base DNs, and attribute mappings, for syntax errors or invalid parameter values.
Check the currently installed AD/LDAP plugin version and compare it against compatibility matrices for the target Windows Server Domain Controller version.
Upgrade the application AD/LDAP plugin to the version verified to support the target Windows Server and AD schema.
Perform authentication and directory lookup validation tests in a User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment before promoting changes to production.

4c6c1bb2-5764-49b2-bb0d-22487c010f4d.title: API Lacks Bulk Processing Support
steps: Send a single-record test payload directly to the API endpoint using Postman, then send a bulk or multi-record payload to the same endpoint.
Check the API behavior and error response from Postman to verify whether the API is structurally constrained to single-record transactions.
Notify the client that the endpoint only supports single-record processing and advise their development team to update the API design if bulk execution or batch file uploads are required.
Instruct the client to validate any newly implemented API updates directly in Postman before reconnecting through the Advanced REST Client plugin or other integration tools.

a3418c80-51e0-4557-a8f0-9a1b6a1c5649.title: Process Studio Launch Failure Troubleshooting
steps: Inspect the local client environment to verify Java runtime prerequisites, single sign-on configuration, and plugin assignments.
Verify that a valid Process Studio license is assigned to the target user and that local license files are not corrupted.
Create a new user profile on the machine and assign Process Studio access and required plugins to test for profile corruption.
Deregister the existing Process Studio client instance, download a fresh installation package, install it, and re-register the client.
Launch Process Studio and confirm that the main interface opens and all assigned plugins load without error.

4f22e660-6c49-47f0-8df3-e68f61f5bf80.title: Missing or Unassigned DocEdge Plugins Causing Workflow Failures
steps: Inspect the failure details of the affected workflow (such as WF_DataExtraction) to identify the specific missing DocEdge plugins (such as 'DocEdge: Converter And Crop' and 'DocEdge: GenAI'), the target Organization Code, and the server name.
Assign the required DocEdge plugins (such as 'DocEdge: Converter And Crop' and 'DocEdge: GenAI') to the target Organization Code or server.
Re-run the failing workflow (such as WF_DataExtraction) to verify that the DocEdge plugins initialize and process tasks successfully.

2d5889e7-8aec-400e-89c6-bd2b455d8c3a.title: Process Studio Functionality and Deployment Failures
steps: Examine the failure symptom and deployment error message to distinguish between a local Process Studio client issue and a target server plugin error.
Close and restart Process Studio to clear transient memory states or publishing session locks.

Check the plugin list and plugin version numbers on the target server, comparing them against the plugins utilized in Process Studio (specifically verify that GUI Plugin version 4.7 is not deployed to an environment running a version earlier than 4.7).
Upload the missing plugins or update plugin versions on the target server so that they match or maintain compatibility with the version used in Process Studio.
Re-attempt workflow publishing from Process Studio to the target environment and execute a test run of the workflow.

929e3ef9-f1b6-4660-9df4-92c32e9d3bd1.title: Custom Development for Advanced Data Handling Requirements
steps: Assess the data handling requirement against standard platform plugins and check environment execution constraints, such as PowerShell script execution policies.
Develop and embed custom Java code using a User Defined Java Class (UDJC) step within the data pipeline to handle the unsupported logic (e.g., generating password-protected ZIP files).
Test the pipeline with sample data and verify that the output files meet client format and security specifications (e.g., verify password prompt and file contents upon extraction).

49b22f43-4810-4645-bcc5-fe44934a6c52.title: AI Studio Initial Configuration and Integration Issues
steps: Identify whether the issue is related to internal API and port bindings or external service integrations (such as WhatsApp integration or PostgreSQL database connectivity for AutomationEdge Reports).
Verify the allocated API settings and listening ports in the AI Studio configuration files, ensuring no port conflicts exist on the host.
Validate and provide integration parameters for external services, including WhatsApp credentials for AI Studio and PostgreSQL host, port, user, and database details for AutomationEdge Reports.
Perform an end-to-end connectivity test to confirm successful API responses and data flow between AI Studio and configured external services.
Escalate unresolved API, port, or custom integration issues to the AI Studio engineering team with current configuration logs, port binding maps, and target endpoint details.

1787d10e-0af2-41cd-9d44-16a2bad80c09.title: Expired or Missing SSL/TLS Certificate Resolution
steps: Inspect the SSL/TLS certificate details on the target endpoint to verify expiration dates, certificate chain validity, and subject alternative names.
Back up the existing certificate files, private keys, and web server or load balancer TLS configuration files to a secure backup directory.
Deploy the updated, valid SSL/TLS certificate, private key, and required intermediate/root CA certificates to the target endpoint or load balancer, then reload or restart the service listener.
Validate the endpoint connection using a secure client or validation tool to confirm that the new certificate is active, trusted, and presenting the correct expiration date and chain.

7bd7d53a-b95a-417a-9593-83b5961026a8.title: PowerShell Session Instability with Windows PowerShell Plugin
steps: Review the plugin configuration to verify how session initialization, lifetime, and session reuse are configured.

Open a PowerShell session to the target host directly from the plugin runner host using standard PowerShell remoting (Enter-PSSession or New-PSSession) to verify network connectivity, WinRM status, and user permissions.
Update the Windows PowerShell plugin settings to ensure sessions are properly initialized before running commands, and adjust session reuse options to match the workload requirements.
Run a multi-step test command sequence through the plugin to confirm that the PowerShell session initializes cleanly, executes commands, and maintains state as expected.

aaed0acd-6ede-4700-b5e7-c538b89286c9.title: External Service Plugin Connectivity Failure due to Expired Token
steps: Inspect the agent configuration and connection logs to check for token expiration errors and verify whether proxy configuration settings are defined.
Generate a new session token key in the external service management interface and update the plugin configuration file with the new key.
Update the agent server configuration with the required outbound proxy host, port, and proxy credentials if proxy settings are missing.
Restart the agent service to reload the updated session token and proxy settings.
Test integration connectivity by executing a test sync or verifying that live events process successfully without authentication or network errors.

dc6daec5-5c60-4a62-a348-be213cb27686.title: Workflow Variable Passing Failure
steps: Inspect the parent and child workflow definitions. Examine the variable mapping configurations, step transition logic, and any intermediary plugin steps that process or modify payload data.
Remove unnecessary plugins from the workflow definition and update the variable passing logic to directly pass required fields into the child workflow.
Trigger a test execution of the parent workflow and inspect the child workflow's input parameters.
Escalate to the workflow platform engineering team, providing the parent and child workflow identifiers, execution IDs, and variable trace logs.

7d2a08ea-d1a2-4f4b-82d8-a934836d2b3d.title: Manual AutomationEdge Custom Role Provisioning
steps: Review the service request to confirm the target environment, requested custom role name, and the specific feature permissions needed.
Log in to the AutomationEdge administration portal for the target environment and create the custom role with the requested feature access settings.
Verify the role configuration in the AutomationEdge administration portal to ensure all requested feature permissions are assigned correctly.
Add a resolution note with the configured role details to the service request ticket and close it.

7c297e44-b3a2-4b9a-b2f6-9880ec8cf076.title: Incorrect LDAP User Email Attribute Mapping
steps: Inspect the LDAP configuration settings for the user email parameter mapping (such as AE_USER_EMAIL) and compare it against the directory schema attribute used for email storage (such as mail or userPrincipalName).
Export or record a backup of the current LDAP integration settings prior to applying configuration changes.
Update the AE_USER_EMAIL parameter in the LDAP configuration to point to the correct LDAP/Active Directory attribute and save the configuration.
Initiate a test user synchronization or authenticate an affected user account to verify that the email address is accurately populated.

e77d4509-4db9-45d5-af1f-0894c7c87e06.title: Manual User License Renewal Approval Process
steps: Check the user account status and identify whether the account is active, disabled, or dormant, and note the specific license type requiring renewal.
If the account is disabled or dormant, activate the user account before proceeding with the license renewal request.
Route the renewal request to the License Team and assign it to Fernando Baldin for manual approval.
Verify that formal approval has been granted by Fernando Baldin in the ticket.
Assign and apply the renewed license to the user account in the licensing console.
Confirm that the user account reflects active license status and notify the user that renewal is complete.

7a3489ec-92cd-4ddb-8a6f-ebdd04bb2431.title: Compliance Audit: Data in Transit Encryption Verification
steps: Identify all endpoints, load balancers, and external interfaces in scope for the audit, then extract current Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol versions, supported cipher suites, and certificate configurations.
Sanitize the collected evidence to ensure no private keys, internal credentials, or sensitive network secrets are exposed.
Compile the sanitized configuration extracts into the auditor-requested format and submit the evidence package to the requesting auditor or client.

96eb8b74-d116-43e1-92a1-e01ad797c564.title: Intermittent Folder Creation Failure on NFS Mounts with Generic Error
steps: Inspect the application workflow execution logs to extract the precise failure timestamp and the target directory path where createFolder() failed.
Examine the NFS client system logs and NFS storage server audit/event logs matching the recorded failure timestamp for network dropouts, RPC timeouts, stale file handles, or permission denials.
Perform a test folder creation and deletion directly in the target NFS directory from the host running the automation to determine if the issue was transient or persists.

If the issue is transient and self-resolved, advise the infrastructure team to monitor NFS connection stability and document the incident for upcoming platform enhancements that provide explicit file system error details.

b31f4e0e-0c9a-4763-bd29-723f8f94cffa.title: Environment Upgrade Blocked by Missing Software License
steps: Identify the specific license entitlement required for the environment (such as the required unit step count for the target upgrade version and VAPT remediation).
Acquire the required unit license file and upload it to the target environment.
Check if required metering utilities or supporting tools need to be downloaded under strict security or network constraints.
If single file downloads fail due to security controls, attempt downloading the entire enclosing directory or container folder, or request an approved internal transfer channel.
Draft and finalize the environment upgrade implementation plan, incorporating VAPT fix verifications.

b82e2207-34fb-40fd-8b10-50849bbb9d6c.title: Audit Log Purging Failure Due to Product Defect
steps: Inspect the audit log retention configuration and compare it against the oldest log timestamps present in storage.
Engage the product development team with purge job logs, software version details, and reproduction data to log a defect ticket.
Establish a temporary manual archival or log rotation schedule to prevent storage exhaustion until the official release patch is deployed.

785a8413-fb3a-4baa-a07b-db503c5c6f30.title: LDAPS Connection Failure Due to Certificate Chain and Java Version Mismatch
steps: Back up the current Java truststore file (cacerts) to a secure temporary location before making modifications.
Import the full LDAPS certificate chain—including Root CA, Intermediate CAs, and server certificates—into the Java truststore.
Verify the Java Runtime Environment version used by Tomcat and compare it against both the application's required Java version and the Java installation path whose truststore was updated.
Align the application server (e.g., Tomcat) Java configuration by pointing JAVA_HOME and JRE_HOME to the correct supported Java version where the certificate chain was imported.
Restart the application server and initiate an LDAPS connection or test authentication.

101c29b1-997d-482b-8bd5-eb658f0c7b09.title: EdgeAI and Co-Pilot User Provisioning and Onboarding
steps: Check the user account status in the identity provider and verify the requested access level (EdgeAI standard, EdgeAI Beta, or Co-Pilot).
Provision the user credentials for EdgeAI and assign the corresponding service license or feature entitlement in the administration portal.
Send the access credentials, login portal URL, and initial onboarding instructions to the user.
Validate that the user can authenticate and that no license assignment errors or registration blocks occur during first sign-in.
Escalate license assignment failures, pool exhaustion, or machine registration errors to the EdgeAI platform administration team.

6cd610b2-9a68-4f07-94c4-89fa0adbd13a.title: Client Inquiry: API Functionality for User Lifecycle Management
steps: Review the client inquiry to determine the exact user lifecycle requirements, target identity types (such as RPA User IDs), and the intended IDAM API integration scope.
Locate and provide the standard IDAM API documentation, endpoint specifications, authentication requirements, and lifecycle management workflows for RPA User IDs to the client.
Confirm with the client that the provided API specifications resolve their inquiry and provide all necessary information for their integration needs.

d68be2db-850e-4f6d-a1c9-985e654d10c5.title: Critical Software Vulnerability Identified
steps: Identify and inventory all target servers running the vulnerable software component.
Check for operational dependencies, bot automation health, and stakeholder approvals before initiating the maintenance window.
Back up application server configuration files, deployment directories, and custom environment variables.
Apply the software upgrade or security patch to the target component on the affected servers.
Restart the application service and verify application health checks, endpoint responsiveness, and version strings.

50a68b0d-a7b2-4c2d-9b04-c3d92f66bcc7.title: Unrecoverable Accidental Workflow Deletion
steps: Identify the exact name, process ID, workspace location, and approximate deletion timestamp of the missing workflow from the user.
Check whether local workflow export files (such as XML or package exports) or scheduled environment database backups exist from before the deletion timestamp.
Verify within Process Studio whether any native undo, version history, or recycle bin mechanism exists to restore the deleted workflow directly.
Notify the user that permanently deleted workflows cannot be recovered within Process Studio, provide guidance to restore from offline backups if found, and close the request.

f40991d3-5351-47aa-906b-f6647f63a3e0.title: Email Sent Without Intended Attachment
steps: Inspect the sent email in the sender's sent items folder to verify if the attachment was omitted prior to transmission.
Retrieve the correct file, attach it to a reply on the original email thread, and send the message to the recipient.
Check with the recipient to confirm that the attachment was received and can be opened cleanly.

52eeba5b-dcc1-4f92-b4c8-fcdf7e495caa.title: Policy-Driven Restricted Log Access
steps: Confirm whether the customer is restricted from sharing raw diagnostic log files externally due to company security or compliance policies.
Offer and schedule a supervised remote session (such as a Microsoft Teams call) with the customer to review logs interactively on their screen.
Join the remote session and guide the customer to open, filter, and display the relevant error traces and timestamps directly on their workstation.
Record the observed error codes, timestamps, and agreed follow-up actions in the support ticket.

967771fd-3b44-4d42-9d3a-cd86c24042dc.title: Third-Party Software Licensing Compliance Queries
steps: Identify the specific third-party utility requested (e.g., GPG, Gpg4win), its license type (e.g., GPLv3), and the mechanism of invocation (e.g., standalone command-line execution versus compiled library linking).

Provide a written compliance clarification explaining the component's license model, confirming that invoking an independent external binary does not create a derivative work or alter core product licensing.
Confirm with the customer compliance or SAM team that the provided explanation satisfies their assessment requirements.

1e328730-363d-41c7-b075-f5c739846635.title: Excel Input Plugin - Limited Multi-Header Validation
steps: Identify the expected list of column headers for the Excel input file and verify current pipeline failure behavior upon missing headers.

Implement custom validation logic prior to the Microsoft Excel Input step to inspect the header row, compare all required column names simultaneously, and aggregate any missing headers into a consolidated error report.
Review plugin release updates to determine if the upcoming Microsoft Excel Input plugin version with native multi-header validation is available, and upgrade when ready.

7f3d4a13-ed6b-44cd-b966-06c18fa80b6d.title: AutomationEdge Process Studio Project and Workspace Recovery
steps: Close Process Studio completely and create a backup copy of the entire workspace folder, the project directories, and the Process Studio installation directory to a safe location.

Check the Process Studio logs for specific errors regarding workspace settings, plugins, file corruption, or connection issues (such as '.pluginsconf file is tampered or corrupted', 'Error while creating .settings : Access is denied', 'Invalid process studio distribution', or tenant field mismatch).

If projects are not visible or workspace launch fails with workspace settings errors, inspect the workspace directory. Verify write permissions on the directory and update the .settings file to ensure active projects are properly listed.

If logs report that .pluginsconf is tampered or corrupted, navigate to the conf folder in the Process Studio directory. Take a backup of the .pluginsconf file and delete it. If the error persists upon reopening, backup the entire conf folder and delete the files inside conf before restarting Process Studio.

If Process Studio reports missing plugins when opening workflows (.psw), open Process Studio, go to Tools, click 'sync plugins', provide username and password in the AutomationEdge connection details window, and click Connect. If the issue persists, close Process Studio, delete the psplugins and .process-studio folders from the Process Studio directory, and start Process Studio by running process-studio.bat.

If pull operations fail due to local repository metadata corruption, re-clone the project repository into the workspace. If specific project files cause null pointer exceptions during opening, replace the corrupted project files with fresh copies from source control or production.

If Process Studio throws 'Invalid process studio distribution' or connection version mismatch errors, verify the AutomationEdge server version, download a matching process studio.zip package from the AE server, extract it cleanly to a different drive or clean directory, and start Process Studio.
Launch Process Studio by running process-studio.bat, open the target workspace, open the relevant .psw workflow files, and perform a test save and pull operation.

b56aa9db-a3c7-49a4-8005-f323b39ec298.title: Third-Party Library Critical Security Vulnerability Remediation
steps: Identify the vulnerable third-party library name, its current version in the environment, and the target patched release version of AutomationEdge (e.g., AE 8.0.2 or higher for Bootstrap 5.3.3, or Patch 8.2.4 V for Log4j 2.25.3+).
Plan and deploy the target AutomationEdge patch or upgrade version (such as AE 8.0.2 or designated patch release) across all affected application nodes.

Verify the AutomationEdge application version is at the target version or higher, and verify the third-party component version (e.g., open browser Developer Tools → Sources / Network to confirm Bootstrap version 5.3.3 or inspect underlying service library versions).

e01fbb36-818b-4162-9232-de999982bda0.title: Automated Download Failure Due to Browser Behavior Change
steps: Verify whether the browser update changed the default download behavior by running the automation script and observing if a 'Save As' dialog appears instead of initiating a direct file download.
Update the automation framework Java codebase to issue Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) commands configuring download behavior to allow automatic downloads and set the designated download path.
Execute the automation workflow against the target download task and verify that files save directly to the configured target directory without opening UI prompts.

b2b068f9-8b03-480f-836c-fcde668a1771.title: Bot Automation Failure Due to Complex UI Interaction Limitations
steps: Inspect the target UI element in the web application and test if programmatic event simulation (such as Ctrl-click or multi-selection) is supported by the frontend framework.
Check if an underlying API, backend service, or alternative batch-operation workflow is available to perform the target action without UI multi-selection.
If no programmatic workaround exists, document the inherent UI constraint in the ticket and close the issue as an unsupported UI automation pattern.

bcdd6834-d9ad-42a6-816a-3fb5888647c7.title: Resolving Automation Focus Loss After Browser Tab or Popup Closure
steps: Inspect the automation workflow steps preceding the window closure to check if any special keyboard keys (such as Shift, Ctrl, or Alt) were triggered with key-down events and not explicitly released.
Update the workflow to explicitly release any held special keys before attempting window-focus transitions.
Configure the 'Switch Window' plugin step immediately following the popup closure to explicitly select the original window by its title or handle.
Run the updated automation workflow end-to-end through the popup launch, closure, and subsequent interaction steps.
Escalate the issue to the internal engineering team for underlying plugin and browser driver investigation.

72256d7b-a2b5-439e-b992-ae1120b9918a.title: Agent Work Stoppage Due to ActiveMQ Queue Saturation or Misconfiguration
steps: Inspect the ActiveMQ administrative console to verify queue depth across active queues (such as SequentialWorkflowQueue) and check if memory usage has reached the broker limit while requests remain in 'NEW' state.
Stop the workflow schedulers that are generating high-frequency or long-running requests, and stop the associated agents assigned to those workflows to halt inbound traffic.
Purge the saturated queue (such as SequentialWorkflowQueue) in ActiveMQ to clear stuck messages, and update any corresponding stale request entries in the application database.

Update <ACTIVEMQ_HOME>/conf/activemq.xml under <destinationPolicy> to configure bounded queue limits and prevent future broker memory exhaustion. Set policyEntry for queues:
<policyEntry queue=">" producerFlowControl="true" memoryLimit="200mb" maxPageSize="2000"/>
Ensure that total per-queue allocations (memoryLimit multiplied by number of queues) do not exceed total broker memory capacity.
Restart the ActiveMQ service and the application services to apply the new broker configuration and reset internal connection pools.
Restart the workflow schedulers and agents. Submit a test workflow request and verify that the agent picks up the message, transitions the state from 'NEW' to processing, and dequeues successfully.

1f4d43da-5bdb-4931-b835-0bb5ae695e41.title: Manual TOTP Plugin Enablement Request
steps: Identify and validate the requested client ID, project name, and environment target to confirm authorization and current TOTP plugin status.
Assign and enable the Authenticator TOTP plugin for the validated client or project profile in the OnDemand administration interface.
Verify that the TOTP authentication option appears as available for users within the target client or project.

5dedc371-e21e-4534-b126-c3553e61ad22.title: SFTP Plugin Connection Failures to Legacy Servers
steps: Whitelist the target SFTP server URL or IP address and destination port in your firewall, proxy, and outbound network security rules.
Enable the legacy SSH algorithm compatibility option in the SFTP plugin configuration settings.
Initiate a test connection from the SFTP plugin to the destination SFTP server.

3bd6c9ee-d928-4a3d-b0af-a642b5142cba.title: Third-Party CAPTCHA Service Unreliability
steps: Inspect the active CAPTCHA solver error logs to confirm failure rates and latency with the Death by Captcha (DBC) service.
Update the CAPTCHA service integration configuration to use 2Captcha, providing the corresponding API credentials and endpoint settings.
Execute a test CAPTCHA resolution request through the updated 2Captcha integration.

f43723f4-f165-474e-9183-ce4e856e3152.title: Function Returns Null for Expected Output Despite Successful Operation
steps: Inspect the target destination or storage location to confirm that the operation physically created or processed the expected artifact.
Insert a 'Write to Log' step immediately following the action to explicitly print the output variables (such as file path, file name, or text results) into the execution log.
Execute the workflow and review the generated log output to verify that the internal values are exposed and accessible for downstream tasks.

4df138c0-0521-4862-97a4-de2960c4a2f9.title: Application Authorization Failure Due to Incorrect OAuth Scope/Refresh Token
steps: Inspect application error logs for authorization failure messages, token refresh errors, or connection resets during the authentication phase. Do not modify network proxy or firewall settings before validating the OAuth parameters.

Review the configured OAuth authorization URL, application registration permissions, and the explicit `scope` parameter values required for the target Microsoft API operations (e.g., Outlook 365 mail transmission).
Update the application configuration with the corrected OAuth `scope` parameters matching the necessary resource permissions.
Regenerate the OAuth refresh token using the updated scope parameters and reload or restart the application auth session.
Execute a test API call or trigger the bot workflow (e.g., send a test email via Outlook 365) to confirm successful token acquisition and resource access.

89fb4afc-7861-4fd6-8e6e-a43715bcc6a8.title: Insecure Tomcat Auto-Deployment Remediation
steps: Create a timestamped backup copy of the current server.xml file before making modifications.

Edit the server.xml file. In the <Host> section, set autoDeploy="false" and deployOnStartup="false". Within the same <Host> section, add the explicit context definitions:
<Context docBase="${catalina.home}/webapps/aeengine.war" path="/aeengine" />
<Context docBase="${catalina.home}/webapps/aeui.war" path="/aeui" />
Restart the Apache Tomcat service and verify that the /aeengine and /aeui endpoints are accessible and functional.

1de99393-abb4-4c27-8aba-17f63e9a510e.title: Security Vulnerability Remediation via Software Release
steps: Review the vulnerability report to identify the affected components, current installed versions, and the target release version required to patch the issue.
Create a full backup of application configuration, state, and relevant databases before applying any version upgrades or new software releases.
Deploy the target software release or upgraded component package into the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment.
Execute functional regression tests and run a security vulnerability scan in UAT to confirm the vulnerability is resolved and existing functionality remains intact.
Deliver the validated release package to the customer or production environment and apply the upgrade.

0548189e-436c-48e5-94d2-978df74f997f.title: Bypass Script Execution Restrictions in Automation Plugins via JavaScript Injection
steps: Inspect the failure logs of the unattended automation run to determine if the failure originates from a PowerShell-backed plugin (such as the Windows Mouse Action plugin) encountering execution restrictions or throwing NoSuchElementException.
Replace the restricted PowerShell-based plugin step with the Inject JavaScript plugin and supply a custom JavaScript script to interact directly with the target element in the browser context.
Run the updated automation flow in unattended mode and confirm that the Inject JavaScript step completes successfully without throwing NoSuchElementException.

9757829e-95d6-452f-a491-4fd65f6c09e3.title: Input Plugin Data Inconsistency and Performance Troubleshooting
steps: Inspect the input plugin configuration parameters and query strings to verify that all variables and filter values are correctly dynamically mapped rather than hardcoded.

Check the query sorting clause. If the query uses timestamp ordering combined with record ID (such as `ORDERBYsys_created_on^ORDERBYsys_id`), update the parameter to sort solely by unique record ID (`sys_id`) to avoid race conditions caused by record creation delays.
Check whether the external data source API supports bulk record extraction or if it is architecturally constrained to single-record transactions.

If performance degradation is caused by an upstream API limitation that only processes single records rather than batch operations, defer and escalate the issue to the application owner or API development team.

055189e1-6bd6-4d8f-8b7f-250ecb86f3e8.title: AutomationEdge OnDemand Access and Performance Issues Due to Configuration
steps: Check network connectivity to ondemand.automationedge.com from the client environment, verifying client proxy settings and checking if the client ISP is blocking traffic.
Instruct client IT or network administrator to correct local proxy settings and request their Internet Service Provider to unblock access to ondemand.automationedge.com.
Create a backup copy of server configuration files including server.xml and aeui/WEB-INF/web.xml before applying any modifications.
Inspect server.xml for URL and port configuration mismatches if the server console URL is unreachable or throwing access errors.
If encountering HTTP 403 Forbidden errors during SSO login, comment out the POST method configuration block in aeui/WEB-INF/web.xml and restart the server.
Check the running AutomationEdge version. If version is AE 8.2.0 and the server experiences abnormal memory utilization, upgrade the OnDemand instance to AE 8.2.1.
Inspect agent controller and scheduler configuration. Ensure 'Skip if Ongoing' is enabled where applicable to prevent agent queue congestion and verify agent connectivity.
Perform end-to-end verification by logging in via SSO, navigating console pages, and confirming workflow execution on assigned agents.
