85520a29-f1c6-4b23-9b62-fadf8eb5b5cc.title: Resolving SQL Date Format Mismatches in Automation Platforms
steps: Inspect the automation workflow run logs to capture the exact SQL query, runtime date parameter values, and specific database error message (e.g., ORA-01843).
Compare the date format passed by the automation platform variable with the date format expected by the target database query.

Update the SQL query or automation parameter transformation to use explicit date formatting (such as wrapping parameters with TO_DATE and an explicit format mask like 'YYYY-MM-DD') instead of relying on implicit string-to-date conversions.
Trigger a test execution of the automation workflow using the modified query or date parameter configuration.

4aba6364-5576-43f4-9e7a-7f7ddd2a03f0.title: Excel Plugin Protected File Handling and Engine Configuration
steps: Inspect the target file format (.xls, .xlsx, or .xlsb) and identify the specific protection mechanism applied (password-protected sheet/workbook vs read-only attribute).

For password-protected .xls or .xlsx files failing to read, open the Excel Input plugin step settings in Process Studio and set the spreadsheet engine type to 'Excel 2007 XLSX (Apache POI)'. Save the step configuration.

If handling a password-protected .xlsb file, check if the installed plugin version is 4.8 or later. If running on an earlier version, convert or save the source workbook as a password-protected .xlsx file before running the process.

If requiring read-only protection features on .xlsx files where the plugin only supports read-only for .xls files, convert the file workflow to use .xls format or remove the read-only flag constraint prior to plugin execution.
Execute the process workflow and verify that the Excel plugin reads or writes the target protected workbook without throwing engine or decryption exceptions.

425ed935-ab53-4327-8441-03a861403062.title: Recurring Information Request: API Authentication Limits
steps: Identify the specific API tier, endpoint, and authentication method mentioned in the user inquiry.
Lookup the defined rate limits, time window, and throttling headers (such as HTTP 429 Too Many Requests and Retry-After) for the user's tier.
Respond to the user with the requested rate limit specifications, threshold details, and links to official API documentation.

7500512f-c0bc-450c-b3be-e21a0677f599.title: Handling Client Requests for Unsupported Deployment Models
steps: Review the client's architecture request to identify requested services and verify whether the requested deployment model (such as on-premise hosting for cloud-native RAG services) is supported.
Notify the client that the requested feature requires cloud infrastructure (e.g., Azure) and that on-premise or custom alternative deployment models are not supported.
Close the support request or escalation with an unsupported deployment resolution code if the client cannot or will not provision the required cloud infrastructure.

71c0368d-661e-450a-8bc3-35134262e4c1.title: Evaluation Access Blocked by Company Device Issues
steps: Verify the company laptop issue and confirm that the hardware or software failure prevents participation in the scheduled evaluation.
Submit a request to the evaluation coordinator or relevant authority for temporary authorization to use a personal laptop.
Confirm that the user can authenticate and access the evaluation platform from the personal device.

f259ce8c-c368-4aa3-81fe-f6fa2ceca9d5.title: T3 User Login Failure Due to Password Issues
steps: Verify with the user that they are entering the correct password without typographical errors or outdated browser autofill values.
Reset the user's password for their T3 account.
Have the user attempt to log in to the T3 server or dashboard using the updated credentials.

b450364c-0a12-4647-969a-3ebd33f30d10.title: Workflow Failure Due to Unhandled Null/Empty Data
steps: Run the affected workflow in debug mode and inspect the step-by-step variable payloads to identify which step receives an unhandled blank or null value.
Inspect variable mappings and naming across the workflow steps, specifically verifying whether response bodies or plugin inputs (such as JSON Input plugins) share duplicate variable names.
If a duplicate variable name is causing values to be overwritten, assign a unique variable name to capture the response body and update downstream consumer steps to reference the new variable.

Add explicit null-check validation logic and conditional branches immediately following external API calls and parameter assignments to catch empty data before it enters loops or downstream processing.
Execute the modified workflow in debug mode with both empty and populated test payloads to verify that valid data flows correctly and null inputs trigger the configured validation branch.

9119fbe2-4c92-4dc5-a6f6-94fec2895fbb.title: Agent-Workflow Execution and State Troubleshooting
steps: Check if the agent is stuck in 'Updating' or failing on a specific agent after workflow assignment, and verify workflow assignment status.
Unassign the problematic or newly deployed workflow from the affected agent. If the agent is stuck in 'Updating', test and verify the workflow definition locally before re-assigning.

Check if the workflow uses a CredentialPool and inspect for requests stuck in RETRY status by checking the AutomationEdge UI for 'Status= Retry' or running the SQL query: Select * from vae_workflow_instance where Status='Retry'

Inspect Apache ActiveMQ queue size and broker memory. Check if messages are accumulating in SequentialWorkflowQueue or general queues due to long-running executions or mismatched thread configurations.

If workflow submission fails or requests remain stuck on the agent: stop the agent, restart the agent, unassign the assigned workflows, wait briefly, then re-assign the workflows to the agent and submit a test request.
Stop the workflow scheduler and stop the agent assigned to the workflow. Purge stuck requests from the ActiveMQ queue (such as SequentialWorkflowQueue or retry queues).
Restart the Apache ActiveMQ and application services (such as Apache Tomcat), update any stale database records if applicable, and resume the scheduler.
To prevent recurring memory saturation under high loads, open <ActiveMQ_Install_Dir>\bin\win64\wrapper.conf, set wrapper.java.maxmemory=2048, save the file, and restart the ActiveMQ service.
Submit a test workflow request and verify that the agent picks up the task from the queue and transitions the instance from NEW to IN_PROGRESS or COMPLETED.

2ae9f00a-fa6f-4c26-b1e4-7d76aee9daed.title: Stale Database Schema in Process Studio Due to Caching
steps: Check if the source database table has recent schema updates (such as renamed or added columns) that are visible in the plugin preview but missing during workflow execution.
Locate the Process Studio configuration and find the setting UseDBCache=Y. Modify the value to UseDBCache=N.
Restart Process Studio.
Open the workflow, open the Input Table plugin, and verify that the updated database column names are properly fetched and used across downstream steps.

ededcb86-62f2-4459-95b1-25f8899ada58.title: AutomationEdge Database Purging Failures
steps: Check available disk space on the drive hosting the AutomationEdge server and the PostgreSQL database.

Log in to the AutomationEdge UI as a System Administrator. Navigate to Settings > Purging > Purge Policy and Settings > Purging > Purge Schedule to verify that Purge Duration (in months) is configured for Audit Logs, Workflow Requests, and Notification History, and that the purge schedule is active.
Examine the database execution logs and Catalina logs during or after purge runs to identify the failure mechanism (e.g., constraint errors or unpurged records).

Evaluate the identified root cause from logs: if a foreign key constraint 'fk_nf_history_Wfinstance_Id' on 'ae_notification_history_old' is blocking deletion, proceed to upgrade. If records have Tenant_ID=NULL preventing deletion, proceed to manual query analysis. If disk exhaustion prevents AEUI login, perform manual database cleanup.
If purge fails due to foreign key constraint 'fk_nf_history_Wfinstance_Id' on 'ae_notification_history_old', upgrade AutomationEdge to version 8.1.4 or higher.
If audit logs fail to purge because records contain 'Tenant_ID=NULL', verify the record count in the audit log table and coordinate with the engineering team for targeted record cleanup.
If AEUI is inaccessible due to full disk space caused by accumulated audit logs, delete obsolete audit log data directly from the PostgreSQL database.
Trigger or wait for the next scheduled purge job, then check the record count in Audit Logs, Workflow Requests, and Notification History tables to confirm data reduction.

e096d427-044d-4ff0-818e-44076afd6f8a.title: Plugin Configuration Failure: SFTP Port Not Parsed
steps: Check the installed version of the File Transfer 2.0 Secure FTP plugin and verify whether the SFTP port fails to pass when entered in the Configuration tab of 'Put Files With SecureFTP'.
Hardcode the target SFTP port number directly within the step parameters or connection string instead of using the Configuration tab input field.
Run a test transfer using 'Put Files With SecureFTP' to confirm the connection establishes and transmits files using the hardcoded port.
Upgrade the File Transfer Secure FTP plugin to Release 4.8 or higher once available, and test moving the port parameter back into the standard Configuration tab.

fca533cd-0e7d-4d0f-8994-e69bb4d73d76.title: Linux Plugin SSH Connectivity Failure Due to Incompatible SSH Configuration
steps: Create a backup copy of the existing sshd_config file on the target Linux server before making any modifications.
Update the sshd_config file on the target Linux server to enable compatible algorithms, ciphers, MACs, or key exchange methods required by the Automation Edge Linux plugin.
Restart the SSH service on the target Linux server to apply the updated configuration.
Test the SSH connection from the Automation Edge Linux plugin to the target Linux server.

4aa9470f-6178-4b2e-9012-abc41f2a2f42.title: Process Studio Workflow Design and Execution Troubleshooting
steps: Inspect the workflow structure in Process Studio for invalid nesting patterns, specifically checking whether any 'Loop' step is placed inside a 'Try/Catch' block or uses unsupported step-level error handling.

Restructure the workflow to eliminate incompatible nesting: move the 'Loop' step outside of the 'Try/Catch' block, or wrap individual actions inside the loop with error handling rather than enclosing the entire loop.
Review the execution logs to determine if failures occur at specific UI interaction points due to element visibility or dynamic load delays.
Insert a 'Wait Until' step with explicit error handling immediately prior to the step targeting dynamic or slow-loading UI elements.
Check the runtime execution environment on the Agent for discrepancies with Process Studio, specifically verifying active RDP session state, plugin data conversion, and Unicode character handling.
Execute an end-to-end test run of the modified workflow directly on the target Agent environment to verify stability and successful completion.

11642b1d-7d0e-4e81-9822-591ac0b251cf.title: Custom User Role Permission Configuration Assistance
steps: Identify the target user account, target entity or organization, and the specific workflow permissions required for the custom user role.
Create the custom user role in the system access management settings if it does not already exist.
Assign the required feature permissions and workflow access to the custom user role, then attach the role to the designated user accounts.
Verify with the affected user that they can log in, access the target workflows, and perform actions permitted by the new role.

3634afe0-5628-4227-908c-b011336b9cdc.title: AE License Upload and Step Unit Verification
steps: Identify the target environment (Dev vs UAT) and calculate the step units required for the AE upgrade.
Determine if the current license file covers the calculated step units for the target environment.
Request and obtain an updated license file that includes the necessary step units for the specified environment.
Upload the license file to the designated AE server in the target environment.
Verify that the AE server recognizes the new license and reflects the expected step unit capacity.

47acd7b0-15bc-4af9-a876-ed57a8960fa0.title: Automation Edge License Provisioning/Update
steps: Check the workflow activation logs in AutomationEdge to determine if the failure is caused by insufficient step unit capacity.
Provision and apply an updated AutomationEdge license containing the required additional step units for the relevant environments (such as Development, UAT, and Production).
Activate the affected workflows in the target environment to verify that the new step unit capacity allows successful execution.
Contact the user or workflow owner to confirm that all required workflows are operating normally across environments.

0b43d798-44d4-44fb-a8be-ca9e83301858.title: User Reported Functionality Issue Due to Misaligned Expectations
steps: Inspect the user's input parameters, plugin synchronization, and local configuration files (e.g., verify form names, plugin settings, and context cache validity).
Determine whether the issue is caused by unsupported user expectations or an actual technical fault (such as an SSL handshake 'Connection reset' or plugin sync failure).
Conduct a live walkthrough or demonstration showing the correct configuration and supported workflows directly to the user.
Inspect client-side network connectivity and SSL handshake logs if connection resets or environmental failures persist during execution.
Confirm resolution with the user, log the clarified workflow in the ticket, and close the incident.

5216e09a-b6d2-46dc-b95c-e90524b18499.title: Incorrect Microsoft Graph API Endpoint for SharePoint Site Creation
steps: Inspect the application configuration files (such as web.xml or environment property files) to locate the configured Microsoft Graph API endpoint URL for SharePoint operations.
Verify whether the configured endpoint targets an invalid, deprecated, or malformed Microsoft Graph route for SharePoint site provisioning.
Update the API endpoint configuration in the configuration file (such as web.xml) to the correct Microsoft Graph API endpoint.
Deploy or reload the updated configuration and execute a test SharePoint site creation request.
If updating the endpoint requires application code changes or a formal deployment cycle, schedule and defer the fix to the next software release.

5674f1f1-fdda-4dd6-b848-1e7201dccc04.title: SMTP Mail Sending Failure Due to Authentication or Connectivity Issues
steps: Inspect the application mail logs to identify the exact rejection message from the SMTP server, specifically checking for 'Access denied, banned sending IP' or authentication rejection notices.
Test network connectivity from the application server to the SMTP server on port 25 (or the configured mail port) to determine if a network firewall is blocking outbound traffic.
Review the application mail protocol configuration (e.g., in AutomationEdge) and account credentials to verify the correct mail protocol, hostname, port, and authentication parameters are configured.
If the sending IP is flagged as banned ('Access denied, banned sending IP'), submit a delisting request to the mail provider or route outbound mail through an approved relay IP.
If port 25 is blocked by a firewall, update firewall rules to allow outbound TCP traffic to the designated SMTP server IP and port.
Trigger a test email dispatch from the application to verify end-to-end delivery.

29053c84-e444-4fb8-a3db-c3161281c176.title: Application Crash Due to System Memory Exhaustion (JVM Native Memory)
steps: Check operating system memory metrics, swap/page file usage, and system crash logs to verify that the JVM termination was caused by native system-level memory exhaustion rather than JVM heap exhaustion.
Inspect the failing workflow definition and isolate steps with high memory overhead, specifically Stream Lookup operations processing large datasets.

Reconfigure the pipeline transformations: in the SQL script plugin, enable "Execute for Each Row" and enable options to capture delete statistics to process records incrementally rather than buffering all rows in memory.
Deploy and execute the updated workflow in the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment with full-scale production dataset volumes.
Deploy the validated workflow and plugin configuration changes to the Production environment, then monitor OS memory and page file utilization during the next scheduled run.

782710b9-486f-43e1-99af-013fa3ce8639.title: Troubleshooting Incorrect Query Parameter Limiting Results
steps: Inspect the incoming or outgoing query string and request payload for parameters restricting result count, specifically checking for sysparam_limit=1 or similar pagination limits.
Update the query to adjust or remove the limiting parameter, setting sysparam_limit to the intended batch size or removing sysparam_limit=1.
Re-run the updated query and verify that the full expected dataset is returned to the consuming application.

851d2fd2-a338-4c9c-930c-805b4daaea29.title: AutomationEdge Process Studio Launch Failure Remediation
steps: Back up the current Process Studio installation directory, workspace folder, and the local .pluginconf directory before modifying files.
Inspect the Process Studio plugins directory for manually copied JAR files, duplicate libraries, or mismatched Log4j dependencies.
Remove the manually copied plugin and Log4j JAR files from the Process Studio plugins directory, then update and install plugins through the standard Process Studio update mechanism.
Attempt to start Process Studio to check if the application launches properly following plugin cleanup.
Deregister Process Studio and then re-register it to clear the corrupted .pluginconf folder and resynchronize plugins.
Create a new user, assign the required license, register Process Studio under the new user profile, sync all plugins, and switch to a fresh workspace directory.
Launch Process Studio and verify that all core functionalities, menu items, and workflow designer components open without crashing.

95fe54a7-6817-494b-a1e8-54513fe87d47.title: AutomationEdge Post-Upgrade Service Instability and Configuration Drift
steps: Check the AutomationEdge server startup logs for port conflicts on port 8081 and deployment errors such as IllegalStateException during aeengine.war initialization.
If port 8081 is in use by another application, reconfigure the AutomationEdge management server port property to an unassigned port and restart the service.
If aeengine.war deployment fails with an IllegalStateException due to a partial or corrupt version installation, re-deploy the clean full release package for the target version (such as 8.2.3).
Check the backend database for active locks or long-running transactions blocking plugin updates or engine operations.
Upload the compatible Process Studio and plugin packages (e.g., plugin version 4.2 or 4.6) matching the target platform version into the AutomationEdge console.
Inspect agent connectivity and TLS cipher configurations if AutomationEdge agents fail to reconnect after server restart or VAPT cipher changes.
Perform post-upgrade operational validation: access the server URL, verify SSL certificate status, test file upload limit configurations, and confirm agent workflow execution.

a15dd75c-f31b-4576-a37a-0ae800364569.title: Automation Edge Agent Insufficient Administrative Privileges
steps: Inspect the Access Control List (ACL) permissions on the Automation Edge Agent installation directory to check if the running user or service account has full control.
Grant full administrative access (read, write, execute, modify) on the Automation Edge Agent installation directory and all subdirectories to the service account or user running the agent.
Restart the Automation Edge Agent service and verify that it initializes cleanly without access denied errors.

843f532d-e0a7-4129-87e9-0976ca324626.title: Intermittent Application Failures Due to Concurrency-Related Product Bugs
steps: Inspect automationedge.log on the server machine for the exact date and time the scheduled event failed. Check whether schedule execution was attempted, whether any errors or thread exhaustion occurred, or if schedule modification entries were logged.

Access the AEUI directly from or referencing the server machine, and compare the configured schedule time against the Tomcat server timezone and client machine timezone to rule out timezone discrepancies.
Check current thread utilization and database connection pool states to determine if simultaneous job triggers exceed thread capacity or if worker threads have entered a conflicting state.
If internal worker threads are locked or jobs are failing silently due to connection conflicts, restart the AutomationEdge server services to clear the conflicting state and restore processing.

Apply interim workaround: adjust concurrency or schedule distribution to avoid simultaneous thread exhaustion, or deploy the hotfix JAR provided by engineering for specific plugin defects (such as Surface Action Plugin).
Trigger test schedules and monitor message processing across concurrent workflows to verify tasks fire on time and process data correctly.

Review the installed AutomationEdge version and schedule an upgrade to the permanent fix release (such as AE version 8.1.0 or targeted maintenance release 8.2.5+), or escalate to product engineering for a permanent defect patch.

e7f0082d-8e69-450e-a70f-3b3b9f7b6730.title: Handling Native MFA Requests via SSO Alternative
steps: Review the customer's access requirements and determine if their organization utilizes an external Identity Provider that supports Single Sign-On (SSO).
Explain to the customer that native direct MFA is not supported on the platform and propose configuring Single Sign-On (SSO) so MFA can be enforced upstream via their Identity Provider.

Evaluate customer response: if the customer accepts SSO, initiate standard SSO configuration; if the customer strictly requires direct native platform MFA, submit an enhancement request to Product Management.
Confirm customer acknowledgement and verify whether the ticket can be resolved or closed following the SSO proposal.

65023bb3-f0da-422a-aaec-01d5e337fb61.title: Agent Enters Unknown State Causing Delivery Failures
steps: Inspect agent status metrics and export delivery error logs to determine the exact timestamp and initial error signature of the transition into the unknown state.
Request configuration comparison details and recent environment change history from the customer.
Verify whether the customer provided the requested configuration comparison details within the agreed support window.
Analyze the configuration differences between working and failing environments, revert any unsupported settings, and restart the agent service.

172c2979-7ae2-48fd-90ab-609a4c0c4bb5.title: Python Script ModuleNotFoundError Due to Missing or Outdated Dependency
steps: Inspect the failure logs of the failing task to identify the specific module name reported in the ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
Install or upgrade the required Python library in the environment where the script runs.
Rerun the affected Python workflow to verify that the script imports the library and completes execution without ModuleNotFoundError.
Update agent machine setup scripts, Docker images, or requirements documentation to ensure all execution hosts have the updated dependency installed.

df6b09d8-fabe-4a32-8850-2b4f1040c190.title: AutomationEdge Log Level Configuration Inquiry
steps: Inspect the AutomationEdge application configuration to determine the active log level and the location of the logging configuration file.
Reply to the client with the verified log level setting and the configuration file path, confirming whether any modifications are necessary.

6bd9f576-a88a-47ef-accc-25b998dd75ae.title: RPA Workflow Failures During Excel File Operations
steps: Verify that the target file path exists, is correctly formatted for the executing agent operating system, and check if the file format is a password-protected .xls or .xlsm file.
Check whether the Excel file is actively open, locked by another process, or being accessed concurrently by another scheduled workflow instance.
Terminate any orphaned background Excel processes on the agent host and configure the system environment to disable blocking Excel pop-ups and dialogs.

Modify the workflow design to enforce sequential execution with blocking steps for shared table access, replace fixed delay timers with dynamic condition-based waits, and add a brief delay before executing file deletion plugins.

If intermittent Java NullPointerExceptions, memory exhaustion, or password-protected format bugs persist, re-register a new AutomationEdge Agent, adjust agent memory limits, or upgrade to patch release AE 8.2.4 V.

11e0c9e9-3ea0-47bd-94f7-6af4f062b2c4.title: Customer Feature Request Denied Due to Architectural or Security Constraints
steps: Evaluate the customer request against platform boundaries to identify if it introduces cross-tenant data leakage, violates data privacy regulations, or causes unacceptable processing overhead.
Check existing platform safeguards to determine whether existing security measures (such as secured database storage) already mitigate the customer's underlying concern.
Draft a formal technical response detailing why the request cannot be implemented, explaining the architectural or performance constraints, and highlighting any existing compensating controls.

Deliver the response to the customer. If the customer accepts the existing controls or denial, close the ticket. If the request represents an unmet product capability that warrants roadmap evaluation, route the request to Product Management for future planning.

7f564b39-fca6-4b03-88c7-6d76680d4ce2.title: Post-Deployment Connectivity Failure Due to New Build
steps: Run the previous stable build or a standalone test workflow against the same target environment to verify baseline network connectivity.
Trace the new build or workflow execution step by step to identify the exact step throwing SocketTimeoutException: Connect timed out.
Roll back the active deployment to the previous known-good build version if the issue is impacting production operations.
Provide the failing step details, timeout stack traces, and differential configuration to the build owner or customer to address code-level dependency or timeout settings.

228eb751-b342-4101-b842-b563decfb78b.title: Application Compatibility Issues with Platform Updates
steps: Create a backup copy of current JVM configuration files, environment variable definitions, and startup scripts prior to making changes.
Review application JVM launch arguments and configuration files for deprecated experimental options affecting browser integration and automation.
Remove or update the deprecated experimental JVM options in the configuration and restart the application service.
Execute a test run of Chrome browser automation tasks to verify that rendering and feature interactions operate normally.
If Internet Explorer or Robot handling issues persist, check host operating system compatibility (such as Windows Server 2022) and document affected robot tasks for vendor or platform escalation.

e5ba8eea-1372-463d-b1cb-6ad78191d151.title: Copilot Access Provisioning and Plugin Assignment
steps: Identify the user role, target environment, and whether the issue is a missing Copilot plugin or a request for agent assignment in the T3 instance.
If the request is for agent visibility/assignment in the T3 instance, notify the user that by architectural limitation, agents are not assigned to Copilot users in the T3 instance.
For users lacking standard Copilot capabilities (such as ITPA candidates), assign the required Copilot plugins to the user account.
Have the user restart their Copilot session and confirm that the assigned plugins are accessible and functioning as expected.

25cd7a1e-2085-4d2e-910a-ae3b33512c66.title: UAT Application Deployment Failure Due to web.xml Parsing Error
steps: Inspect the UAT deployment and server logs for XML parser errors, specifically looking for SAXParseException pointing to invalid tags or structure (such as misplaced content where 'init-param' is expected) in web.xml.
Create a backup copy of the current web.xml configuration file before applying any modifications.
Edit web.xml to correct the malformed XML elements, ensuring tags such as init-param and servlet configurations strictly comply with standard XML deployment descriptor schema rules.
Repackage the application archive (e.g., aeui.war) if necessary and redeploy the application to the UAT server.
Perform functional verification by attempting to log in to the UAT web interface and executing a workflow update.

62a963f4-9dcf-48c6-89b0-96c89f5ae9ca.title: SFTP Automation User Permission Policy Conflict
steps: Inspect the automation job configuration and SFTP server logs to identify the user account, target directory path, and specific permission error.
Check with the system administration team or review the server security policy to confirm whether root-level directory creation is strictly restricted for automated service accounts.

Provide an approved sub-directory path for automation uploads, update the automation workflow to use the designated subfolder instead of the root folder, or submit an exception request to the system team.

423b2cd4-6ae1-4b61-8cb1-c8f3a49165ab.title: Agent Resource Contention Due to Overlapping Workflow Execution
steps: Inspect the process table on the agent host to identify lingering OpenJDK processes and measure current CPU and memory utilization.
Terminate all orphaned and lingering OpenJDK processes associated with completed or stuck workflow runs prior to starting new tasks.
Restart the AutomationEdge Agent service or the host server if CPU utilization remains saturated or the agent remains unresponsive.
Verify that host CPU utilization returns to normal baseline levels and that the agent successfully picks up pending workload without spawning duplicate runaway processes.
Adjust workflow schedule configurations to stagger resource-intensive workflows and shift heavy workloads to non-peak hours.

4638b6f2-dc18-47b8-8b0d-14cac4329551.title: O365 Email Message Input Plugin Connectivity and Shared Mailbox Troubleshooting
steps: Verify whether the workflow is using the modern Office 365: Email Message Input plugin (built on Microsoft Graph APIs with OAuth2) or the legacy OOTB Email Message Input plugin (which relies on basic authentication with POP3/IMAP).
Check if correct proxy details are configured for the client server / Process-studio environment and verify network firewall whitelisting for Microsoft Graph endpoints.
Perform a test connection in Process Studio to capture the exact error message and error code.

If a Microsoft API error for client secret occurs or application type is Web, inspect the Azure Active Directory app registration. Configure the application type as Public Client/native (mobile & desktop) in Azure AD and regenerate the Refresh token.

For shared mailbox access issues, verify and grant required delegated permissions on the Azure AD app registration and ensure the service account has mailbox delegation permissions in Microsoft 365 / Exchange.

Validate if the issue is caused by known plugin limitations: (1) Graph API filter cap limiting results to ~250 emails per request, or (2) shared mailbox folder visibility issues. If folder visibility is obstructed, apply the ARC plugin workaround until the plugin is updated.

1c443ad1-3e5f-4a2a-b28d-7f5ea938c58c.title: Process Studio SSO Port Binding and Callback Configuration
steps: Inspect the Process Studio authentication logs to verify if the local SSO callback server started on port 2611 and check for HTTP 400 status or port binding errors.
Verify that no existing Process Studio processes or other local services are actively holding port 2611, and ensure local firewall/proxy settings do not block localhost on port 2611.

Log in to the Azure Portal, navigate to Azure Active Directory > App Registrations, open the target application, go to Authentication, and under Redirect URIs / Reply URLs add http://localhost:2611/ then save the configuration.
Clear the browser cache and session cookies, restart Process Studio, and attempt the SSO login again.

If port binding fails during concurrent logins across multiple instances, avoid simultaneous login attempts on the same host and track the known defect awaiting the permanent multi-port range release.

22e65e2a-6647-4792-8744-8dd8d12b3b2b.title: Troubleshooting RDP Session Initialization Failures and VBScript Timing Issues
steps: Inspect the initial RDP connection for any active modal popups, security prompts, or dialog boxes that block the session from completing initialization.
Create a backup copy of the target VBScript plugin file prior to modifying its execution timing logic.
Insert a delay (sleep interval) in the VBScript plugin immediately before the call that accesses or hooks into the RDP session.
Execute the automated workflow end-to-end to verify that the RDP session is consistently found and initialized without timing out.

c5ea5304-36aa-4088-8060-2c6ed69ebf8f.title: Metering Unit Utility Operational Issues During License Upgrade Preparation
steps: Verify that the Metering Unit Utility package can be downloaded and accessed. Check download URL validity and file system permissions.
Check if Java is installed and properly configured in the system PATH environment variable.
Append 'encrypt=false;trustServerCertificate=false' to the database connection string in the utility configuration if database connection errors occur.
Execute the Metering Unit Utility to extract usage metrics and generate the XLSX report.
Inspect the generated XLSX file to ensure data completeness and proceed with applying the license upgrade.

a893f93e-7256-48c9-a00c-a0efe4409f1f.title: UAT Server Browser Access and Service Instability Remediation
steps: Inspect the Apache Tomcat logs (`catalina.out` or standard error logs) for ClassNotFoundException errors, missing JAR file exceptions, or unexpected shutdown sequences.
Deploy the missing JAR file into the Tomcat library directory and restart the Tomcat service.
Import and configure the required UAT environment SSL/TLS certificate into the server's certificate store and browser truststore.
Contact the IT/Network administration team to request an exemption or policy update for network-level restrictions that block Google Chrome execution and generate unexpected credential prompts.
Launch Google Chrome on the UAT server and navigate to the local UAT application URL.

c5dec922-3b1d-4f0f-919c-e53e66371872.title: Stalled Administrative Approval Due to Personnel Unavailability
steps: Inspect the pending request ticket to identify the target item (e.g., course enrollment), the submission timestamp, and the designated approver.
Check the designated approver's out-of-office status and review the organizational directory or workflow system for a designated backup approver.
Reassign or route the approval request to the identified backup approver, functional team lead, or administrative manager for manual sign-off.
Verify that the backup approver has granted approval and confirm that the enrollment or access provisioning has completed successfully.

d775a1ad-da55-4942-a15e-42aef6d8ccc0.title: Heap Memory Exhaustion during Large Data Processing with Excel Writer
steps: Inspect the agent process logs for the failed bot execution and verify that the failure is caused by an OutOfMemoryError (OOM) / Java heap space exhaustion during Excel Writer execution.
Increase the maximum heap memory allocation configured for the bot agent or runner runtime to accommodate large volume processing with the Excel Writer plugin.
Rerun the affected bot workflow with the large dataset and verify that the Excel Writer operation completes successfully without memory exhaustion errors.

bac7e296-5ccb-4e52-a005-c67e8bd152c6.title: GUI Spy Functionality Issues Due to System Resource Constraints
steps: Inspect the RPA development machine's task manager or resource monitor to check current RAM usage and available hard disk drive (HDD) storage.
Provide the client or infrastructure team with recommendations to increase RAM and HDD storage, and apply the updated custom GUI-Automation JAR file to the Process Studio installation directory.
Relaunch Process Studio, open GUI Spy, and test element identification and hotkey responsiveness on the target application.

eb8daa73-9e5d-4045-aff5-1c9d2c1cf8b6.title: RPA Tooling Compatibility Management (Chrome Driver & AutomationEdge Extension)
steps: Check the installed browser version (Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge) and confirm the requested version of the browser driver and AutomationEdge extension.
Back up the existing browser driver executables and AutomationEdge extension files from the local RPA runtime or installation directory to a backup folder.
Download or locate the matching driver executable (ChromeDriver or EdgeDriver) and AutomationEdge extension package, and replace the files in the designated RPA tooling directory.
Launch a test RPA process or initiate browser automation to verify that the browser opens and the AutomationEdge extension communicates properly without version errors.

e8f124eb-8f7a-459c-a2d1-18460f312786.title: Product Feature Gap Requiring Custom Development
steps: Compare the customer's functional requirement against native product capabilities to determine whether the requested capability is supported out-of-the-box.
Reclassify the ticket from an operational incident or product defect to a custom development request.
Notify the customer that the requested feature requires custom development, provide options for custom solution engagement, and request customer confirmation to close the support ticket.

163b1392-a5b4-49d4-8b95-ce7cf36f9b10.title: Process Incompatibility After Library Upgrade
steps: Check the installed component versions across your development (Process Studio) and deployment environments to verify version parity and identify recent upgrades.
Check if the failure is due to a GUI Plugin version mismatch between Process Studio (v4.7) and a target environment running a version earlier than 4.7.
Align the GUI Plugin version across Process Studio and the deployment environment so that both use the same or a compatible version (version 4.7 or later).
Inspect the failing workflow logic for steps incompatible with the updated JAR (specifically checking for failures at the 'Get Variable' step resulting in empty values or blank output files).
Modify the workflow to pass values via parameters instead of using the failing 'Get Variable' step.
Execute and validate the modified process in the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment to confirm outputs (such as Excel files) are populated properly.
Deploy the validated workflow to the Production environment and perform post-deployment verification.

f8fdbafa-ed05-4cf0-bbcb-49f860c271bf.title: SOAP API Integration and Execution Failure in AutomationEdge Studio
steps: Compare the SOAP endpoint URL, headers (such as Content-Type and SOAPAction), and XML request body against a known working request in Postman.

Add a 'Generate Rows' step before the API call to declare request parameters separately (base URL, fields, query parameters 'q', and authorization token) instead of passing a single concatenated URL string.
In the Advanced REST Client plugin step, map the separated parameters to their respective URL and query fields, configure required headers, and attach the SOAP XML body.
Execute the workflow in AutomationEdge Studio and inspect the step output to ensure the request succeeds without 'Illegal character in path' errors.

7833f9d3-10eb-446c-94c9-85c971b70c7a.title: UI Component Absence Due to Dependency-Related Bug
steps: Check the AEUI Document Metadata interface to confirm the dropdown control is missing, and inspect the current AutomationEdge installed version.
Create a full backup of the AutomationEdge configuration, database, and application state before applying any upgrade.
Upgrade the AutomationEdge platform to version 8.4.0 or apply the corresponding release patch.
Log into the AEUI, navigate to Document Metadata, and verify that the dropdown control renders and functions as expected.
Collect browser developer console logs, AEUI service logs, and version details, then escalate the ticket to the AutomationEdge engineering team.

e9457596-2af3-45ff-a734-1d93044f24e6.title: Misunderstood Rate Limiting for Bulk Operations
steps: Examine the rate limiter configuration to identify whether rate limiting policies evaluate per HTTP request or per individual item within a bulk payload.
Analyze the client workflow logs and downstream event processing (such as batch notification dispatches) to determine how individual items in the payload trigger actions.
Provide rate limiting behavior clarification to the client team and recommend client workflow adjustments, such as client-side batch throttling or payload chunking.
Run a test bulk operation with the updated client workflow or configuration adjustments to verify that downstream services are not overwhelmed.

d21da030-3fb6-45a7-8725-e9f09519c516.title: Bot Operational and Integration Troubleshooting
steps: Query the bot API to retrieve the request ID, current execution status, and error logs for the affected run.
Check the host process list for duplicate bot processes and inspect the configured environment variables and Java path.
Reconfigure the system environment variables and set the correct Java path to prevent duplicate parallel execution, then terminate any orphaned bot processes.
Verify proxy configurations and network reachability to external endpoints (such as CDSL proxy endpoints or target APIs).
Validate bot JAR file dependencies and ensure all required library versions match the current API specification.
Retrigger the bot request via the API using the original request parameters.
Escalate unresolved bot failures to engineering with the request ID, Java environment details, proxy status, and full execution logs.

96774f2e-e37b-46cb-a264-3cc0cc608c2c.title: Third-Party API Integration: Data Mapping and Authentication Troubleshooting
steps: Check the integration plugin authentication settings, API permission scopes, and OAuth token refresh configuration.
Inspect the data mapping configuration in the plugin, verifying static value definitions, XPath selectors, and key field mappings including 'category' and 'Email id'.
Send a single test record through the integration plugin and review the raw HTTP request and response payloads.
Update misconfigured field mappings in the plugin schema and refresh expired credentials or access tokens in the connection profile.
Collect integration logs, failing payload samples, error codes, and token lifecycle details, then escalate the issue to the integration plugin vendor for assistance.

7e6d3b7d-d06a-48cc-b8e6-5c06cd949bf5.title: Misrouted Feature Request and Complex Requirement Triage
steps: Review the support ticket description and requirements to verify whether the request describes broken existing functionality or an unbuilt business requirement, such as dynamic calculation rules or custom business logic.

Evaluate the triage determination: if the ticket is a standard break/fix issue, route it to standard engineering support; if it is a complex requirement or feature enhancement, proceed to ticket conversion and re-routing.

Do not close the ticket as 'not a product issue'. Reassign or link the ticket to the Product Management or Solution Architecture intake backlog, preserving all technical context and business justification.
Send a customer update stating that the request has been transferred to the product development pipeline for roadmap review rather than handled as a break/fix defect.

afdcf8d0-1ff7-422a-9fba-077e247c8359.title: Unattended UI Automation Blocked by OS-Level Authentication Pop-up
steps: Check the display resolution and DPI scaling settings on the unattended automation runner machine.
Set the runner machine display resolution to a standard fixed mode (such as 1920x1080 at 100% DPI scaling) and apply the changes across unattended sessions.
Re-run the automation workflow in test mode and verify that the UI element inspector can highlight and send credentials to the OS authentication pop-up.

If UI inspectors still cannot target the native prompt, escalate to IT or application owners to configure Integrated Windows Authentication (IWA), auto-login policies, or switch from web selectors to native OS UI automation libraries.

a45a6b02-fdf7-448c-a37f-ea05d150a6ef.title: Application Request ID Processing Failure
steps: Query application error logs using the failed request ID to identify the exception stack trace or configuration mismatch across High Availability (HA) nodes.
Apply the required configuration correction or deploy the approved software patch to resolve the request processing defect across all cluster nodes.
Send a synthetic test transaction through the application endpoint and verify that a new request ID is generated and processed successfully.

835ae433-9a46-42e0-96aa-b4aee15cf66a.title: Plugin Operational Issues: Driver and Configuration-Related Failures
steps: Review plugin logs and configuration to identify whether the failure is caused by missing, incorrect, or improperly placed driver dependencies.
Upload the required driver files to the designated plugin driver directory.
Apply the 'Inject JavaScript plugin' script to restore plugin operations when driver resolution is unavailable or pending driver management correction.
Execute a test transaction through the plugin to verify that normal operational workflows succeed.

1dc56a30-901f-4ffe-bcdf-02518845e98d.title: Remediating Agent Operational Issues Caused by Missing or Misconfigured Dependencies
steps: Check the agent startup and execution logs for Java exceptions, missing driver classes (such as missing sqljdbc or logging libraries), and database connection failure messages.
If logs indicate logging framework errors during initialization, inspect and repair the Log4j configuration file in the agent configuration directory.

If database connection errors indicate missing or incompatible drivers, place the correct JDBC driver JAR file (e.g., sqljdbc JAR for Microsoft SQL Server, or compatible driver JAR for Vertica/PostgreSQL) into the agent's driver library directory.

Update the database connection string and connection settings in the agent plugin configuration based on the target database type:
- For Vertica databases, select the 'Vertica5+' connection type.
- For PostgreSQL databases not configured for SSL, append sslmode=disable to the JDBC connection string.
- For Microsoft SQL Server, configure explicit connection string parameters and timeout settings as required.
Restart the agent service and verify that the agent initializes without Java exceptions and successfully establishes connections to all configured databases.

23eb43c7-0fe0-4bac-8892-92ad19c05034.title: GenAI Plugin Authentication Failure Due to Time Synchronization
steps: Check the current host system time and verify clock drift against a reliable Network Time Protocol (NTP) server or standard time reference.
Correct the server time by synchronizing the host clock with the designated NTP service.
Execute the GenAI Plugin workflow that previously failed to verify successful authentication against Google Vertex AI.

f87a3589-b104-4ab6-872c-87c138d6d5c2.title: AutomationEdge-ServiceNow Integration Configuration & Authentication Troubleshooting
steps: Inspect the AutomationEdge integration logs (e.g., IntgServiceHandler, IntegrationJob) to identify the specific failure signature: missing parameters, OAuth token failure, invalid organization code, or abort plugin termination.
Verify and update the integration parameters (URL, Username, Password, and Organization Code) in the AutomationEdge Integration Component and ServiceNow server configuration.
For OAuth authentication, configure the redirect URL in ServiceNow OAuth settings, assign required user permissions, and generate a new refresh token for the ServiceNow Input plugin.

Open the AutomationEdge workflow and check if an 'Abort plugin' is configured to 'Abort and log as error'. If present, replace it with a 'Set Workflow Result plugin' to prevent single-record errors from stopping the entire batch.
Trigger a manual integration run or poll cycle in AutomationEdge to verify data fetching from ServiceNow.

c770bdee-6086-485a-9394-9ad0d449229f.title: RPA Development Machine Performance Degradation Due to Insufficient Hardware
steps: Inspect the development machine's hardware specifications to confirm available RAM, current memory utilization, and whether the system drive is an HDD or SSD.
Deploy the custom GUI-Automation JAR file to the Process Studio library directory to optimize GUI component performance.
Provide hardware upgrade recommendations to the client or infrastructure team, specifying an upgrade to at least 16GB RAM and migration from HDD to SSD.
Relaunch Process Studio and test GUI Spy against target applications to verify responsiveness and stability.

f449f80b-23ed-4357-9da0-fab6f6f06532.title: Handling Intermittent and Unreproducible Support Issues
steps: Schedule and conduct a live diagnostic session with the reporting user to observe the issue directly in their environment under identical user conditions.
Assess whether the reported issue reproduced during the diagnostic session or if real-time system logs indicate intermittent failures.
Request explicit confirmation from the client on whether the issue is currently resolved or still impacting their operations.
Document all reproduction attempts, session findings, and explicit client closure agreements in the ticket notes before closing the ticket.

98d8de2a-60ca-466f-b488-fb302f2d25b9.title: Handling User Knowledge Gap for System Operations
steps: Identify the exact operation the user wants to perform and confirm that the system feature is functioning normally without service errors or permission blocks.
Provide the user with step-by-step instructions or conduct a live demonstration showing how to perform the specific operation.
Ask the user to execute the operation independently and verify that the target task completes successfully.

3a5e2fde-c783-4c49-b1f5-641a4abaf2ba.title: Post-Upgrade API Incompatibility Due to Request Structure Change
steps: Inspect the failed API request logs from the client to identify differences between the legacy request format and the upgraded version's API specification, checking for parameters moved from the request body to the URL path or query parameters.

Update the calling client or workflow integration to use the new API request structure, passing required identifiers (such as scheduler ID) directly in the endpoint URL rather than passing legacy attributes (such as scheduler name) in the request body.
Execute a test API call using the updated request format and verify the HTTP response code and workflow invocation.

9edf2b36-6200-4bf8-8c7b-88e949a6cffa.title: Process Studio Plugin Sync and On-Demand Loading Failure Troubleshooting
steps: Inspect the client proxy configuration and outbound network logs for HTTP 403 Forbidden responses during Process Studio plugin sync and on-demand page requests.
Verify enterprise browser policy settings to confirm that required extensions (such as AutomationEdge extension) are permitted and can execute without policy blocks.
Update the client-side proxy configuration and allowlist rules to permit traffic to the required Process Studio plugin synchronization and on-demand page endpoints.
Relaunch Process Studio, trigger plugin synchronization, and open the on-demand page to verify operational status.

f504074d-5826-4ba2-b04a-1dbb18b7ec83.title: AutomationEdge and DocEdge Upgrade and Migration Playbook
steps: Review the target AutomationEdge and DocEdge release notes, component dependencies (e.g., Angular version, security CVE fixes), and decommissioning requirements for existing instances.
Verify that a valid license is available for the target server environment (e.g., Development/UAT license) prior to migration or decommissioning of old servers.
Take a complete backup of the existing application installation directory, database, and configuration files on the target server.
Execute the upgrade installer or migration procedure on the UAT server to deploy the target AutomationEdge and DocEdge packages.
Inspect the web application deployment descriptor (web.xml) for schema validity, ensuring configuration tags such as async-supported are valid and correctly positioned.
Start the AutomationEdge and DocEdge services, apply the updated license, and run smoke tests to verify web portal access, user authentication, and workflow execution.

46845a57-78ca-40c4-b966-30b543c72cd0.title: Network Access Denied to Database from Application Agent
steps: Verify network layer reachability and test whether the database port (such as Oracle port 1521) is open and accessible from the agent host machine.

Contact the IT network security team to allow outbound and inbound traffic between the application agent IP address and the database server on the required database port across firewalls and network security groups.
Re-test network port reachability and trigger a test database connection or workflow from the application agent.

01c73268-1ce1-4a42-a137-f19f861432e8.title: Manual Trial License Provisioning
steps: Validate the incoming trial request by confirming the customer entity, target product, evaluation duration, and recipient contact information.
Generate and issue the trial license with the requested product modules and expiration date.
Upload the generated trial license to the customer environment or dispatch it to the designated customer contact.
Confirm that the trial license applies cleanly and notify the customer of the active trial period.

6cd1f366-2ab2-4bb9-9ad8-6eafbe87a29f.title: Routine Plugin Assignment Fulfillment
steps: Review the request ticket to identify the target user or system and the specific list of requested plugins.
Assign the requested plugins to the target user or system.
Verify that the assigned plugins are active and accessible to the user or system.

ec98a4a5-1441-4322-90c8-b6a0581048fc.title: Client Inquiry: Excel Mapping Feasibility
steps: Review the client's source Excel layout and target schema to determine mapping feasibility and identify required transformation rules.
Create and deliver a working sample mapping configuration or logic demonstration to the client.
Confirm with the client that the provided sample logic runs as expected against their test dataset.

03fb9cef-cee8-4238-b19d-cde8e1c2c470.title: Email Agent Certificate Loading Failure on Startup
steps: Restart the email agent service to force re-initialization and certificate acquisition.
Verify whether the email agent is successfully connecting and reading email messages.
Check the active Java installation by opening a command prompt and running: java -version

Open a command prompt as an administrator and import the required SSL certificate into the Java truststore using: keytool -import -trustcacerts -file "D:\Exchange_Certificate\Exchange_UAT.cer" -alias exchange_certificate -keystore "D:\Java\OpenJDK11U-jdk_x64_windows_hotspot_11.0.11_9\lib\security\cacerts"
Restart the email agent service after the truststore import.

4a10921a-bb54-4345-b934-12d727f5ea27.title: ServiceNow AutomationEdge Plugin Rollback from 4.7 to 4.2
steps: Review active workflows to identify any that were created or modified using plugin version 4.7, and verify corresponding version compatibility across Process Studio and the target environment.
Downgrade the AutomationEdge plugin from version 4.7 to version 4.2 in the production environment.
Trigger and monitor affected workflows on plugin version 4.2 to confirm successful execution.

bb35d404-8e13-4b4c-aca7-0c699a68ddee.title: Automation Plugin UI Element Interaction Failure
steps: Inspect the failing automation task definition and verify whether the Robot Handling plugin is configured to interact with a native OS UI element, such as the File Explorer address bar.
Update the automation script configuration to replace the Robot Handling plugin with the Windows plugin for the target UI interaction step.
Run a test execution of the automation script to confirm that the file path entry or UI interaction succeeds.

e95a03e2-f138-427b-93df-9cb5db3f13e6.title: Compliance/Security Document Request Fulfillment
steps: Identify the requested document type (SOC, SBOM, VAPT), the target software/system version (e.g., 8.x), and the required level of detail.
Check if the requested artifact for the target release exists in the standard compliance repository.
Engage the internal cloud or platform engineering team (e.g., Google Cloud Platform team) to obtain detailed reports or missing assessment information.
Deliver the verified compliance or security document to the requester via approved secure channels and close the ticket.

f7a62a52-de28-420a-828a-61ed941d7968.title: Handling User Requests for Custom Scripting Assistance
steps: Review the user's data structure and determine whether their extraction requirement relies on a static format or requires complex dynamic handling.
Provide a working code example (such as JavaScript) demonstrating static extraction for the sample structure, and document the boundaries showing the user how to extend it for dynamic requirements.
Confirm that the sample snippet executes against the provided static sample data without errors.

2a6952eb-e089-4113-ab36-e255ed415b69.title: Product Defect and Queue Saturation Causing Workflow Unassignment
steps: Inspect the ActiveMQ broker queue depth, memory consumption, and agent polling status to determine if messages are saturated in the queue without being delivered.
Purge stuck messages from the saturated ActiveMQ queue and update any stale database records associated with the pending workflow requests.
Restart the ActiveMQ service and associated application services.
Open <ActiveMQ_Install_Dir>\bin\win64\wrapper.conf, set wrapper.java.maxmemory=2048, and restart the ActiveMQ service.
If workflow unassignment persists despite message broker recovery, escalate the issue to the Engineering team for defect remediation or plan deployment of release 8.4.0 containing the code fix.

20d96fcb-c521-4e21-9405-5853793eb6ff.title: Web Automation File Download Interruption Troubleshooting
steps: Identify the exact failure symptom during the download step: (A) 'Insecure Download Blocked' alert, (B) 'Multiple File Download' permission popup, (C) OS 'Save As' dialog, or (D) file opening in a new tab/window without downloading.
If insecure downloads are blocked in Chrome/VDI environments, update the browser or site-level permissions to explicitly allow downloads from the target domain.
If a 'Multiple File Download' alert appears, configure the browser profile or Start Browser Plugin settings to allow automatic multiple downloads without prompting.
If Microsoft Edge displays a 'Save As' dialog instead of downloading automatically, update the custom automation Java code/browser plugin to version-compatible handling for the running Edge version.

If the file opens in a new tab/window instead of direct download, configure the 'Download/Print' option in 'Start Browser configuration' or add workflow logic to explicitly click the download icon inside the viewer tab.

When downloads spawn a new tab or window, use the 'Switch Window' plugin to shift context to the active download tab, perform download actions, close the tab, and switch focus back to the parent window.
Validate that the target file is present in the specified download directory with a valid file size and that the automation flow cleanly proceeds to subsequent tasks.

393cf5c2-d449-44f0-8205-7bc7e8e6612e.title: Automation Process Failure Due to Input File Formatting
steps: Inspect the automation process error logs and the input file to identify formatting discrepancies such as invalid delimiters, missing headers, unexpected newline characters, or encoding mismatches.
Correct the formatting errors in the input file to match the required format specifications.
Rerun the automation process with the corrected input file.
Verify that the automated process completes with a success status and that output records or downstream effects match expected results.

0ecfc38e-86a6-4ffb-86f1-e6209b03c428.title: ServiceNow Workflow and Integration Logic Remediation
steps: Inspect the queue state of affected ServiceNow records and review execution logs for items stuck in 'NEW' state, request timeouts, or duplicate staging tickets.

Verify the publication type and dynamic parameter mappings, ensuring components requiring dynamic parameters are published as processes rather than static workflows, and review incident and closing logic.
Refactor workflow variable passing: switch from script-based extraction (such as 'Get File Name and Modified JavaScript') to direct parameter passing, and remove unnecessary or conflicting plugins.
Remove hardcoded delays (such as 1-hour wait timers) that hold agent threads, and adjust environment thread limitations to prevent worker starvation and timeout expiration.
Trigger a test transaction through the modified workflow in a non-production environment, monitoring request state progression and verifying no duplicate staging tickets are generated.

e011a716-c966-41ce-b827-488ba6d57070.title: SFTP Connection and Credential-less Setup Support
steps: Identify the customer's SFTP connection details, client software, and whether they have generated an SSH key pair for credential-less access.
Provide guidance on configuring the SFTP client with the SSH private key, ensuring the matching public key is placed on the SFTP server.
Assist the customer with navigating the remote directory structure and transferring the requested file.

2a9360e3-8bd4-422e-b559-08846c02ca4d.title: Web Automation Blocked by Browser Security Restrictions
steps: Inspect the failure state in the automation log or active session to confirm whether the workflow is blocked by a native browser security prompt or internal warning page.
Configure the browser settings or enterprise browser management policies to disable the specific security prompt or add the target URL to the trusted site exception list.
Rerun the automated process Studio workflow to ensure the browser extension interacts with the web application without interruption.

892b0cee-c497-49ad-912f-f565953139d2.title: Browser Automation Driver Compatibility and Deployment Remediation
steps: Identify the installed major version of the target browser (Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge) and the AutomationEdge environment version (AutomationEdge 7.x or 8.x).

Download the WebDriver binary matching the exact browser major version, place it in the designated driver folder structure, ensure execution permissions are granted, and unblock any OS/antivirus security flags.
Update the Web GUI plugin JAR file in the installation directory: deploy web-gui-3.24.jar for AutomationEdge 7.x or web-gui-4.2.jar for AutomationEdge 8.x.
Open process-studio.bat in a text editor and add the JVM flag -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true to the Java startup options.

Configure the Agent with the JVM flag -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true. For AutomationEdge 7.x, edit startup.bat in the Agent installation bin directory to include the flag. For AutomationEdge 8.x, navigate to AE UI -> Agents tab -> Edit Agent and add the JVM flag.

Verify that the required browser extension is installed and enabled in the browser profile, and confirm that the browser executable path in the automation settings points to the valid executable location.
Restart the AutomationEdge Agent service and Process Studio, then execute a sample browser automation workflow to validate initialization.

8b069d9c-1188-4ccb-ae13-b6e3b64ff84d.title: Application Startup Failure: Missing Runtime Dependency Folder
steps: Inspect the application installation directory and verify whether required runtime dependency folders (such as Java components) are present and intact.
Verify that application license files are present in the expected directory, correctly assigned, and not corrupted.
Restore the missing Java components or runtime dependency folders from a known-good source package, or update the installation files to match required versions.
Launch the application and verify that all modules initialize without runtime dependency or license errors.

1d924a39-d2ff-4818-ba8f-bde063a3afae.title: Application Login Failure Due to Missing JavaScript Library
steps: Open the browser developer tools (Console and Network tabs) on the affected portal login page and refresh the page to identify failed asset requests or script execution errors.
Deploy and test the updated GUI Extension-based plugin containing the missing JavaScript libraries on the portal environment.
Clear the browser cache or open an incognito window, navigate to the portal login page, and attempt authentication.

7e009a6a-0092-4b60-b1e4-87530aec509f.title: False Positive Malware Detection of Chrome Driver
steps: Request specific security block details from the client, including the name of the security software, the exact threat name/signature flagged, and the blocked download URL.
Verify the SHA256 checksum of the provided Chrome Driver binary against the official repository or vendor release to confirm the file has not been altered or corrupted.
Provide the official file checksum and source URL to the client's IT security team, and instruct them to add a whitelist entry or exclusion for the Chrome Driver binary in their security software.
Have the client re-attempt the Chrome Driver download and run the browser automation to confirm the driver launches without being blocked.

8be0cbff-3f90-46f1-a3fc-8635c0310cef.title: Inefficient Bulk Data Processing with API Batching Challenges
steps: Inspect the data pipeline flow to identify whether source records (such as rows from an Excel file) are sent individually to the API or grouped into batches.
Restructure the request pipeline to aggregate incoming records into a single batch payload using the 'JSON output' plugin before calling the target batch API.
Configure the 'Split_To_Rows' (JSON Input) plugin to parse the batched API response array and split items back into individual tabular records.
Compare the row count and key attributes from the source data with the output rows produced by 'Split_To_Rows' after batch processing.

If 'Split_To_Rows' fails to correctly parse valid batch response structures, capture the raw response payload and pipeline plugin configurations, then escalate to the pipeline tooling/plugin maintainers.

5790fc04-6795-46fa-be9b-21e696452d54.title: T4 Production Server Automation Agent/Bot Environmental Discrepancy Remediation
steps: Inspect the domain-based URL settings and outbound network proxy configuration on the T4 production server, comparing them with known working production environment baselines.
Update the domain-based URL configuration and apply correct proxy settings on the T4 production server to align with functional environment parameters.
Check the automation agent service account permissions on the T4 production server, specifically evaluating 'Launch Application' privileges and file system write/upgrade permissions.
Grant the required administrator and full permissions to the automation agent service account, including explicit rights to launch applications and execute agent upgrades.
Verify whether the automation agent process requires an active interactive user session to execute tasks properly on the T4 server.
Engage the server infrastructure team to review and configure session handling policies if the automation agent requires a persistent active user session to function.
Trigger a full end-to-end test execution of the automation bot workflow on the T4 production server.

9ad646f4-0187-4b23-afbf-8167c8955789.title: Resolving Plugin and Dependency Version Mismatches Across Environments
steps: Compare the plugin folder and dependency JAR files (such as javassist JAR in the Process Studio/Agent lib directory) between the failing production environment and the working UAT environment to identify version differences or file corruption.
Take a backup of the existing plugin folder or dependency JAR file from the Process Studio or Agent lib directory on the target production machine.

Copy the matching, verified plugin folder or latest compatible dependency JAR file from the working environment (such as UAT Process Studio or Agent lib folder) and replace the target file in the production environment.
Restart Process Studio or the AutomationEdge Agent service to load the updated JAR files.
Perform a plugin sync (if applicable in Process Studio) and execute a test run of the affected workflow to verify end-to-end operation.

226fb677-7487-488d-b555-1afc8194d137.title: Web Automation Workflow Execution Failures
steps: Check workflow execution logs to identify whether the failure originates from the 'Start Browser' driver initialization or an error inside the 'Inject JavaScript' step.
Add the appropriate browser driver binary corresponding to your installed browser version and configure the 'Start Browser' plugin path to locate it.
Review the 'Inject JavaScript' step inside the loop construct, updating variable scopes and script syntax to ensure proper per-iteration execution.
Run the complete automation workflow from start to finish to confirm end-to-end execution.

c3a1d3ea-c0fa-4597-b2af-d233be24b2c6.title: Post-Upgrade Flow Activation Failure Due to License Step Count
steps: Inspect the AutomationEdge license status and server logs to verify whether flow activation failures stem from step-count license limits.
Acquire an updated AutomationEdge license that supports the required step count capacity and apply it to the server.
Reactivate the impacted client flows and trigger a test execution.

b8202b98-644a-49da-9d39-4c00bb445630.title: Vendor-Dependent Security Vulnerability Resolution Tracking
steps: Identify and catalog all detected vulnerabilities (such as weak ciphers) that require upstream vendor code or configuration fixes to resolve.
Submit the vulnerability details to the vendor and obtain a confirmed target resolution date and tracking reference.
Log the vendor dependency and resolution timeline in the internal tracking system to account for AppSec testing blockers.
Verify whether the vendor delivered the fix on or before the committed target resolution date.
Deploy the vendor remediation to a staging environment and re-run AppSec vulnerability scans to confirm resolution.

44e3995e-58d2-4529-85dd-cb17a818cafa.title: Python Server Initialization Failure After Server Restart
steps: Inspect the AutomationEdge Agent and embedded Python server logs to confirm whether the failure is caused by an unstarted runtime session, a port conflict, or a missing plugin dependency.
Restart the AutomationEdge Agent or Process Studio service to trigger a clean re-initialization of the embedded Python server session.
Verify that all required Python plugins and configuration parameters are loaded and intact within the agent environment.
Execute a basic test workflow containing a Python script step to validate that the embedded Python server accepts execution requests and returns output.
Escalate to the AutomationEdge platform administrator or support team with collected agent logs, environment variables, and Python server diagnostic logs.

84aa87c6-9795-4a11-84cf-fc0dbeb1adcc.title: Documentation Discoverability and Access Guidance
steps: Identify the specific product release, feature area, or topic requested by the user.
Locate and provide direct links to the relevant updated manuals, release notes, and configuration guides.
Confirm that the provided documentation links open without authentication or permission errors and fully address the user inquiry.

9be1e428-1c43-4934-ab86-106ceb5edbf6.title: Automation Platform Configuration Update
steps: Open Automation Edge, locate the target report or workflow configuration, and update the recipient email address with the newly requested value.
Trigger a test execution of the report or workflow to verify notification dispatch.

17bf5d27-ac6d-4b75-bdc8-38cc0b11aafe.title: Iterative Excel Column Validation Errors
steps: Compare all column headers in the user's Excel file against the complete required schema or template specification in a single pass to identify every missing column.
Add all missing required column headers into the Excel file and re-attempt the upload.
Link the incident to the planned product enhancement for batching column validation errors and notify the user of the resolution.

a83dc192-0220-422c-8a91-cb5b1f78c0dd.title: Dormant Account Activation
steps: Verify the identity of the requester and confirm they are authorized to request account reactivation.
Locate the affected account in the identity management directory and check its current status flags.
Enable the account and clear any dormancy or inactivity block flags.
Confirm the account state shows active and prompt the user to test authentication.

434ea279-f3e7-4260-bc35-1ee3e8556eb9.title: AutomationEdge User Access and Authentication Failures
steps: Verify whether the user is attempting to access the Web Portal or Process Studio, and confirm the target environment URL (T3 vs T4). Ensure the user is not entering T4 credentials into the T3 portal or vice versa.
Check the user account status in the AutomationEdge administrative console. If the account is marked as dormant, reactivate it. If the user has invalid credentials, trigger a password reset.

If Process Studio Single Sign-On (SSO) fails with Azure Active Directory, check the Azure AD application registration and verify that the Redirect URI http://localhost:2611/ is configured. Add http://localhost:2611/ to the Azure AD Reply URLs if it is missing.
If Process Studio reports a credential synchronization error, navigate to the AutomationEdge UI settings and enable the 'Use Server Credentials in Process Studio' option.

Verify user license assignment and validity in the AutomationEdge portal. Ensure an active Process Studio license is allocated to the user. If the license is expired, initiate a renewal using the tenant Org Code.

If Process Studio displays 'Unable to Validate Process Studio' or license validation errors on startup, check the local workstation NT ID / OS username case against the registered username on the server. If workstation restarts alter the character casing (e.g., uppercase vs lowercase), coordinate with local IT to standardize workstation username casing or apply patch 8.5.1 or later.
Conduct an end-to-end verification by having the user log in to both the AutomationEdge Portal and Process Studio, ensuring projects load without validation prompts.

33ee0520-5640-480e-8b57-93ce65690d3b.title: IE Automation Session Dependency on Windows Server 2022
steps: Verify whether the automation failure occurs exclusively when the RDP or interactive desktop session is disconnected. Run the job with an active, open RDP window, then run it again immediately after disconnecting the session.
Inspect the custom Java automation code and versions of Selenium and IEDriverServer in use on the Windows Server 2022 host to check for unsupported legacy dialog interaction methods.

Adjust the automation architecture to bypass disconnected UI session limitations by maintaining an active virtual display session or updating the automation logic to avoid reliance on native Windows file dialogs.
Trigger a complete test run of the file upload workflow while the RDP session is fully closed and disconnected.

d4b68832-5f50-40eb-889c-8b27779a3d0d.title: Issues Awaiting Product Release Fix (AE v8.4.0)
steps: Cross-reference the reported defect or feature request against the product development tracking backlog for AutomationEdge (AE) v8.4.0 to verify fix scheduling.
If a pre-release build or patch containing the AE v8.4.0 fix is provided by engineering, deploy it to the customer's User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment and execute validation tests.
Place the support incident on hold or pending release status, link the internal development tracking item, and set a recurring communication schedule to provide timeline updates to the customer.
Upon general availability of AutomationEdge v8.4.0 and clearance of any required environment access permissions, schedule and execute the production upgrade.

6aba3b44-d3d2-4dba-9a0e-db3636c6a7e4.title: Jira Plugin Project Fetch Failure Due to Account Configuration
steps: Verify whether the Jira account configured in the integration plugin is active and possesses 'Browse Projects' and 'Create Issues' permissions in the target Jira project.
Create a new Jira user account with appropriate project-level permissions and generate an API token for integration use.
Update the Jira plugin configuration in Process-Studio with the new Jira account username and API token.
Run the project fetch action within the Jira plugin to verify that project details load correctly.

5c8bf3e3-f3bf-41ea-81fd-780995e10ed5.title: Edge IE Mode Failure Due to Missing or Incorrect Drivers
steps: Inspect the environment or driver directory to determine whether the 32-bit or 64-bit IE driver is missing, outdated, or mismatched with the host architecture.
Upload and deploy the correct IE 32-bit or 64-bit driver to the designated driver directory or system PATH.
Restart Microsoft Edge and attempt to navigate to the target website in IE mode.

30b36305-5484-40e8-9c5e-59241a40da70.title: AutomationEdge SSO Configuration and Integration Troubleshooting
steps: Verify administrator access to both AutomationEdge and the Identity Provider (Azure AD or ADFS), and ensure the AutomationEdge server is accessible over HTTP/HTTPS (for example, http://aeserver:8080/aeui).
Determine which Identity Provider is being integrated with AutomationEdge: Azure AD or ADFS.

For Azure AD integrations, create or open the Azure AD Enterprise Application for AutomationEdge, configure SAML 2.0 settings (Entity ID, Reply URL), and ensure proper Service Principal Name (SPN) permissions and refresh token settings are established.

For ADFS integrations, configure the Relying Party Trust for SAML protocol. Verify that the identifier name matches the AutomationEdge entity ID exactly, ensure claim rules match required casing, correct the logout URL, and disable unused WS-Federation protocols.

Navigate to the AutomationEdge Settings tab and configure Single Sign-On parameters, including the IdP metadata, Keycloak SSO settings, SAML endpoints, and valid signing certificates matching the Identity Provider.
Initiate a test SSO login session from a new browser window to the AutomationEdge login URL.

c65cf67f-8bff-4310-af9d-ecf2c644af81.title: Process Studio: Custom Decryption for Unsupported Algorithms
