steps: Identify the encryption algorithm of the incoming file (for example, AES) and check if existing standard steps like PGP Decrypt Stream support it or fail due to external tool requirements like GnuPG.

Add a 'User Defined Java Class' step to the Process Studio transformation. Implement custom decryption logic in Java using standard Java cryptography libraries (such as javax.crypto.Cipher) tailored to the required algorithm and key specifications.
Execute the transformation using a test encrypted file and verify that the downstream step receives the plaintext data.

e86a5f12-1696-414f-bfe8-4152539252a5.title: Handling Client Rejection of Proposed Paid or Third-Party Solutions
steps: Assess the technical feasibility of the client request and identify whether the viable implementation requires commercial third-party plugins, external licensing, or additional costs.
Present the feasible solution to the client, explicitly detailing licensing costs, recurring fees, and third-party dependencies required for implementation.
Evaluate the client's formal response to determine whether they approve the commercial solution or decline based on cost or third-party preference.
Document the client's decision to decline the commercial or third-party solution in the ticket summary and close the request without implementation.

c767861f-53d1-4a02-a479-2f656e9a31f7.title: SFTP 'No Such File' Error Due to Incorrect Pathing
steps: Inspect the configured remote target path in the SFTP transfer settings. Verify whether the path begins with a leading slash '/' or if it is formatted as a relative path.

Update the remote path configuration to specify the absolute path starting with a leading slash '/'. If available, verify and copy the exact directory path directly from an SFTP client such as WinSCP.
Execute a test transfer or trigger the SFTP upload job with the updated path.

If errors persist after path correction, request remote directory permissions and transfer session logs from the client or remote SFTP server administrator to check for account access restrictions or server-side issues.

a314a2b1-c880-4dd7-9610-c7e159dc7d5d.title: Inject JavaScript Plugin Inconsistent Output and Null Returns
steps: Check the installed version of the Inject JavaScript plugin.
Upgrade the Inject JavaScript plugin to version 4.5 or later.
Inspect the data type configuration for input and output variables defined in the Inject JavaScript script step.
Add a 'Get Value' step directly after the Inject JavaScript step in the workflow to retrieve and map the output variable.
Run a test execution of the workflow and verify the variable output.

64383884-16ee-4f4d-a077-faee3e414802.title: External Email Service Connectivity and Timeout Troubleshooting
steps: Check network connectivity and latency from the application host to the external SMTP gateway endpoint on the configured port.
Increase the SMTP connection timeout and socket read timeout parameters in the application email configuration to accommodate intermittent network latency.
Contact the external email service provider (e.g., Proofpoint support) and internal network administrators to check for upstream packet drops, throttling, or gateway-side rate limits.

4b4ee04a-a00d-4025-ae0b-ae0d471075d1.title: Concurrent Workflow Execution Due to Orphaned Agent Processes and Cluster Misconfiguration
steps: Inspect the Task Manager or process table on the agent host to identify whether multiple orphaned java.exe processes are running from previous agent sessions.
Terminate any orphaned background java.exe processes remaining on the agent host after the agent session was closed.

Open the ae.properties file located in the AE Home directory and verify the ae.clusters.members= property contains the IP addresses of both cluster servers (for example, ae.clusters.members=10.0.0.1,10.0.0.2).
Verify in Windows Firewall rules that inbound and outbound traffic is permitted for the ae.clusters.port range between 5900 and 5910 on all cluster nodes.
Check the installed Java Runtime Environment (JRE) version on the AE and Agent systems to verify it matches the recommended version jre1.8.0_201.
Trigger a scheduled workflow and verify that it executes in a single thread without duplicate requests or simultaneous background runs.

5391c312-5aa5-4ad7-a43c-2f6d3ab4510e.title: Security Vulnerabilities (VAPT) Blocking Production Deployment
steps: Review the Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) report to classify points into items requiring code fixes versus items resolvable through architectural justification or remarks.
Obtain and deploy the vendor or engineering remediation patch (such as client 8.2.5 patch) for the actionable VAPT findings.
Draft and submit formal remarks and risk justifications for the remaining VAPT points that do not require code modifications.
Verify the applied patch in staging to confirm vulnerability remediation without introducing functional regressions.

0a4b67e1-368c-436d-bb7d-99ebe68ec5cb.title: Ticketing System Automated Notification Delivery Failure
steps: Check the recipient contact details and email address associated with the affected ticket in Zoho Desk to verify that the address is properly formatted, active, and correctly spelled.
Inspect the Zoho Desk notification settings and outgoing mail delivery logs for the ticket to determine the exact failure reason (e.g., hard bounce, spam block, or trigger rule misconfiguration).
Correct the identified notification trigger rule or clear the recipient email from the internal bounce and suppression list.
Send a test notification or manual message through the ticket and verify delivery confirmation with the recipient.

2a6f52bf-0a51-4869-9b6a-901a8ed8e402.title: Standardized OS and Database Migration Procedure
steps: Confirm the scheduled migration maintenance window, target host specifications, and stakeholder notification schedule.
Create full consistent backups of the PostgreSQL database, database configuration files, and system-level configuration files before initiating any migration actions.
Perform the operating system migration and relocate the PostgreSQL database to the designated target environment.
Verify PostgreSQL service status, database connectivity, data integrity, and dependent application connections on the target host.
Close the planned migration ticket and direct stakeholders to open a new support ticket for any subsequent post-migration issues.

3dd28795-f792-4548-97e1-5bbcfdf51e4a.title: Handling Client Requests for Sensitive or Confidential Data
steps: Review the client request to identify whether it explicitly asks for restricted entities, such as client names, bank names, or proprietary dataset details.
Notify the client that specific entity names and sensitive implementation details cannot be shared due to security policies, and propose providing high-level or anonymized information instead.
Escalate the inquiry to the appropriate internal team (such as the account management, product, or compliance team) to prepare the authorized high-level response.
Close the initial frontline support ticket after documenting the internal escalation ticket ID or handoff recipient.

5438eb3d-9f20-469f-9539-1892c2036d33.title: Email Server Connection Failure Due to SSL/TLS Hostname Mismatch
steps: Review current email configuration to record the configured SMTP server hostname, port, and required encryption protocol (STARTTLS or implicit TLS).
Inspect the SSL/TLS certificate presented by the destination SMTP server on the configured port and retrieve the Common Name (CN) and Subject Alternative Name (SAN) list.
Compare the configured SMTP hostname against the names listed in the certificate Subject Alternative Names (SAN) and Common Name (CN).
Update the email configuration hostname to match one of the valid domain names listed in the certificate Subject Alternative Names.
Perform a test email transmission to confirm successful TLS handshake and message acceptance.

If the remote mail server cannot be addressed using an existing certificate name, contact the customer to update their mail server certificate or provide an approved endpoint FQDN, and place the ticket on hold pending their updates.

62652ffd-f73e-48eb-abb1-622c208417d6.title: Workflow Execution Failure Due to Invalid Authentication Token
steps: Inspect the failed workflow logs to verify whether the failure reason is an 'access_denied' error associated with authentication or token refresh.
Open Postman and generate a new refresh token using the correct, current password and authentication parameters for the target service.
Update the workflow plugin configuration with the newly generated refresh token and save the settings.
Trigger a test run or observe the next scheduled workflow to verify that execution succeeds without access errors.

0f734733-9ea9-4180-9085-28c93b80cf1c.title: Manual File and Driver Provisioning from SFTP
steps: Confirm the request details, including the exact filename, driver type (such as Chrome or Edge), target version, and requester authorization.
Log in to the designated SFTP server and verify that the requested file or driver version exists in the storage directory.
Download the requested driver or file from the SFTP server to your local staging directory.
Deliver the downloaded file or driver package to the requester through the approved secure sharing channel and confirm receipt.

ddb76acf-82a5-42d4-be69-b4eacf7724e7.title: SSO Concurrent Session Restriction Misunderstanding Resolution
steps: Check the authentication type of the affected user accounts reporting concurrent session limit issues to determine if they authenticate as native application users or via Single Sign-On (SSO).

Inform the customer that internal concurrent session restriction settings apply only to native accounts. Explain that SSO session management and concurrent login controls are governed by their external Identity Provider (IdP) and must be configured at the IdP level. Note that product version 8.4.0 introduces updates for SSO-related session handling.

1317ff70-028a-4293-bdeb-a38000918a90.title: Copilot Access Failure Due to Cache Inconsistency During On-Prem Setup
steps: Open Process Studio, launch the Copilot tool, and check for the error 'Vertex AI API Error: HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found'.
Close Process Studio and clear the local application cache.
Relaunch Process Studio and access the Copilot tool to confirm API communication.
Escalate the ticket to the platform infrastructure team with Process Studio logs and on-premise Copilot configuration parameters.

a2b97a73-3738-4414-8403-674cabc5deb0.title: CSV and Spreadsheet Date Format Discrepancy Resolution
steps: Open the generated CSV file in a plain text editor (such as Notepad or Notepad++) to inspect the raw date strings directly.
Check whether the raw date strings in the text editor match the required target date format.

If the raw CSV data is correct but displays incorrectly in Microsoft Excel, advise the user that Excel applies automatic locale-based date formatting to standard CSV opens. Instruct the user to verify via plain text or import via Excel's 'Data > From Text/CSV' wizard while explicitly setting the date column data type to 'Text'.
If the issue involves automated processing of binary XLSB files where dates fail to parse correctly in dd-mm-yyyy format, verify the file extension and automation plugin version.
Convert XLSB files to XLSX format prior to plugin ingestion using a VBScript automation script executing Excel Application SaveAs with xlOpenXMLWorkbook format (file format code 51).

db0a9ef1-8c23-4c45-881e-fe9061c8bdfe.title: Incomplete SSL Certificate Chain Causing MID Server REST API Failures
steps: Check the MID Server logs for SSL handshake errors (such as PKIX path building failed) and verify whether the target web server presents a complete certificate chain.
Import the missing intermediate and root CA certificates into the MID Server's Java truststore (cacerts) and restart the MID Server service if required.
Execute a test REST API call through the MID Server to the target endpoint.
Contact the team managing the target web server and request that they install the complete certificate bundle (including intermediate certificates) on their server to fix the root cause.

62a10f1c-0b32-4fc4-9044-6c3e593573c3.title: DocEdge Decommission Runbook Management
steps: Collect environment details for the legacy DocEdge instance, target merged DocEdge setup, and any related AutomationEdge (AE) upgrade requirements.
Draft or update the DocEdge decommissioning runbook, including pre-checks, data backup requirements, migration sequence, and final service teardown steps.
Share the updated draft runbook with project stakeholders and schedule a review discussion to walk through the plan.
Perform a dry run or verification of the runbook procedures in a User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment.
Publish the finalized runbook to the team repository and obtain final sign-off for production decommissioning scheduling.

245629b6-9244-44da-9ec0-19034de457ef.title: AutomationEdge Process Stuck at Update Plugin Due to Database Contention
steps: Inspect the AutomationEdge database for active locks, blocked sessions, or long-running queries tied to the plugin update transaction.
Terminate or allow the identified blocking database transaction to complete, releasing the locks held on plugin execution tables.
Rerun the affected AutomationEdge process from the Agent and verify that the plugin update completes without freezing or throwing a Java NullPointerException.

f308ea98-de72-44b1-91e7-8f9f3756f668.title: User Login Failure Due to Authentication/Authorization Misconfiguration
steps: Inspect the application registration settings, redirect URIs, API permissions, and client secret validity in the Azure portal for the affected application and OneDrive plugin.
Create a new Azure application registration with the required API permissions and credentials for the failing plugin integration.
Test user authentication and refresh token generation through the integrated plugin using the new application configuration.
Escalate unresolved login issues and tenant-wide refresh token generation failures to the Azure/IT identity team for tenant-level policy and permission review.

48968fd1-e761-4a52-94d1-6e721d9f6dd6.title: AutomationEdge Process Studio Installation and Environment Troubleshooting
steps: Inspect the Process Studio installation directory and startup logs for missing Java Archive (JAR) files or ClassNotFound exceptions.
Verify network proxy settings and SSL certificate trust on the host machine to ensure outbound connectivity to required AutomationEdge endpoints.
Check that the host meets base Java runtime requirements and that the current user has read/write permissions to the installation and configuration directories.

If network connectivity, proxy authentication, or corporate SSL interception prevents Process Studio from completing setup, gather installation logs and proxy error details and escalate to the internal IT or Network team.

3ca5e9f9-4c9c-4463-b9a1-16bef15fb4b0.title: Application and Plugin Software Defect Resolution
steps: Identify the failing component and isolate the defect by analyzing error logs, bot execution traces, and environment dependencies (such as TN5250). Determine whether the defect requires an interim hotfix JAR or a major platform version upgrade.
Back up the existing plugin JAR files, agent configuration files, and relevant database state before deploying any software modification.

Obtain the required fix JAR (e.g., updated Terminal Automation plugin) or target version release package (e.g., AutomationEdge version 8.1.4) and deploy it to the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment.

Execute the failing workflow in UAT to validate that the bug is resolved (e.g., verify Terminal 'Get' output formatting, successful screen writes, login flows, or scheduled purge jobs) without breaking dependent bot scripts or requiring unauthorized coordinate shifts.
Secure production access and maintenance approvals, then deploy the verified fix JAR or upgraded platform build to the production environment.
Execute production sanity checks and initiate post-deployment monitoring (typically for two weeks) to confirm stability, bot execution success, and absence of secondary regressions.

5b4c88b0-3c95-442e-850a-2e94817d58ce.title: Trend Micro False Positive on New ChromeDriver Executables
steps: Inspect the Trend Micro alert details to confirm the detection engine flagged the ChromeDriver executable under heuristic rule HEU_AEGIS_CRYPT.
Verify the SHA-256 hash of the flagged ChromeDriver executable against the official distribution source to ensure file integrity.

Submit the verified ChromeDriver executable and hash details to the client's Information Security or Antivirus team, requesting immediate whitelisting and sample submission to Trend Micro for false-positive reclassification.
Request that the client security team configure persistent Antivirus exclusions based on directory paths or digital signature certificates rather than individual file hashes.
Provision the ChromeDriver executable back into the automation environment and run a validation test suite to ensure browser automation proceeds without interruption.

a09c77ad-0554-4ec2-a2fd-bca240d84559.title: RPA Platform Upgrade Blocked by Environmental Prerequisites
steps: Inspect the host operating system version and platform license validity against target RPA platform prerequisites.
Create backups of existing RPA platform configurations, Tomcat directories, JDK installations, and ActiveMQ data prior to applying any component changes.
Evaluate whether the host operating system meets minimum version requirements (e.g., Windows Server 2019 or above) and licensing is current.
Perform partial component upgrades by upgrading Apache Tomcat, Java Development Kit (JDK), and Apache ActiveMQ to remediate security vulnerabilities and compliance issues.
Validate service health for Apache Tomcat, JDK runtime, and ActiveMQ across target environments.
Submit an infrastructure request to upgrade the underlying server operating system to Windows Server 2019 or newer, and reschedule the full platform upgrade.

db65a46c-e955-4def-a635-1330676d6827.title: Intermittent PostgreSQL Client Connection Failures
steps: Inspect application execution logs for the failure signature: 'org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: The connection attempt failed. Caused by: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out at org.postgresql.core.v3.ConnectionFactoryImpl.enableSSL()'.

Connect to the PostgreSQL instance and verify the server SSL status and connection capacity by running 'SHOW ssl;', 'SHOW max_connections;', and inspecting active sessions in 'pg_stat_activity'. Confirm pg_hba.conf rules.

Update the client application JDBC connection URL to explicitly disable SSL negotiation and pass the required schema: 'jdbc:postgresql://<servername>/<database_name>?currentSchema=public&sslmode=disable'.
Execute the application workflow multiple times to test connectivity under load and inspect application logs for zero ConnectionFactoryImpl.enableSSL errors.

73068ffc-9480-4b1f-8ed2-b7631d5369d5.title: Agentic AI Plugin Lacks Direct Workflow State Management
steps: Identify the required variables, state parameters, and handoff points between the source and target workflows.
Configure an alternative variable routing or external state persistence mechanism (such as explicit payload metadata forwarding or an external data store) to bridge the workflows.
Execute a test transaction across the connected workflows to verify that downstream steps successfully receive and process the forwarded state variables.

dd082cc4-0b1c-4552-ba21-36bfe572df5c.title: Email Configuration Failure Due to Mailbox Storage Limit
steps: Check the current storage usage and quota allocation for the configured email address in the mail provider admin console or webmail interface.
Free up mailbox space by permanently deleting unneeded messages (including Trash, Spam, and Sent folders) or increase the mailbox quota limit in the mail administration panel.
Send a test email through the application's email configuration interface.

d7324504-fe3b-4a29-8457-e49f9dce8f24.title: Missing or Incorrect Certificate Deployment
steps: Inspect the application logs and target Java KeyStore (JKS) to verify whether the required certificates are missing, expired, or improperly chained.
Create a backup copy of the existing Java KeyStore (JKS) file and current certificate store to a safe location.
Deploy the required valid certificates into the target Java KeyStore (JKS) or application certificate path.
Restart the application service if required, then test the secure endpoint connection to verify the certificate chain is accepted without errors.

a34c0fbc-e3e0-4377-b3a6-5174b41ffca0.title: Audit-Identified Non-Compliant URL Configuration Remediation
steps: Locate the configuration files or environment variables that define the production frontend URL containing the exposed IP address.
Update the target URL configuration to use the approved domain name instead of the raw IP address.
Deploy the updated configuration and verify that application traffic routes through the domain-based URL without exposing IP addresses in the browser or API responses.

84b73cd0-8a20-4532-9e06-a4fae750ca7f.title: VBScript Automation Failure Due to Unhandled Excel Pop-ups
steps: Inspect the automation runner session to identify any active or background excel.exe processes and inspect visible modal prompts such as save prompts, update alerts, or add-in notifications.

Coordinate with the system administration or IT team to disable the identified pop-up by configuring Excel application policies, registry suppression keys, or default template settings for the automation service account.
Trigger a test run of the VBScript automation and verify that excel.exe terminates cleanly without leaving orphan processes or throwing file access errors.

17170b11-fcc6-4ced-9982-930beff92a5a.title: Post-Upgrade License Exhaustion and Functional Regression
steps: Check workflow execution logs and platform dashboard to identify whether job failures are caused by step unit license limits or agent/browser component failures.
Run the license step unit calculation utility provided for the upgraded version to determine total required step unit capacity across active workflows.
Apply and activate the updated license key matching the calculated step unit requirements in the platform license management interface.
Inspect agent status and update browser drivers or agent configurations to match target version compatibility requirements.
Execute a test run of sample and critical production workflows to verify successful end-to-end execution.

b028c855-dfe3-4f2b-88af-8674cc02a8c5.title: EWS Mail Input Plugin Configuration Support
steps: Check the integration platform being used. Verify whether the user is running the Windows-based plugin or a Java-based EWS implementation.
If the Windows plugin cannot download emails in the target environment, switch the implementation to a Java-based EWS solution.
Review the custom Java EWS configuration parameters, including endpoint URL, mailbox target, authentication credentials, and query filters.
Run a test email fetch operation using the verified Java code against the target mailbox.

13c58320-e2cc-40be-80ec-f92912fb5088.title: Malformed CSV Output Due to Text File Output Plugin Configuration
steps: Open the job transformation settings, navigate to the properties of the affected Text File Output plugin, and check the status of the 'Minimal Width' option.
Enable the 'Minimal Width' option in the Text File Output plugin configuration and save the transformation.
Run the transformation and inspect the newly generated CSV file in a text editor to confirm whitespace padding is removed.

55f8c63a-7547-43e0-96f7-a3f038928445.title: SQL Script Plugin Data Insertion Failure with ORA-01013
steps: Inspect the application execution logs to verify that the failure is isolated to the Execute SQL script plugin and displays error code ORA-01013. Confirm whether running the identical insertion query directly or via standalone application code completes without errors.
Check the plugin configuration for execution timeout thresholds or socket timeout parameters that could be triggering an automatic cancel request to the database.

Engage the Database Administrator (DBA) team with the session identifier, execution timestamp, and user credentials used by the plugin to review active database profiles, resource manager limits, lock waits, or database-side statement cancellation triggers.

72113119-f5e4-49c1-941b-297ce1c3946e.title: Planned Cloud Patching Impact Communication
steps: Identify the exact maintenance window and review which cloud components, such as the Automation Engine (AE), will be affected by the scheduled patching.

Send a communication to affected users and stakeholders stating the maintenance window, clarifying that no direct configuration changes are required on their end, and instructing them to ensure no automated workflows or jobs are running during the maintenance window.

Verify that all cloud services and Automation Engine (AE) components have returned to normal operation after the maintenance window closes, and notify stakeholders that automated workflows may resume.

206cc018-6271-480a-8fed-851952a0b28f.title: Client-Induced Logging Failure Due to Critical File Deletion
steps: Inspect the application installation directory, library path, and configuration directories to verify whether critical logging files (such as log4j library JARs or configuration files) are missing.

Restore the missing logging library files and configuration files from the official application release package, artifact repository, or system backup into their designated paths with correct file permissions.
Restart the affected application service if necessary, perform a test action that triggers log output, and inspect the target log directory to confirm that new log entries are generated.

17cb3eba-fbb8-454c-bd22-40c0860bfd7e.title: Handling Upgrade Failure and Rollback when Database Backup is Unavailable
steps: Verify the status and integrity of any existing pre-upgrade database backups and note any blocking UI or workflow errors in the upgraded environment.
Uninstall the faulty version (AutomationEdge 8.4.0) and perform a clean reinstallation/rollback to the previous stable version (AutomationEdge 8.2.4).
Perform necessary product licensing activities to re-license the newly installed AutomationEdge 8.2.4 instance.
Log into the AutomationEdge console and verify that custom task columns appear correctly in the UI and test workflows execute without errors.

49edc3bb-7fa3-4b5b-977c-af7250cd1957.title: File Decryption Strategy Due to Missing GPG Dependency
steps: Verify whether GPG.exe is absent or restricted in the host environment when executing the PGP Decrypt Stream plugin.
Replace the PGP Decrypt Stream step in the data pipeline with the User Defined Java Class plugin configured to perform Java-native PGP decryption.
Run a test pipeline execution using a sample encrypted file to validate that the User Defined Java Class successfully produces the decrypted output.

8c24fef4-11e9-4739-9561-2f4c3821bb69.title: New Client or Team Feature Access Provisioning
steps: Review the access request to confirm the target shared instance, client or team name, and specific feature licenses required.
Create and configure the new client or team tenant on the designated target instance.
Assign the requested feature licenses to the newly created tenant.
Perform a post-provisioning verification check by querying tenant status and confirming feature availability on the instance.

6d4c3099-d5c7-4634-8998-5fcb1e9803f0.title: Plugin Update and Compatibility Troubleshooting
steps: Identify the failing plugin, the exact host framework version, and the failure symptoms from logs (e.g., payload size limits, MIME type parsing errors, or missing API endpoints).

Inspect the email payload or server configuration: check whether the email body content type is 'text/plain', 'text/plain; charset=us-ascii', or 'message/rfc822', or if external mail server size limits are blocking delivery.
Back up the existing plugin JAR file and configuration files to a safe location before applying any replacements.
Deploy the updated patch JAR file matching the current framework version, ensuring all configuration properties are set properly.
Execute a test run using the failing payload (such as MIME types 'text/plain' or 'message/rfc822' or large attachments) to verify resolution.
If webmail or standard API retrieval is unsupported or failing, configure an alternative UI/Windows automation plugin to handle data ingestion.

If the issue is confirmed as a product defect scheduled for a future major release (e.g., version 4.7), document the known defect ID, notify the client, and provide temporary mitigation or release timeline tracking.

84b93796-07b4-4708-a57a-48c2f6647d1a.title: AutomationEdge Database Connectivity Misconfiguration
steps: Verify whether the requested datasource connection string URL is supported and available for your specific environment tier (e.g., On-Demand vs dedicated).
Check the DNS resolution of the database hostname from the AE environment to determine if it resolves to a public IP instead of a private IP across the VPC peering connection.
Enable the DNS resolution setting on the VPC peering connection to allow the database hostname (e.g., RDS) to resolve to its private IP address.
Test the datasource connection from the AutomationEdge instance or dashboard interface.
Contact the IT / Infrastructure team with the database endpoint, AE instance ID, and network trace details if connectivity fails and no further AE-side settings apply.

c6eb0956-d887-43c6-9de9-9bb0da4b448e.title: Database Schema Knowledge Gap Hindering Self-Service Data Access
steps: Review the request to identify the target database and the specific entities, attributes, and relationships needed (such as category, workflow, scheduler, or agent details).
Locate the relevant schema definitions and construct tested, read-only SQL queries that join the requested entity tables.
Provide the query templates and schema documentation to the requester, and request direct confirmation that the output satisfies their data requirements prior to ticket closure.

a819e8b8-be72-481f-aaa3-987a4418ec19.title: Third-Party API Rate Limiting Affecting Plugin Functionality
steps: Inspect the failing plugin's execution logs and identify error payloads returned by the upstream third-party service, specifically checking for 'Too many requests', HTTP 429 status codes, or quota exhaustion messages.
Check the public status dashboard and health status of the upstream third-party API provider to distinguish between an upstream service degradation or quota exhaustion.
Pause automated retries or wait a brief cooldown interval to allow upstream rate limit buckets to reset and avoid compounding rate-limit penalties.
Trigger a single test run of the affected plugin action to verify that upstream API calls succeed and downstream processing resumes.
Escalate to the integration owner or API administrator to evaluate account quota tiers, request a quota increase with the vendor, or implement client-side rate limiting and exponential backoff.

d04106bc-a9b0-4215-a1b0-5d788903b2a0.title: Initial Git Repository Setup and Connection Challenges
steps: Inspect the Git client SSL/TLS configuration and endpoint connectivity to the Git hosting service to identify the cause of the connection error.
Configure the required SSL/TLS settings or certificates in your Git client environment to establish a trusted secure connection to the remote repository.
Structure the local project within a single repository using designated separate folders and configure the required branch hierarchy.
Push the organized repository structure and branches to the remote Git hosting service.
Verify the remote repository web interface to confirm that the folder hierarchy and branches reflect the intended organization.

1f09fb8f-6007-47ff-8a8d-e87ff7e27f98.title: T3 Server Access Provisioning and Dormancy Activation
steps: Enable the user's account in the access management system for the T3 server.
Activate the dormant T3 server instance assigned to the user.
Verify that the T3 server is responsive and that the user can establish a connection.

27caad9f-5714-4246-a4f2-d85f935fa3e5.title: Application UI Component Failure Due to Linux File Access Restrictions
steps: Check application error logs to confirm if the failure in the UI component or plugin (such as Formula settings or Help) is caused by the Linux server blocking the required SWT JAR file.
Apply the workflow workaround by replacing the restricted plugin component with an alternative native step (for example, replace the Formula step with a Calculator step).
Run the updated transformation or workflow to verify that the step executes successfully without triggering UI or JAR loading errors.

4f398e03-9ee5-4a70-bc6e-f79cda41c139.title: RPA Task Failure Due to Unicode Character Handling
steps: Inspect the input data payload processed by the failing RPA task for non-ASCII or Unicode characters in fields like email subjects, recipient names, or body text.
Deploy and integrate the unicode converter using unicode_to_ascii_converter.txt into the RPA workflow to sanitize incoming text before processing.
Trigger a test execution of the automated RPA task with the Unicode payload and confirm task completion.

e5ca810c-9ef1-4e1f-8ce4-2802e1e3a152.title: Agent-Controlled RDP Session Lifecycle Management
steps: Log in to the agent machine and run the session query command to inspect current session status: query session <user_name>

Inspect the agent execution logs for errors during session initialization, checking for entries like 'Unable to get the Session status' and failures in QueryCommandParser.getActiveRDPSession or AgentUtil.startAndWaitForRDP.
Increase the configured time delay between consecutive workflow executions to ensure prior RDP sessions completely disconnect and log off before a new session is requested.
Verify the agent machine configuration against standard setup requirements and provide documentation on secure RDP workflow configuration.

7723a9b6-b8b4-44e1-99cd-f9071ac79130.title: Automation Bot Failure Due to Target Application UI/Event Changes
steps: Inspect the bot failure logs and inspect the target application page DOM to determine whether the bot failed to find the element selector (e.g., XPath) or failed to trigger the application's underlying input event listeners.

For selector mismatches: review the automation script (such as the Python automation file) with the development team and update the XPath or element locator to match the modified application UI structure.

For event detection failures where fields do not register updates: modify the bot step to inject JavaScript directly into the target page to dispatch native change or input events on the target element.
Execute an end-to-end test run of the automation script in a staging or non-production environment against the target application to confirm successful task completion.

21be57bc-486a-4b92-b0de-1e174287cbd4.title: Guiding Users to Generate Reports Using Existing Custom Report Tools
steps: Review the user's requested metrics and filters (such as agent utilization) to verify that the system's custom report builder supports all requested fields.
Provide clear step-by-step navigation instructions to the user on how to locate the custom report builder, select the required fields, apply the appropriate filters, and run the report.
Confirm with the user that the generated report meets their requirements and successfully displays the intended data before closing the ticket.

2e4fbf99-8234-48c2-bbee-720262cb324b.title: Plugin Distribution Request Fulfillment
steps: Identify the exact plugin name and target version specified in the user request.
Locate and retrieve the requested plugin distribution ZIP file corresponding to the verified version.
Validate the retrieved ZIP archive to ensure the file is non-empty and uncorrupted before distribution.
Provide the verified plugin distribution ZIP file to the user through the ticket attachment or secure delivery link, and resolve the ticket.

22ded704-3aeb-4991-9399-e52085a0f14e.title: S3 Outbound Connection Timeout
steps: Verify DNS resolution for the target Amazon S3 bucket or regional endpoint from the client machine.
Test TCP connectivity on port 443 from the client machine to the resolved Amazon S3 endpoint.
Inspect and update local firewall rules, proxy environment variables (HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY), and network security egress policies to allow outbound traffic on port 443 to S3.
Attempt the file download or connection to Amazon S3 again using the client application or standard AWS tools.
Escalate the incident to the Network and Cloud Infrastructure team with client IP details, target S3 bucket URI, traceroute results, and timestamped error logs.

5d1a20a3-b6fb-4551-abd1-1c2ac433f678.title: Chrome Compatibility Issue with Web GUI on AWS
steps: Create a backup copy of the existing Web GUI JAR files and JVM configuration files on the AWS instance before applying modifications.
Add the required Chrome compatibility JVM flag to the application server configuration.
Deploy the updated Web GUI 4.2 JAR file, replacing the previous version in the application directory.
Verify and apply proper ownership and execution permissions on the updated Web GUI 4.2 JAR file and modified configuration files.
Restart the Agent service to load the updated JVM parameters and Web GUI 4.2 JAR file.
Access the Web GUI from a Google Chrome browser session to confirm UI elements render correctly and functionality is restored.

97c03595-28ca-46a2-8b0e-90eed45da5aa.title: External Regulatory File Version Update Handling
steps: Identify the specific regulatory authority, the new return file format or version (such as updated eXtensible Business Reporting Language / XBRL specifications), and the affected internal target directory (such as the Automation folder).
Escalate the file version update request, including release specifications and Automation folder details, to the Professional Services (PS) team for deployment.
Link the intake ticket to the newly created Professional Services tracking ticket and close the initial service request.

431b2e6f-82a5-4e09-9de8-ade88a4589c1.title: Operational Overhead Due to Manual Bulk Credential Unassignment
steps: Review and validate the list of user accounts and corresponding credentials slated for unassignment against the authorized request ticket.
Navigate to each user record individually within the identity management console and manually remove or unassign the designated credentials.
Perform a lookup query or audit check on all processed accounts to confirm that none retain the unassigned credentials.
Log the completed manual changes in the access request ticket and track operational overhead to support product enhancement requests for bulk tooling.

72d522b2-8a62-44b1-8bb4-817684d266a5.title: Missing or Disabled Vault Connection
steps: Inspect the Vault connection settings for the affected service and environment to determine if the connection profile is unassigned or set to disabled.
Assign and enable the required Vault connection for the requesting service and environment.
Trigger a secret retrieval request from the application or restart the service to confirm successful authentication and secret retrieval from Vault.

5818ded7-4d0b-4ea9-aa85-8b60bb28fe00.title: Elara Solution Database Connection Timeouts and High CPU Utilization
steps:
Run a continuous timestamped network ping test from the agent machine to the database IP to rule out packet loss and latency spikes. Log the output to C:\Temp\PingLog.txt using the following batch script:

@echo off
setlocal EnableDelayedExpansion
set "LOGFILE=C:\Temp\PingLog.txt"
echo ==============================================>>"%LOGFILE%"
echo Ping started on %DATE% %TIME%>>"%LOGFILE%"
echo ==============================================>>"%LOGFILE%"
echo.>>"%LOGFILE%"
:loop
set "TS=%DATE% %TIME%"
echo [!TS!]>>"%LOGFILE%"
ping -n 1 10.3.7.53>>"%LOGFILE%"
echo.>>"%LOGFILE%"
timeout /t 1 /nobreak >nul
goto loop
Inspect client and workflow execution logs for SSL negotiation errors, specifically searching for org.postgresql.core.v3.ConnectionFactoryImpl.enableSSL.

Query PostgreSQL server parameters by running SHOW ssl;, SHOW max_connections;, and check active sessions in pg_stat_activity. If deeper connection handshake logging is required, verify postgresql.conf contains:
logging_collector = on
log_connections = on
log_disconnections = on
log_min_messages = info
log_hostname = on
Update the JDBC connection string configuration to explicitly disable SSL negotiation and define the schema: jdbc:postgresql://<servername>/<database_name>?currentSchema=public&sslmode=disable
Check AWS EC2 CPU utilization metrics and recent VPC routing/NAT gateway additions to determine if CPU saturation or routing issues are impacting agent connectivity.
Escalate to the infrastructure team if AWS EC2 high CPU alarms and database timeouts persist after applying the JDBC connection string fix and validating NAT routing.

cab1459d-1616-4070-93e9-e3dd704894e7.title: Customer Inquiry: Source IP Resolution Logic
steps: Review the customer ticket to identify the exact audit log scope (such as Application Engine (AE) UI audit logs) and the specific technical clarification requested regarding source IP capture.
Provide the customer with a detailed explanation of the source IP capture mechanism, detailing header evaluation order and fallback behavior for recording client IPs in the audit logs.
Confirm with the customer whether the provided explanation satisfies their inquiry or if further clarification on audit compliance is required.

a9872002-a1bd-40c4-8d85-7ee19c6744fe.title: Incident Log Retrieval Challenges
steps: Locate and copy the Sys ID of the target incident record from your incident management platform.
Navigate to the log search interface and apply the copied Sys ID into the 'Source Request' filter field instead of using the incident number filter.
Execute the query and verify that log entries matching the incident timeframe and events are displayed.

f16cccd3-5b51-46b3-b306-3b8370a28e3f.title: Agent Upgrade Feature Misunderstanding and Clarification
steps: Inspect the reported agent version, current status indicator, and the exact behavior or prompt described by the customer.
Compare the reported behavior against the release notes and feature specifications for the installed agent version to determine if the behavior is an intended feature or an actual defect.
If the behavior is an intended feature, provide the customer with detailed documentation explaining the functionality, including upgrade indicators, benefits, and opt-in/opt-out management options.

If the behavior is a confirmed bug (such as a plugin sync failure), log the bug details, inform the customer of the upcoming patch release version containing the fix, and apply any known temporary workaround.
Verify that the agent is running, active processes are executing successfully, and the customer has no further blocking issues before closing the ticket.

bdecfb6a-88ff-4c9b-8a58-7c5839aefab9.title: Troubleshooting Inconsistent File Deletion Plugin Behavior and Configuration
steps: Determine whether the target files reside on the local system or on a remote server.
For files located on a remote server, execute file deletion using PowerShell commands targeted at the remote host rather than local file system plugins.
In Process Studio, inspect the Delete files plugin configuration. Verify that the file path is specified and that a wildcard expression is defined (for example, .*txt).
Check the plugin version and workflow script functions. If using version 4.7 or higher, note that deleteFile() explicitly throws an exception when the specified target file is not found.

0c8cdb39-3c83-49a5-b23f-a9a074187447.title: Misconfigured Service URL Mapping Leading to Access Issues
steps: Inspect the URL mapping and routing configuration for the affected service to identify which backend server destination is configured.
Update the server configuration so the service URL mapping points to the correct target server.
Attempt to log in to the application through the service URL to verify access restoration.
Escalate the incident to the backend infrastructure or application engineering team with diagnostic logs and current mapping details.

c1d8afb1-78eb-48da-8d5f-a02e8864e71f.title: Incorrect API Token Usage for Specific Operations
steps: Inspect the failing API request headers and payload to identify the target endpoint and the type of token currently being passed.

Check the API specification for the target endpoint to verify the required authentication type (for example, whether the endpoint requires an encrypted operation token rather than a general session token).
Send the user the official token generation documentation and specific instructions for generating the required operation token.
Have the user execute the API call using the newly generated operation token and confirm that the operation (e.g., file transfer) succeeds without authorization errors.

f91fd3ca-4f01-4ed5-8bfb-75aa78ce1c33.title: New User Trial License Activation Failure
steps: Check if the user provided an Organization Code (ORG Code). If not, request the ORG Code from the user.
Process and assign the free trial license to the provided ORG Code in the licensing system.
Ask the user to log in and confirm they can open Process Studio and access core features.

17076911-21a8-4214-b925-effd04643608.title: Monitoring Incident Data Ingestion Failure
steps: Inspect the incident staging table and ingestion logs to confirm whether SolarWinds event payloads are arriving and failing parsing or missing entirely.
Check the installed SolarWinds integration plugin version to determine if the staging table ingestion issue matches the known defect scheduled for resolution in release 4.5.
Acknowledge the known plugin issue, link the incident to the tracking record for plugin release 4.5, notify stakeholders of the planned release resolution, and close the incident ticket.

ad8c02a9-37cd-4799-a883-5197bae2b74d.title: Remediating Application and Workflow Failures from Java Environment Issues
steps: Inspect the active process table on the application server to check for multiple running OpenJDK processes and assess system memory utilization.
Inspect client-side logs for Java runtime exceptions, specifically looking for java.lang.NoSuchMethodError or classpath library mismatches following server restarts.
Terminate conflicting orphaned OpenJDK processes, increase the configured memory allocation for the agent, and restart the server application service.
Trigger a test workflow execution and verify whether jobs complete without returning 'unknown errors at server side' or NoSuchMethodError exceptions.

71b3282a-3c03-43a0-b0c7-11f1b7f2be3b.title: AutomationEdge Platform Upgrade Challenges
steps: Verify underlying infrastructure compatibility prerequisites, specifically confirming that the PostgreSQL database version meets target version requirements (e.g., PostgreSQL 14–15).
Perform a complete pre-upgrade backup of the AutomationEdge application files, database instances, and configuration files.
Obtain the required target AutomationEdge upgrade packages and plugins via the secure download process.

Execute the platform upgrade to the target version (e.g., AutomationEdge 8.2.3 or 8.2.5), deploying updated web archives (including aeengine.war) and clearing tempDir caches if temporary directory errors occur.
Upload the updated platform license and verify user account roles (such as creating or assigning a T3 user license if validation fails).
Upload and deploy compatible Process Studio packages and required workflow plugins (such as plugin 4.2 or 4.6).
Check web application SSL/TLS connectivity to ensure the URL does not display 'Not Secure' warnings by verifying the Java KeyStore (JKS) certificate file path configuration.
Validate end-to-end operational functionality including agent connectivity, workflow activation, and Process Studio validation.

ee47bf41-29b4-46d3-8dd0-090eaa9a566a.title: Agent O365 Plugin Connectivity and Proxy Configuration
steps: Check the current proxy settings on the agent machine by inspecting the system LAN settings and checking if a proxy configuration file exists in the AGENT_HOME/conf directory.

Open Internet Options -> Connections -> LAN Settings on the agent machine. Ensure proxy configuration is set and add the AutomationEdge Server's IP address as well as required Office 365 endpoints into the proxy exception list. Alternatively, replicate the exact proxy exception list from a known working agent.
If utilizing automatic proxy configuration, download the Automatic Configuration Proxy config file from AEUI -> Settings -> Proxy Settings and deploy it directly under the AGENT_HOME/conf directory.
Restart the agent and verify that the agent connects to the server and the O365 plugin initializes and establishes connection successfully.

If proxy settings are correct but the agent fails to synchronize the O365 plugin during automatic configuration download, escalate the issue to the platform engineering team for manual plugin deployment and package investigation.

abcbda87-73f0-4e5f-8b85-61571e29abc9.title: Excel Input Plugin Data & Metadata Interpretation Troubleshooting
steps: Inspect the incoming Excel file format to verify it is not in legacy Excel 5.0 / 7.0 (BIFF5) format.
Check dynamic sheet name parameters for unintended formatting, such as numeric conversions appending '.0' to the sheet name.
If the table header does not begin at cell A1, open the Excel Input 'Sheets' tab and configure the start row and start column to match the header position (for example, row 7).
Check column header strings for leading or trailing whitespace. Enable the 'Trim' option on string fields in the plugin configuration or sanitize the source headers.
When processing files where column sequence changes dynamically but total column count is known, configure the field names sequentially as 'Col1, col2.....' in the Microsoft Excel Input Plugin.
When using 'SheetName.FieldName' format, verify that the 'Field in the input to use as filename' configuration field is populated.

Configure decimal data types and source cell formatting. For XLSB files where displayed precision limits read values, adjust the column formatting in the source workbook or update the target field data type in the plugin to prevent unexpected rounding.
Enable 'fail on column name not found' in the plugin and encapsulate the step inside a Try-Catch block to handle missing column exceptions cleanly.
Check file encoding settings if non-standard characters cause parsing errors. Set file encoding to Windows-1252 or recreate the file with UTF-8 encoding.

f0e2e580-bf82-4f47-873c-08f387b07a6e.title: Application Component Failure Post-Migration Due to Incomplete Deployment or Misconfiguration
steps: Inspect the aehome directory on the target host to verify whether the psplugin folder is present.
Copy or restore the missing psplugin folder from the source migration package into the aehome directory.
Check the agent configuration directory for an active proxy configuration file and confirm if the network environment requires an outbound proxy.
Remove or back up and delete the proxy configuration file from the agent configuration directory if no proxy is needed in this environment.
Start the agent service and verify that plugin downloads complete and the agent successfully initializes.

0a8ac1c3-0133-49d7-b802-de11a36da286.title: Undiagnosable NetApp NAS Shared Path Issues Due to Missing Audit Logs
steps: Inspect the audit configuration on the affected NetApp NAS storage virtual machine and share to confirm whether audit logging is currently enabled and what event types are tracked.
Enable audit logging on the NetApp NAS storage virtual machine for the affected shared path, configuring it to record access attempts, authentication events, and session activity.
Generate a test access event against the shared path and verify that a corresponding audit event appears in the NetApp audit log repository.

Document in the incident ticket that root-cause analysis for the past incident cannot be completed due to lack of historical logs, inform stakeholders, and place the shared path under monitoring for reoccurrence.

2da5fd9d-f373-49ed-85a3-30e9ae7d59e2.title: Agent Failure Due to Server Configuration Discrepancy
steps: Collect agent execution logs and runtime status from both the failing server and a known functional reference server.
Perform a line-by-line configuration comparison between the failing server and the working reference server, checking config files, environment variables, network endpoints, and user permissions.
Create a timestamped backup of the current agent configuration files on the failing server before modifying any settings.
Update the agent configuration on the failing server to align mismatched parameters with the working reference server baseline.
Restart the agent service on the affected server and check process status and communication health.
Escalate the incident to the engineering team, providing the side-by-side configuration diff, collected logs from both hosts, and connection test results.

2c77dc02-a081-4eff-a747-539c864abe4e.title: Process Studio License and Registration Failures
steps: Check the licensing portal or administrative console to verify the current license assignment and registration status of the affected user.
Unassign the Process Studio license from the affected user account in the licensing portal to clear the corrupted or stale registration lock.
Re-register Process Studio by assigning the license to a clean user profile or new user account.
Launch Process Studio and log in using the newly registered user credentials.
Escalate to the application licensing administration team to inspect backend registration seats and reset the node identifier for the workstation.

993f74ec-d647-4c08-a585-17ecc9e7d90a.title: Java Heap Space Exhaustion During Large Excel File Processing
steps: Inspect the host system memory utilization and the JVM heap configuration parameters allocated to Process Studio and the Agent.
Increase the maximum Java heap allocation for Process Studio and Agent, or provision additional system RAM to the host environment.
Configure the workflow to process the Excel dataset in smaller row batches rather than loading the entire file into memory at once.
Re-run the Excel processing job and monitor JVM memory usage to confirm the run completes without heap exhaustion.
Engage the engineering team for code-level investigation into stream-based parsing or architectural memory optimizations.

57164d50-2c70-43a9-897b-d33f7ba83354.title: Handling Client Feature Requests Denied or Deferred by Product
steps: Review the requested feature against existing plugins and third-party library limitations to determine technical feasibility.
Submit the requirement to the product team to evaluate business justification and determine if the use case applies broadly across customers or is specific to a single client.

Check the product team's decision: proceed to step 4 if the request is deferred for a future release due to technical roadmap feasibility, or proceed to step 5 if the request is denied outright for insufficient business justification.
Inform the client of the current plugin or library limitations, log the request in the product backlog for consideration in upcoming plugin releases, and update the ticket status.
Inform the client that the requested custom plugin or feature cannot be prioritized due to product scope and business justification limits, then close the ticket.

fc4217ea-5100-409c-911e-f6ff3b5e7622.title: RDP Plain Text Password Handling and Security Policy Violation
steps: Inspect the active RDP client configuration and determine the installed application version.
Upgrade the RDP application or component to version 8.1.0 or later to apply the security fix for plain text credential handling.
Configure credentials securely using cmdkey or implement certificate-based authentication in accordance with policy mandates.
Engage the customer and security stakeholder to review the authentication method and verify policy compliance before ticket resolution.

69f527a7-9898-4c5b-bbc4-c3d3233d5a19.title: Automated Workflow Stalling/Failure with External Integrations
steps: Inspect the bot workflow definition for static xpaths, unmanaged static delays, and missing explicit wait conditions on interactive elements.
Refactor the bot workflow by replacing static xpaths with dynamic locators, removing arbitrary static sleep delays, and inserting explicit wait plugins before UI interaction points.
Check if the bot stalls when processing multiple inputs concurrently, such as multiple email inputs arriving in the scheduler queue.
Split tightly-coupled plugin actions into separate, modular workflows instead of relying on implicit delay timers within a single job.

For external service failures (such as O365 connection reset errors), inspect the redirect_uri parameters, token refresh settings, and firewall/network connectivity during scheduled execution windows.

2ce2dfd8-4a08-4af2-9d11-530fd607c0c1.title: AEUI Functional Regression After DocEdge Upgrade
steps: Record the exact version numbers of the deployed AEUI client and the newly upgraded DocEdge instance.
Reproduce the copy/paste and task management failures in AEUI while capturing browser developer console logs and network traffic HAR files.
Extract DocEdge backend server and API gateway logs corresponding to the timestamps of the failed AEUI actions.
Open an engineering escalation package containing the client HAR files, backend log traces, reproduction steps, and version details for hotfix prioritization.

376f8c97-097c-4022-b09a-d86114a48d85.title: Log Content Security Justification for Operational Data
steps: Identify and examine the specific log entries and workflow file paths flagged by the client or auditor in the agent server logs.

Verify whether the logged data contains secrets, credentials, or Personally Identifiable Information (PII), or if it consists strictly of operational metadata required for workflow tracking and diagnostics.
Confirm that access to the agent server logs is restricted to authorized personnel and protected by existing server-level access controls.

Prepare and send a formal response explaining the operational necessity of logging workflow paths (e.g., job tracking, troubleshooting, and execution integrity) alongside details of existing access controls protecting the logs.
Confirm client or auditor acceptance of the provided justification and close the inquiry ticket.

40fd3ce1-0d41-4f06-bdc0-0f3f37d4c6dc.title: AutomationEdge Scheduled Process Failure Due to Timezone Mismatch and Scheduler Corruption
steps: Check automationedge.log around the expected execution timestamp to verify whether the scheduler fired and whether any user recently modified the schedule.

Check the timezone configured on the Tomcat application server, the database server, and the client machine used to access the AutomationEdge User Interface (AEUI). Access the AEUI directly from the server machine to inspect the configured schedule time.
Align the database server timezone and the Tomcat application server timezone so that all system components operate under the required matching timezone.
Verify whether the existing schedule triggers correctly after aligning the timezones.
Recreate the scheduler in the AEUI: delete or disable the malfunctioning schedule entry and create a fresh schedule using the aligned server timezone.
Monitor the next scheduled execution window in automationedge.log to confirm the newly created scheduler executes successfully at the specified time.

76505870-8ab9-4f2d-aa54-36e6626f9df9.title: Automation Edge License Deactivation Due to Nginx Service Failure
steps: Check the status of the Nginx service on the Automation Edge DC environment host.
Start the Nginx service on the DC environment host.
Log in to the Automation Edge portal and launch Process Studio to verify license validity and user access.

7c5910b2-1756-4c99-b41f-bfbf2bfa7e45.title: Web Automation GUI Spy/Recorder Malfunction Due to Input State
steps: Inspect the active GUI Spy/Recorder session to confirm that element inspection and URL launching are unresponsive due to input state locking.
Reset the mouse cursor and clear the system input state by moving and clicking the mouse outside the target application window.
Open the target URL and attempt to spy on a UI element using the GUI Spy/Recorder tool.
Replace the specific automation JAR (Java Archive) file associated with the GUI Spy component with the updated or patched version.

88c134eb-d06f-4948-9a5c-59875b83258c.title: Client-Specific Certificate and Attestation Document Provisioning Challenges
steps: Identify and categorize the incoming certificate or attestation request into one of three categories: Regulatory/Compliance Attestation Document, Source Code Certificate, or Server SSL Certificate Installation.

For regulatory compliance requests (such as RBI ITE compliance), verify the expiration status of the existing source code attestation document, retrieve the latest validated attestation document corresponding to the client's deployment, and deliver it to the client.
For source code certificate requests, confirm the exact deployed AutomationEdge version (e.g., version 7.6.3) and record the client's specific certificate format and sharing requirements.

For server SSL certificate requests, determine if the client requires a Certificate Signing Request (CSR) generated on the server or if they can provide a signed certificate bundle directly for import into the AutomationEdge server.
Escalate unresolved certificate format conflicts or CSR process mismatches to the Product and Engineering team, and arrange a joint technical bridge with the client.

0d96ea49-8aeb-42f4-97b5-b0f2a1494069.title: Resolving RDP Configuration and Windows Security Policy Conflicts in AutomationEdge Agent
steps: Inspect the AutomationEdge agent execution log for session initiation failures referencing startAndWaitForRDP, getActiveRDPSession, getActiveSession, or 'Unable to get the Session status'.
Verify that the agent service account is an active member of the local 'Remote Desktop Users' group on the target host.
Check if Windows Defender Credential Guard or domain security hardening policies are actively blocking the reuse or storage of RDP credentials.

Coordinate with the Windows and Infrastructure security team to request a policy exception or configure Group Policy Objects to allow credential delegation for the AutomationEdge agent service account.

For workflows performing desktop mouse actions and UI interactions, configure RDP client settings and Windows registry keys on the agent host to enforce active desktop rendering when sessions are minimized or lose focus.

6549d074-67ec-4b6a-807d-b437e198d06b.title: OneDrive Plugin 'Item Not Found' Due to Authentication Token Issue
steps: Confirm that the target file exists in OneDrive and verify that the plugin fails with the 'Item not found' error during execution.
Open a new Incognito or InPrivate browser window, log in to Microsoft 365 with the current account credentials, and generate a new OAuth refresh token.
Update the OneDrive Download Plugin configuration with the new refresh token and run a test file download.

f29bcea7-14de-45f1-85a8-937d9ae54c8c.title: Workflow Failure Due to Undefined Field Reference in Data Processing Step
steps: Inspect the failure logs for the failing data processing step (such as GroupByStep) to identify the specific field name reported as missing or undefined.
Check the output schema and field mapping of all steps immediately upstream to verify if the identified field is emitted, renamed, or dropped.
Update the workflow configuration by either correcting the field name mapping in upstream steps or updating the aggregation step to reference the correct available field.
Trigger a test execution or dry run of the workflow with sample input data and verify that the step initializes and completes successfully.

24eb583f-5ff2-4c24-881d-5a5891c566bf.title: Third-Party Plugin Incompatibility Due to Upstream API Changes
steps: Inspect the plugin execution logs to verify whether the failure stems from upstream API validation errors, such as rejected project key/ID formats or duplicate field entries.
Back up the current plugin archive or JAR file and its configuration from the plugin directory to a secure backup location before applying any patch.
Deploy the hotfix plugin JAR file containing updated field mappings (such as lowercase project field mapping and corrected parameter validation) into the environment.
Execute a test integration transaction (for example, creating a test issue via the plugin) to confirm the upstream API accepts the payload without validation errors.
Schedule a permanent upgrade to the official maintenance release containing the permanent fix once published by the engineering team.

766276ea-a976-4cb8-906d-948b99051c68.title: Missing Plugin Access Due to Unassigned Permissions
steps: Inspect the user account, environment, or tenant entitlement settings to identify which plugins are currently assigned.
Provision and assign the requested plugin to the target user account, environment, or tenant.
Ask the user to log out, log back in, and verify that the plugin is visible and operational.

b35aa0f4-1da4-480c-bed0-32725ed9dfed.title: Post-Upgrade Behavioral Change in API or Function Due to Defect Fix
steps: Inspect the failing script execution logs to identify the exact function call and the newly returned error or status code.
Compare the upgraded component version changelog and release notes against the observed error to confirm whether the new behavior is an intentional defect fix.
Update the client script or automation logic to handle the new return code or catch the specific error condition properly.
Open a ticket with the component vendor or development team to request backwards-compatibility flags or report the breaking behavioral impact.

e75d83f4-5f92-4010-a10c-f8c76262bab7.title: Licensing and Resource Allocation Management
steps: Review the customer ticket to classify the request type: licensing model clarification, component instance allocation/trial renewal, demo quota increase, or production license upgrade.
For questions about usage metering, provide standard documentation explaining how minute and step units deduct during workflow executions, then close the ticket.

For instance allocation requests (such as Process Studio) or trial renewals, evaluate against environment policy: approve allocations and renewals for User Acceptance Testing (UAT) or trial environments, but reject non-compliant production instance requests.
For demo or sandbox environments requiring increased step units, adjust the environment step unit allocation directly in the licensing console to the requested limit (for example, 5,000 step units).
For production step unit quota increases exceeding current license tiers, provide instructions for the customer to generate a usage report to initiate the formal license upgrade process.

d7ed7f03-e8fa-4f2f-8a94-8dcc1c03c6ec.title: SharePoint Site Creation Failure Due to Incorrect Graph API Endpoint
steps: Inspect the site creation automation configuration or script to identify the target Microsoft Graph API endpoint URL.
Update the Microsoft Graph API endpoint in the provisioning configuration from https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites to https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups.
Execute a test site creation request through the updated provisioning workflow.

95db4c11-cbfb-4a5a-9c00-504770f1a907.title: Copilot Access Provisioning and Environment Selection
steps: Identify the requester's project context, target version compatibility (e.g., version 8.2 vs 8.4), and determine whether access is needed on the T3 environment (internal/development) or T4 environment (client/project-specific).
Verify that all required project approvals for access to the requested environment (especially for client-facing or T4 environments) have been received.
Provision the user account and assign Copilot access on the T3 server.
Create the project or client tenant on the T4 instance, assign the necessary PS licenses, and enable the Copilot plugin.
Confirm that the user can log in to the assigned environment (T3 or T4) and interact with Copilot features without permission errors.

f2e68dc1-041e-4a6e-b0be-0de9f87736ce.title: Driver Management and Client-Side Configuration Resolution
steps: Inspect the client machine configuration to identify missing drivers or incorrect driver placement locations affecting client operations and log data retrieval.
Provide the required driver packages to the client machine and place the driver files into the approved driver directory structure.
Test the client application and attempt audit log data retrieval to confirm end-to-end functionality.

46cf9f0f-44b0-45ca-a7f7-ae34f9bd6277.title: Intermittent Process Output Mismatch Due to Plugin Configuration
steps: Inspect system metrics and JVM logs during the failed execution to identify memory exhaustion, page file depletion, or abnormal JVM terminations.
Review the workflow design to locate memory-intensive steps such as Stream Lookup operations and unbuffered SQL script plugins.
Modify the SQL script plugin configuration in the workflow to enable "Execute for Each Row" and configure it to capture delete statistics.
Execute test runs of the modified workflow in the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment using production-scale data volumes.
Deploy the validated workflow and plugin configuration to the production environment during an approved maintenance window.

4c2563de-6ab0-4b8c-8839-d7a99dd926f7.title: Automation Workflow Browser Session Termination
steps: Inspect the automation workflow configuration and task sequence for any embedded scripts (such as PowerShell scripts) configured to kill or terminate browser and driver processes.
Remove or disable the identified process termination script from the automation workflow sequence.
Check all downstream integration steps, such as email sending API calls, for improper string handling and formatting that trigger HTTP 400 Bad Request errors.
Trigger a complete test execution of the workflow and monitor the browser session to verify it finishes without 'invalid session ID' errors.
If intermittent browser pauses or stoppages persist despite removing the termination script, inspect network connectivity and endpoint stability between the automation runner and target services.

8f7ac9d4-940e-40c8-84dc-68310af2d96d.title: Application License Invalidation Requiring Re-registration
steps: Verify that the user's license is active and correctly assigned in the central license management portal.
Deregister the application instance from the application user interface (UI) to clear the desynchronized local license state.
Re-register the application instance through the application UI using the assigned user credentials.
Launch the application and verify that the license error no longer appears and the workspace opens normally.

32c4fcae-bf5e-4ca2-8300-89a97925edac.title: Software Upgrade Requiring Full Downtime Despite Rolling Upgrade Request
steps: Review the target release notes and migration guides to determine if the update includes database schema migrations that prevent concurrent old/new version operation.
Perform a complete database snapshot and file system backup of the application server configuration and state before stopping services.
Notify stakeholders of scheduled maintenance, stop all connected application agents, and stop the main application server services to prevent new transactions.
Execute the server upgrade package to run database schema migrations and update server binaries to the target version.
Deploy and execute the target version upgrade package across all application agent nodes.
Start the main application server services and all upgraded agents, then verify agent registration and core transaction health.

5942fd90-953e-4e31-9535-088c5889b303.title: Configuration Granularity Limitation for Time-Based Settings
steps: Inspect the requested time-based configuration parameter (such as 'Cleanup request older than (hour)') to verify whether the system schema only accepts integer hour values.
Inform the requester that the parameter only accepts whole hour values due to system design limitations, and decline the request to set the parameter to minutes.

4f60f2cd-9936-40a1-9afe-53c856674f67.title: AutomationEdge User Management Configuration Constraint
steps: Review the requested configuration changes to separate configurable role permissions (such as the Password tab) from hardcoded product limitations (such as the 'Native Users' option).
Create or modify a custom role in AutomationEdge to remove access to the Password tab for custom users.
Communicate to the customer that the 'Native Users' option is mandatory by product design in AutomationEdge and cannot be hidden or removed.

a10b7b68-7ec7-432e-a161-bc451f55c71a.title: Remediating Plugin Configuration Reversion Due to Persistence Defect
steps: Inspect the execution logs and workflow configuration to verify whether the plugin is executing with previous static values rather than the updated dynamic values passed from previous steps.
Create a backup copy of the existing plugin JAR file and export the current workflow definition before applying any file changes.
Replace the affected plugin JAR with the patched version containing the corrected configuration serialization logic.
Re-save the workflow configuration using the dynamic path parameter, execute the workflow, and confirm that the plugin executes using the dynamic path without reverting to stale values.
Escalate to the plugin development team with workflow execution logs, plugin configuration state, and the JAR version information.

8f92ac43-3faa-46ca-9ef4-b63cab3656ad.title: Automation Edge Workflow Stalling/Failure Due to Plugin/Configuration Issues
steps: Inspect the active workflow execution state in the AutomationEdge console to determine if the agent is frozen or caught in a repetitive step loop.
Inspect the step parameters and column mappings for the failing plugin component (such as Mail Sending or Loops plugins) within the workflow definition.
Verify the environment variable paths, runtime dependencies, and output variable definitions for custom script plugins such as the Python Execution Plugin.
Update the workflow configuration with the required plugin parameters, corrected column mappings, and proper environment variable paths, then save the workflow.
Re-trigger the updated workflow execution on the assigned agent and monitor execution through completion.
Manually terminate the hung agent execution process, clear the blocked queue, and escalate unresolved bot engine defects or platform error-reporting limitations to product engineering.

5a5e4831-af8b-4897-803a-f113bfb2530b.title: DocEdge User Onboarding and Documentation Gaps
steps: Identify whether the user request requires documentation assistance, system plugin enablement, or licensing assignment.

Provide all available technical documentation to the user. Inform them that scenario-specific or client-ready guides are not currently available and require submitting a dedicated documentation ticket.
Enable and configure the required DocEdge plugins in the system environment.
Advise the user to submit a separate ticket directly to the License Team for DocEdge license assignment.
Verify with the user that the configured plugins are visible and obtain confirmation that onboarding requirements have been met before closing the ticket.

4a19b766-31ea-4015-bf9d-27d78e84c7d6.title: Planned T4 Instance Upgrade Service Interruption Handling
steps: Verify whether the current outage aligns with a scheduled maintenance window or planned upgrade notification for the AutomationEdge T4 platform.
Monitor the upgrade progress and await completion of the scheduled maintenance window before attempting configuration changes or service restarts.
Perform post-upgrade health checks by logging into the AE Portal and authenticating via Process Studio.
Escalate the incident to the platform engineering team if AE Portal or Process Studio remain unreachable 15 minutes after maintenance completion.

0507e518-931e-42f5-b458-9709310590eb.title: Security Vulnerability Remediation for Outdated Components
steps: Analyze the vulnerability finding to identify whether the affected component is an embedded application dependency or an obsolete standalone service.
Apply the recommended software upgrade package (such as upgrading AutomationEdge to version 8.2.4 containing Log4j version 2.25.4) to replace vulnerable embedded libraries.
Stop and disable the obsolete or unused service (such as an old Tomcat 11.0.14 instance) on the host.
Run a follow-up vulnerability scan or query component versions to confirm the outdated component is no longer active or exposed.

185a29ea-6fdc-468a-9df1-5a936d4b0f9a.title: User Misunderstanding of System Notification Logic
steps: Check the system event and notification logs for the reported transaction to determine whether the event was a true failure or an alternate state such as a diverted case.
Communicate the notification trigger logic to the user, explaining that notifications trigger on explicit failure states rather than diverted or alternate routing flows.
Confirm resolution with the user and close the support ticket.

778aceae-4fa9-46b9-917f-386535249bd3.title: Restoring Misplaced Credential in Vault
steps: Search all alternative credential pools and storage groups across the credential vault for the missing credential name or identifier.
Move the misplaced credential entry from its current pool back to the original expected credential pool.
Trigger the dependent workflow or service to verify successful retrieval of the credential and execution without errors.

bbc06403-88d2-47ae-90dd-1ba4cde729ee.title: Bot Web Element Interaction Failure After Workflow Changes
steps: Open the workflow execution logs and editor. Identify the specific step where the bot fails to interact with the web element, checking for hardcoded 'Delay Row' steps, static timeouts, and rigid or static XPath selectors.
Export a backup of the current bot workflow definition before making any modifications.
Remove redundant or unnecessary 'Delay Row' steps and arbitrary static sleep timeouts preceding the target web element action.
Update the web element identifier to use dynamic XPath logic that adapts to runtime DOM structure changes instead of relying on brittle absolute or static paths.
Configure explicit 'Wait Until' conditions and dynamic Click actions for the target element rather than relying on fixed execution timers.
Run an end-to-end test execution of the updated bot workflow across all target UI scenarios.

f9be1bd3-9331-43ce-a130-b5c7f1e217fd.title: AutomationEdge License Expiration, Extension, and Renewal Management
