steps: Identify the affected AutomationEdge instance identifier (e.g., T3/T4 instance number, server host identifier) and record the current license expiration date, target version, and required components (such as Process Studio or step units).
Submit a license extension or generation request to the license management team with the instance identifier, target expiration duration (e.g., one-year renewal), and relevant version details.
Apply the new license file to the target AutomationEdge environment or client component (such as Process Studio) following the standard upload instructions provided with the license release.
Validate the instance status in the AutomationEdge administration console to confirm the updated expiration date and verify that core services and workflows run without licensing warnings.

df2adb39-c032-47a9-9e4b-ef6b2b9a0999.title: Vulnerability Remediation via Component Upgrade and License Update
steps: Check host operating system compatibility and identify whether server prerequisites permit a full platform upgrade or require a targeted component-level upgrade (Tomcat, ActiveMQ, JDK).
Back up existing AutomationEdge configuration files, component directories (Tomcat, ActiveMQ, JDK paths), and existing license keys before making changes.

If OS prerequisites restrict a full platform upgrade, perform targeted component upgrades by replacing vulnerable Tomcat libraries, ActiveMQ packages, and JDK binaries in non-production and production environments.
If performing a full platform upgrade, upgrade to AutomationEdge version 8.0.2 or above, which includes Bootstrap 5.3.3 and updated dependencies.
Gather required licensing details, obtain the new license key corresponding to the upgraded version or components, and apply the license to the AutomationEdge instance.

Verify the installation: if a platform upgrade was performed, verify that the AE application version is 8.0.2 or higher and check the Bootstrap version in the browser via Developer Tools → Sources / Network; confirm that Tomcat and ActiveMQ services start and operate normally.

fe8d3641-a0b0-4954-ac83-baf21e610614.title: Process Studio Registration and Connectivity Failure
steps: Verify network connectivity and firewall access from the host machine to the Automation Engine (AE) server, T4 server, and Copilot API endpoints.

Check the proxy settings on the host and server. Verify whether the proxy protocol is set to HTTP instead of HTTPS, and verify whether NTLM authentication details (domain and credentials) are present if required by the proxy.
Update the proxy configuration with the correct protocol and NTLM credentials, or add required firewall exceptions for the Process Studio and server hosts.
Check the Process Studio license status, user assignment, and API token quotas.
Unassign the corrupted license from the server management console, deregister the existing Process Studio instance, and complete re-registration using fresh credentials.
Launch Process Studio, trigger a Copilot plugin sync, and execute a test API call to confirm full functionality.

c863906d-ada1-4468-9d47-c085e1eb7193.title: Automation Edge Version Upgrade Management
steps: Review the upgrade documentation and prepare the environment-specific upgrade execution plan for the target Automation Edge release.
Back up the Automation Edge database, configuration files, and take a virtual machine snapshot of the server host before modifying files.
Execute the upgrade procedure in the Development and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environments.
Apply the Automation Edge platform upgrade to the production environment.
Adjust the Automation Edge agent Java Virtual Machine (JVM) memory allocation setting to 12 GB.
Start all Automation Edge services and agents, then verify platform component health and ensure no Java heap space errors appear in logs.

a0f8b359-f3cc-4487-9bc8-29e29594ea66.title: Process Stuck in Execution Started Remediation
steps: Identify the specific request or process stuck in 'Execution Started' in the management console and verify that standard termination commands have failed to stop it.
Restart the execution agent service responsible for processing the stuck request.
Check the management console to verify that the stuck process has transitioned to 'Terminated' state.
Inspect the ActiveMQ broker queue depth and memory usage to determine whether messages have accumulated beyond broker capacity and delivery has stalled.
Purge stuck messages from the saturated ActiveMQ queue.
Update stale database entries associated with the stalled workflow requests to a cleared or failed state.
Restart the ActiveMQ service and dependent application services.
To prevent recurring queue saturation under load, update <ActiveMQ_Install_Dir>\bin\win64\wrapper.conf to set wrapper.java.maxmemory=2048, then restart the ActiveMQ service.

1f3497bf-dad7-4bc3-a6a8-42f39cf34e37.title: External Service Connection Failure Due to Outdated Plugin or Library
steps: Inspect the application error logs to identify the specific failure mode: determine if the failure is an authentication/permission rejection (such as AccessDenied or blocked key-based auth) or a runtime library restriction (such as com.jcraft.jsch.ChannelSftp security restrictions).

If connecting to AWS S3, verify compliance requirements for authentication. If key-based access is blocked, switch to role-based access and update bucket policies to grant required target bucket permissions without requiring s3:ListAllMyBuckets.
Upgrade the Amazon S3 bucket plugin to version 4.2 or higher to ensure compatibility with role-based authentication and updated API endpoints.
If connecting to SFTP and encountering connection failures with the standard plugin, update the SFTP plugin JAR and the underlying JSch library version to the latest release.

If Java security restrictions block direct use of com.jcraft.jsch.ChannelSftp and the Get Files with SecureFTP plugin performance is too slow for batch file downloads, implement the transfer using the Inject JavaScript plugin workaround.
Perform an end-to-end connection and file transfer test against the target external service (S3 or SFTP) and verify success in the application logs.

aac9db70-8d78-436c-b154-83cb349d88b1.title: Plugin Functionality Failure Awaiting Version Update
steps: Inspect the execution logs and error messages for 'ProcessStudioException' or 'Error 400' when configuring or running the affected plugin.
Verify if the issue is a known defect targeting the upcoming plugin release (such as version 4.7) and verify if temporary JAR hotfixes have failed to resolve the behavior.
Provide the requester with the upcoming version details and the tentative target release schedule.
Link the incident to the product release tracking item and set the ticket status per team operational preference pending version deployment.

d7bc749b-e2fe-41b2-a3f4-d2164fd06e9e.title: Handling Sensitive Data Exposure and Decryption Issues in Process Studio
steps: Identify whether the issue is data exposure in execution logs/previews or a decryption failure during workflow processing.
For log exposure issues: Temporarily remove sensitive fields from 'Write to Log' steps and disable 'Capture Row Data on Workflow Failure' for steps handling sensitive parameters.
For preview exposure issues: Configure the sensitive field or parameter with the 'Credentials' parameter type in Process Studio.
For file decryption issues: Use the 'User Defined Java Class' plugin in the workflow and verify that the configured passphrase matches the encryption key exactly.
Verify the AutomationEdge / Process Studio version. If affected by the logging regression, plan an upgrade to version 8.5.0 or later.

ef31561d-f32c-4cf1-9a76-ef9bd4f152e0.title: API Workflow Failure Due to Incorrect Query Parameter Encoding
steps: Capture the full failing API request payload, including the request URL, query string, and HTTP headers. Check whether the query string contains encoded space characters ('%20') or malformed query syntax, and verify that the authentication token is present in the headers.
If the request fails with a credential or token error, reconfigure the client call to pass the active authentication token in the expected header format.
Remove '%20' URL encodings from the query parameters or adjust query parameter syntax to match the endpoint's expected parameter structure.
Execute the modified API workflow request in a test or lower environment to verify successful execution and parameter interpretation.

21fdd065-fb50-4a0e-95d1-a4d623b659bf.title: Advanced REST Client SSL Handshake Failure Due to TLS Version Incompatibility
steps: Send a test request to the target REST API URL using an external API tool such as Postman to confirm the endpoint is reachable and to check the required TLS version.
Inspect the AutomationEdge Process Studio execution logs for the failing step to distinguish between URL encoding syntax errors and SSL/TLS handshake failures.
Evaluate whether the target server requires TLS 1.3 and whether the Advanced REST Client plugin is unable to establish the handshake.
Implement a custom Java snippet or script step within the workflow to execute the HTTPS request directly using a modern Java HTTP client configured with TLS 1.3 support.
Open a vendor support ticket with AutomationEdge requesting native TLS 1.3 cipher suite support for the Advanced REST Client plugin, providing the test results and reproduction workflow.

e8dcf74b-91c4-4e47-8b21-8575a632728e.title: Web Automation Plugin Inaccuracies Requiring Custom Scripting
steps: Export and save a backup copy of the current web automation workflow before editing any step configurations or replacing plugins.
Inspect the failing automation step and execution logs to determine whether the issue is an unhandled alert race condition or an inaccurate element state evaluation caused by dynamic page rendering.
Replace or bypass the standard Web Alert plugin step with an injected JavaScript script that directly targets, intercepts, or dismisses the browser alert dialog during asynchronous loading.

Replace the Web Element Condition plugin with more granular validation steps: implement 'Web Until' for explicit wait states, extract the raw value using 'GetText', or inject custom JavaScript to query DOM properties only after asynchronous loading completes.
Execute the modified automation workflow across multiple test runs in the User Acceptance Testing environment to confirm that dynamic elements and alerts resolve reliably.

9cf651e2-c846-4fb3-adfa-d53abeea439f.title: Java Application SSL/TLS Certificate Trust Store Misconfiguration
steps: Identify the exact Java runtime instance and path used by the failing application or service, and verify the configured version using 'java -version'.
Obtain the required SSL/TLS certificate file (e.g., .cer, .crt, or intermediate/root certificates) from your IT team or the target service.
Create a backup copy of the target 'cacerts' file prior to modification (located at '<JAVA_HOME>/jre/lib/security/cacerts' or '<JAVA_HOME>/lib/security/cacerts').

Open a command prompt as Administrator, navigate to the active JDK/JRE bin path (e.g., 'C:\Program Files\Java\jdk1.8.0_91\bin'), and import the certificate into the active cacerts keystore using keytool:
keytool -importcert -file "D:\SSL-Certificate\filename.cer" -alias randomaliasname -keystore JAVA_HOME/jre/lib/security/cacerts -storepass changeit
(Alternatively: keytool -import -trustcacerts -file "<your_certificate_path>" -alias <alias_name> -keystore "<java_home_path>\lib\security\cacerts")
Restart the application or agent service and verify that the SSL/TLS connection succeeds without PKIX validation errors.

aa1c01a1-6ed5-4788-a42f-7e7290b62cf4.title: Agent Startup and Functioning Failures Due to Environmental or Configuration Mismatches
steps: Inspect the agent logs for registration exceptions such as com.automationedge.aeagent.exceptions.AgentRegistrationFailed: Agent Registration Failed, and verify that the agent process is being launched from its correct root installation directory rather than a secondary or temporary folder.
Check available disk space on the agent host and server partitions, and verify that the agent process has read/write permissions to its working directories.

Verify the operating system user account executing the agent. Ensure the agent is started under the specific user account with which it was originally registered, rather than an admin or alternative user account.
Check whether the agent host IP address is permitted and whitelisted in the server-side access control list.
Check the current MAC address on the agent host network interface and verify that it matches the MAC address tied to the active agent license.

If the agent fails during script execution (such as Python) or file handling, inspect the system PATH environment variables and verify shared folder path syntax, ensuring consistent escape sequences and network accessibility.
Check the account status in the management portal to verify that on-demand accounts or agent service accounts have not been set to dormant due to inactivity.
Start the agent service using startup.bat or the designated service runner, and verify in the management console that the agent reaches an online and idle state.

7d149176-a9c6-47c5-ae11-a0e096d8272a.title: Application Unavailability Due to Database Connection Exhaustion and JDBC Connection Failures
steps: Check database connection metrics and limits by running `SHOW max_connections;` and querying `pg_stat_activity` on the PostgreSQL server, then inspect application pool utilization.
Check application and database logs for `org.postgresql.core.v3.ConnectionFactoryImpl.enableSSL`. Run `SHOW ssl;` in PostgreSQL and inspect `pg_hba.conf` for host connection rules.
If connection exhaustion is confirmed (100% pool utilization), increase the application connection pool size to 200 and ensure PostgreSQL `SHOW max_connections;` accommodates the increased pool size.
Restart the Tomcat service to apply the updated connection pool settings.

If `SHOW ssl;` returns `off` and `ConnectionFactoryImpl.enableSSL` errors are present, update the JDBC connection URL to: `jdbc:postgresql://<servername>/<database_name>?currentSchema=public&sslmode=disable`. Do not set `sslmode=disable` if PostgreSQL SSL is enabled or organizational security requires encryption.
Execute workflows and access the Automation Edge Production Console to verify connection stability and confirm zero `ConnectionFactoryImpl.enableSSL` errors in logs.

6fcbddd1-c994-4dcb-99f4-29bd51f03c6e.title: Email Server Connectivity Failure During Configuration
steps: Review and verify the entered email server configuration details, including server hostname/IP address, protocol (SMTP, IMAP, or POP3), port number, security settings (SSL, TLS, STARTTLS), and authentication credentials.
Test network reachability from the application host to the email server on the configured port to verify there are no firewall blocks or DNS resolution failures.
Request verified mail server parameters and network access confirmation from the customer or mail administrator, then place the troubleshooting ticket on hold pending their updates.

5887c172-048e-480d-abfb-fdd2a807b8ee.title: Copilot API 403 Errors Due to Missing Token Quota
steps: Inspect the Copilot error logs and response payload to determine whether the 403 Forbidden error is caused by missing token quotas, credential validation failure, or file/endpoint permission denial.
If credential validation failed, perform a plugin synchronization or re-register the Copilot plugin.
If the error is permission-related on a specific resource, verify that the user is referencing the correct file and has necessary access rights for the AI platform endpoint.
If the 403 error is caused by missing or undefined token quotas, escalate the ticket to the API team to configure and assign the required token limits.
Execute a test prompt in Copilot to verify that prompt execution succeeds without returning a 403 Forbidden error.

b00568dd-2770-473a-bbe4-cc43ae8f47f7.title: RPA Agent Stability: JVM Metaspace and Memory Remediation
steps: Inspect the agent execution logs for the error message 'java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace' and confirmation of shutdown via 'Shutdown reason: OutOfMemoryError - Metaspace'.
Log in to the AutomationEdge UI, navigate to the agent configuration settings, and remove the explicit Metaspace tag/parameter configured for the affected agent.
Restart the RPA agent service and monitor thread status and system usage under standard workflow execution volume.
If the agent encounters secondary failures during task execution, check for Python plugin library incompatibilities, expired authentication tokens, and bot download path access.

49284dae-2541-4cdf-a8de-36d3cdd2881b.title: Database Schema Initialization Conflict During Application Upgrade
steps: Inspect the application startup logs (such as the Catalina and Spring application logs) for Liquibase errors, schema creation exceptions, or connection timeouts.
Take a complete snapshot or backup of the application database before performing manual schema modifications.
Connect to the database and manually drop the orphaned sequence 'usergroup_id_seq' created during the partial Liquibase execution.
Restart the application server to allow Liquibase to re-run the initialization schema scripts.
Log in to the web portal using administrative credentials to verify end-to-end service functionality.

95030882-0726-4e73-8c51-07ffac88ca80.title: Premature Application Session Expiration
steps: Identify the exact trigger condition and user action immediately preceding the session termination (e.g., page refresh, long-running form edit without submission, or immediate logout upon login).

If the logout occurred after a browser refresh, verify if the application token is lost. Explain to the user that in AutomationEdge token-based authentication, refreshing the browser page clears the session token and invalidates the session by design for security.
If the logout occurred during long form editing or role configuration in the UI, check the configured session timeout period against the time spent without backend API calls.
If the session expires immediately upon login or on every API call, inspect the session token validation parameters and salted hashing configuration for login time validation.
Update the session timeout configuration to align with business workflow duration, or correct the salted hashing validation settings causing instant expiry.
Have the user log into AEUI and execute their standard workflow to verify that the session persists throughout active use without premature termination.

15a07170-a9b1-484d-b744-d89ab6af0884.title: T3 Server Post-Migration UI Validation: Task Template and Document Metadata Tabs
steps: Log in to the T3 server administrative interface and verify whether the Document Metadata tab, Document Templates tab, and Task Template creation option are visible.
Verify user role assignments and feature license flags for the T3 server instance to confirm the account has permissions to view metadata tabs and create task templates.
If permissions and license modules are active but the tabs remain missing, collect application server logs and escalate to the application engineering team for post-migration schema and cache review.

ab9dd6f4-b505-4133-8d80-39f3a47c16a0.title: ActiveMQ Client Connection Instability and Failover Recovery
steps: Inspect the file <AE_HOME>\ae.properties and check the activemq.broker.url configuration.
Verify that no orphan processes are holding the ActiveMQ transport port (such as 61616 or 61614) on the secondary/slave host to ensure only one ActiveMQ instance attempts to bind the port.
Create a backup copy of <AE_HOME>\ae.properties prior to making modifications.

Edit <AE_HOME>\ae.properties to configure the failover broker URL with reconnect parameters: activemq.broker.url=failover:(tcp://<machine1-IP/Hostname>:<port>,tcp://<machine2-IP/Hostname>:<port>)?maxReconnectAttempts=10 (include warnAfterReconnectAttempts if tracking reconnect attempts).
Restart services in the required order: run 'net stop AutomationEdge', run 'net stop ActiveMQ', run 'net start ActiveMQ', and then run 'net start AutomationEdge'.
Verify AutomationEdge logs to confirm a successful broker connection and verify that the AutomationEdge web interface is accessible.

5f8efcc9-552e-41b4-97f0-64f105f54eec.title: Remediation of Version Mismatch During Software Patch Upgrade
steps: Check the currently deployed application version across all running instances and compare it against the target change specification.
Locate and verify the required target patch package and web application archive (WAR file) in the deployment repository.
Stop the application service and deploy the verified target patch artifact to replace the mismatched build.
Start the application service and verify that the system reports the target patch version.

adeb8109-26cb-4445-87e6-37a9f7a68ffc.title: Process/Workflow Stuck During Database-Related Plugin Update
steps: Inspect workflow execution logs and database activity to determine the cause of the stall. Check if logs report 'org.postgresql.core.v3.ConnectionFactoryImpl.enableSSL' with 'java.net.SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out', check for active locks in pg_stat_activity and 'SHOW max_connections;', or determine if the step hangs after processing rows.
Export or create a backup copy of the existing workflow definition in Process Studio before making configuration or connection changes.
If the issue is caused by SSL negotiation on a non-SSL PostgreSQL database, update the JDBC connection string to: jdbc:postgresql://<servername>/<database_name>?currentSchema=public&sslmode=disable
If the workflow stalls during database update operations due to query timeouts, configure an explicit query timeout threshold in the database update plugin settings within the workflow.

If the workflow hangs on 'Block This Step Until Finish' (such as after a Filter Rows step), open the workflow in Process Studio, double-click the canvas to open Workflow Properties, and increase the Rowset Size from the default 10,000 to a value higher than the total number of rows being processed.
Execute the workflow via the Agent or Process Studio and verify that execution completes successfully without connection drops, timeouts, or stalls.

b93624cb-f5a0-4b58-a259-f930c18e0b1d.title: Post-Deployment UI Asset Configuration Drift Remediation
steps: Check if the custom logo file exists in <Tomcat home>/webapps/aeui/assets/images and verify that its extension is one of .jpg, .png, .svg, or .gif.
Add or copy the customer logo file under directory <Tomcat home>/webapps/aeui/assets/images. Supported file types are .jpg, .png, .svg, and .gif.
Update the property tenantLogoFile with the file name added in the previous step (for example, tenantLogoFile = customer-logo.png) in the UI application configuration settings.
Open the login page in a browser (use a private/incognito window to bypass cached assets) and verify that the custom logo renders properly.

6b45e601-9e80-4034-991c-582281066a9e.title: Handling Audit Log Purging Inefficiency for Historical Data
steps: Inspect the audit log table to identify the age of lingering records and verify if unpurged rows have Tenant_ID set to NULL.
Inform the client or requesting team that the automated purge mechanism intentionally operates in bounded time windows across multiple cycles to protect database performance.
If immediate historical cleanup is required, obtain engineering approval and execute an authorized direct SQL purge query in batches during a scheduled maintenance window.

0d578dba-aaa6-490a-b910-50ae8db9e90a.title: User-Requested Software Component and License Provisioning
steps: Review the customer ticket to identify the exact software components, version requirements (such as AE 8.2.5 setup files), required driver/JAR plugins, or license types requested.
Verify customer support entitlements and target environment compatibility before distributing software binaries or generating license keys.
Retrieve or generate the verified artifacts, including specific installer setup packages, driver JAR files, plugin bundles, or license activation keys from approved repositories.

Upload the staged setup files, drivers, or plugins to the customer's designated SFTP repository or deliver them using authenticated download links. Send license keys securely according to provisioning standards.
Confirm with the customer that download access is functional, software/licenses are successfully applied, and identify if any secondary dependencies or pending plugins remain unfulfilled.

846bebd3-d4eb-48cb-94d7-41a98c9ac908.title: API Response JSON Parsing and Path Extraction Troubleshooting
steps: Inspect the raw API response payload to identify the exact JSON structure, noting all nested objects, arrays, and field naming conventions.
Compare the configured JSON path expression against the raw JSON schema, specifically checking array indices, field names, and nested parent keys.
Determine if the JSON parsing issue can be resolved via standard JSON path syntax corrections or if it involves complex nested structures/inconsistent formatting requiring custom scripting.
Update the JSON path expression in the JSON input plugin configuration to match the exact array and key structure of the API response payload.
Implement custom JavaScript parsing logic in the transformation step to normalize inconsistent or deeply nested structures before downstream processing.
Run a test execution of the pipeline with sample API responses to confirm target fields are extracted and downstream steps (such as Split_To_Rows) execute successfully.

915507e2-97e1-435f-8fba-c16714d096fd.title: Process Studio Concurrent Resource Contention and Port Bind Error Resolution
steps: Identify which process is holding the conflicted local port (such as SSO callback port 2611 or the Process Studio instance port) using OS network utility tools.
Terminate the running process holding the conflicted port to free the resource.
If Process Studio files or runtime are corrupted, deploy a fresh Process Studio ZIP archive and ensure the bundled Java folder is present in the installation directory.
If the failure occurs during Azure Active Directory SSO login, verify that 'http://localhost:2611/' is registered under Redirect URIs / Reply URLs in the Azure Portal App Registration.
Launch Process Studio, perform user login, and trigger a plugin sync to confirm normal operation.

0bee3a88-3858-46ac-9c10-21de72aacf15.title: TOTP Generator Plugin: Version Compatibility and External Authentication Dependencies
steps: Check the installed AutomationEdge platform version.
Upgrade the AutomationEdge platform instance to version 8.x.
Provision the Authenticator: TOTP Generator plugin in AutomationEdge and verify that it generates one-time passwords.
If login fails while TOTP generation works properly, inspect the user account state in Active Directory (AD) or the external identity provider for lockouts, expiration, or permission errors.

90890222-df2c-4d32-a016-7cda5feb7315.title: AutomationEdge Process Studio JDBC Driver Configuration
steps: Close Process Studio and stop the AutomationEdge Agent if either is currently running.

Identify the target database engine and version, and obtain the matching JDBC connector JAR file (for example, 'mariaDB-java-client-3.5.3.jar' for MariaDB 10.3.39 or 'mysql-connector-java-5.1.49.jar' for MySQL/SQLyog).
Copy the downloaded JDBC driver JAR file into the Process Studio library directory at '<ProcessStudio-RootFolder>\lib' or '<ProcessStudio-RootFolder>\lib_ext', replacing any outdated driver JARs.
Determine if workflows connecting to this database will be executed via an AutomationEdge Agent or AutomationEdge Server engine.
If executing via an AutomationEdge Agent, copy the JDBC driver JAR file into '<ae-agent-RootFolder>\lib_ext' (for example, 'D:\AE_Agent\ae-agent\lib_ext').

If configuring AutomationEdge Server / Engine, navigate to 'tools\apache-tomcat-11.0.6\webapps\aeengine\WEB-INF\lib', place the correct database driver JAR there, remove any unused or conflicting drivers, and restart AutomationEdge services.
Launch Process Studio, open the database connection configuration wizard, enter the host, port, database name, and credentials, and click Test Connection.

aef365fb-7dfb-42bc-831f-defa7d7a343c.title: Process Studio SSO/MFA Authentication Failure Resolution
steps: Inspect the Process Studio authentication logs and the error prompt on screen. Confirm the local callback server started with message 'SSO Callback server started on port 2611' and verify if error 'AADSTS50011' or 'Authentication : HTTP Status - 400' occurs.
Determine the Identity Provider configured for Process Studio SSO (Azure Active Directory vs ADFS).

For Azure AD: Log in to the Azure Portal. Navigate to Azure Active Directory → App Registrations. Open the Process Studio application registration, go to Authentication, and under Redirect URIs / Reply URLs, add 'http://localhost:2611/' (or 'http://localhost:2611/callback' if required by the exact error payload). Save the configuration.
For ADFS: Open the ADFS Management console, locate the relying party trust for Process Studio, and add 'http://localhost:2611/callback' to the Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) / Reply URL settings.

Verify that local firewall rules or proxy configurations on the client workstation do not block connections to localhost on port 2611, and clear the local browser cache/session data if persistent session tokens exist.
Restart Process Studio and retry the SSO login flow.

695e9404-16e6-4837-9ab2-f75e684d7e5a.title: PS Plugin Synchronization Failure Due to Outdated Configuration
steps: Create a backup copy of the configuration file at OnDemand\process-studio\.process-studio\.psrc before modifying it.
Open OnDemand\process-studio\.process-studio\.psrc in a text editor and update the PsLastUpdated configuration value.
Initiate the Process Studio plugin synchronization.
Confirm that the Process Studio plugin synchronization completes successfully.

c08785d2-18e5-439f-92ad-bf5c6e25f9f8.title: Workflow Not Visible or Assignable Due to Configuration, Publication State, or Queue Saturation
steps: Check the workflow definition, internal assignment target, and publication state in the workflow management console to verify whether it is assigned to the correct agent type or stuck in an unpromoted state.
Correct the internal workflow assignment target to the intended agent role, apply configuration updates, and republish the workflow.
Check ActiveMQ broker memory utilization and queue message accumulation to determine if queues have exceeded memory thresholds and stalled silent delivery.
Purge stuck messages from the saturated ActiveMQ queue, update any stale database entries, and restart the ActiveMQ and application services.

Update the queue memory configuration in activemq.xml to prevent memory saturation: 
<policyEntry queue=">" producerFlowControl="true" memoryLimit="200mb" maxPageSize="2000"/>
After modifying activemq.xml, restart the ActiveMQ service.
Verify that agents receive new workflow assignments and that workflow items are visible in the agent interface.

4d2e8e79-5d8b-4621-8f6c-af52e9cd4482.title: Workflow Execution Logging and Monitoring Visibility Issues
steps: Inspect the downloaded log archive to check if log files are double-zipped. If the log file shows 0KB or cannot be opened, fully extract the outer zip archive and then extract any nested archive found inside.
Inspect the workflow definition for any explicit 'abort step' or termination nodes that halt execution prematurely. Remove or modify the abort step if it prevents log and metrics generation.

Check the workflow execution history for upstream errors, such as plugin download failures or agent connectivity issues. Verify whether downstream steps skipped execution due to expected error-handling behavior.
Enable debug logging and step metrics logging for the affected workflow execution, then trigger a new run to capture detailed execution traces.
Collect the generated debug logs, workflow definition, and environment details, then escalate the issue to the engineering team for plugin or runtime investigation.

81741e61-e947-4630-a7df-b630174682df.title: Automation Edge Service Termination Due to RDP Session Timeout and GPO
steps: Log into the affected server and check if the Automation Edge Agent and Nginx processes are currently running in Task Manager or via command line.
Check if the processes were launched interactively inside a user RDP command prompt session rather than configured as background Windows services.
Inspect the local and domain Group Policy settings for session timeouts, specifically 'Set time limit for disconnected sessions', and check for interactive logon legal notice policies.
Submit a request to the domain or system administrators to apply a GPO exception for the RPA server, disabling the disconnected session timeout and removing interactive logon prompts.

Restart the Automation Edge Agent and Nginx processes, disconnect the RDP session (do not log off), and verify via remote monitoring or scheduled task execution that the processes remain active past the standard timeout threshold.

d5dece56-5b8c-4edf-b3da-f1a0b08d4b63.title: Security Vulnerability Remediation Workflow
steps: Review the AppSec/VAPT report findings and categorize each item into application-level vulnerabilities, database/third-party software vulnerabilities, and OS/network-level configurations.

For infrastructure, database, or cryptographic findings (such as PostgreSQL version updates, SSL/TLS configuration, and weak ciphers), prepare specific configuration guidelines and provide remediation steps to the customer.

For application-level findings (such as Angular dependencies, Reflected XSS, or core logic issues), determine if resolution requires an application patch or version upgrade (e.g., AutomationEdge version 8.2.5).
Compare the client's mandatory remediation deadline against the official release date of the required target version.
Open a dedicated upgrade tracking ticket for the scheduled version upgrade, confirm closure acceptance for resolved individual items with the client, and close the original VAPT triage ticket.

57aefd6a-8689-4c02-b043-bf72faeac4e7.title: Incident Resolution Stalled by Client Unresponsiveness
steps: Review the ticket history to confirm that all technical requests, required actions, or questions have been clearly communicated to the client and remain unanswered.
Send a follow-up notification to the client stating that the incident cannot proceed without their response, and inform them of pending closure if no update is received.
Close the ticket with notes recording that resolution was halted due to client unresponsiveness, and invite the client to reopen or submit a new request when ready.

37993d8f-3e64-4477-ab1c-76724135afd5.title: ServiceNow Plugin Incompatibility Post-Platform Upgrade
steps: Check the installed ServiceNow plugin version and review the AE Agent execution logs for 'failed to respond' error messages.
Run the failing ServiceNow workflow step directly inside Process Studio to determine if the issue is isolated to AE Agent runtime execution.
Contact the AutomationEdge Support team to request the latest compatible ServiceNow plugin JAR file (version 4.5 or newer hotfix).
Upload and deploy the new ServiceNow plugin JAR file to the AutomationEdge platform.
Trigger a test workflow execution containing ServiceNow steps on an AE Agent to confirm the job completes without 'failed to respond' errors.

336bdfe6-7c80-4f41-815e-9513257b09f2.title: LDAP/LDAPS Integration and Certificate Configuration Failures
steps: Back up the existing Java truststore (cacerts) and current LDAP integration configuration files before making modifications.
Verify the LDAP endpoint configuration to confirm whether LDAPS (port 636) is required, and ensure the configuration uses the Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) rather than an IP address.
Inspect the SSL/TLS certificate received from the LDAP directory server to check if the full chain is present, specifically identifying any missing Intermediate CA or Root CA certificates.
Import the Root CA and Intermediate CA certificates into the application Java truststore (cacerts).
Update the application LDAP configuration to enable LDAPS protocol (ldaps://<FQDN>:636) with secure authentication and integrity checking.
Test LDAP authentication and user search functionality from the application interface or verification utility.

760aa36b-0264-4d39-8a5f-bde16ad52f90.title: Office 365 Plugin Authentication Failure (Refresh Token)
steps: Inspect the application and plugin authentication logs to capture the exact OAuth 2.0 error code and message, specifically checking for 'invalid_grant' or 'AADSTS9002313'.

Open the Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) portal, navigate to App Registrations for the Office 365 send mail plugin, and verify that the configured 'redirect_uri' matches the exact URI expected by the plugin client.

Verify the OAuth grant_type and requested API permissions (scopes) in both the Azure AD App Registration and the plugin configuration to ensure offline access and mail sending permissions are granted.
Trigger a test email send via the plugin to confirm that the refresh token is successfully generated and stored.
Escalate the issue to the Identity and Access Management (IAM) / Azure AD administrator team for advanced tenant-level OAuth policy and token configuration analysis.

0e1d957f-6af9-4ca5-b31f-8a818d184068.title: API Workflow JSON Path Mismatch Due to Array Parsing
steps: Send the failing API request directly via Postman using the same parameters, headers, and payload configured in the workflow engine.
Inspect the raw JSON response body in Postman to verify if bulk execution is supported and if the returned data structure matches the expected JSON array schema.

If the API returns unexpected response formats or fails to support bulk execution in Postman, advise the API provider or client development team to resolve the API endpoint behavior before reconfiguring workflow parsers.

6ae9999a-d148-4425-b747-4dfa27b5ed1e.title: Unexpected Data Modification in Parent Workflow from Child Workflow Due to Pass-by-Reference Semantics
steps: Inspect the parent workflow step that executes the child workflow and identify all variables and row datasets passed as input parameters.
Examine the child workflow steps to identify whether incoming input rows or variables are modified in-place during processing.
Update the child workflow to initialize a secondary local variable and copy the input row values into it before applying any transformations or mutations.
Execute a test run of the parent workflow and inspect the parent dataset immediately following child workflow completion.

bb404094-09f1-43fb-b3a5-c6843b166ff2.title: Browser Automation Failure Due to Environmental Security Policies
steps: Check whether the automation script runs Microsoft Edge in Internet Explorer (IE) mode inside a disconnected Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) session.
Keep the RDP session active during execution or configure an interactive desktop session rather than running in a disconnected state.

Inspect Windows Event logs, Group Policy (GPO) audit logs, and endpoint protection software (AppLocker, WDAC, or Antivirus) to verify if child process spawning for msedge.exe or its driver is blocked.
Escalate the identified policy blocks and log findings to the host IT or security administration team to request appropriate execution permissions or security exemptions for the automation binary.

79d815ae-a3e7-4167-94a4-8d562e61549a.title: Unsupported Direct Database Migration: DocEdge to AEUI
steps: Review the customer ticket to confirm the exact target environment: determine whether they are requesting to restore a backup into the legacy DocEdge UI or attempting to migrate database records into AEUI.

If the customer intends to migrate data into AEUI, notify them that direct database restoration from DocEdge to AEUI is unsupported due to schema differences, and guide them to recreate their assets manually within AEUI.
If the customer is restoring a backup within the legacy DocEdge environment, route the ticket to the legacy system administration queue or provide standard DocEdge database restore documentation.

7b282cce-26d7-4c83-a534-516d986b5983.title: Duplicate Agent Registration Conflict Resolution
steps: Inspect the T3 server registration records and client agent logs to identify if a pre-existing registration shares the same username and hostname.
Update the machine username on the client host to create a distinct identity that does not match the existing registration.
Restart the client machine to apply the updated user settings and clear any lingering registration session state.
Launch the agent and perform a test registration against the T3 server.

17d0c7d2-b278-4175-8284-7dcbeb5ce26d.title: Blocked Upgrade Due to Critical File Download Issues
steps: Identify the exact file that failed to download and determine the root cause of the download blockage (for example: expired link, customer firewall restriction, or proxy block).

Check if an alternative bypass asset—such as an updated User Acceptance Testing (UAT) or production license file—can fulfill the upgrade requirement without downloading the restricted utility package.
Back up existing configuration files, current license keys, and database state before applying new upgrade packages or license updates.
Generate and provide the required replacement asset (such as an updated UAT license file or refreshed direct download link) to the customer through an approved secure channel.
Upload the provided license file or utility package into the AutomationEdge environment following the version upgrade instructions.
Verify that the AutomationEdge upgrade and migration process resumes and completes without download errors.

bbc28425-1474-4fc5-a85b-2fd3a8a854c3.title: Process Studio and Plugin Connectivity, Synchronization, and Registration Troubleshooting
steps: Verify network access and proxy settings from the host machine or VDI to the AutomationEdge server endpoints (such as port 443 connectivity) to ensure firewall or SSL inspection devices are not resetting connections or returning 403 Forbidden responses.
Open the Process Studio application, navigate to the Tools menu, and select 'sync plugins'. Enter the username and password in the AutomationEdge connection details window, then click Connect.
Open the target .psw workflow file in Process Studio to verify that all required plugins and steps load without error.

Close the Process Studio application completely. Navigate to the Process Studio installation directory. Delete the 'psplugins' and '.process-studio' folders. Then, launch the application by running the 'process-studio.bat' file from the directory.
If automatic server synchronization is prevented by strict environment security policies, manually copy the required plugin directories directly into the Process Studio plugins folder.

If connectivity, token issuance, or download issues persist, escalate to the internal IT / network security team to inspect proxy token consistency, client IP mismatch, and complete necessary URL whitelisting.

4da6f913-5dbb-4fd2-9c0e-cdf78d749b2c.title: AutomationEdge Agent Instability and Unknown State Remediation
steps: Log in to the agent host machine and open Task Manager. Inspect CPU and memory utilization, and check if excessive java.exe, javaw.exe, Python, or Chrome driver processes are consuming system memory.
Check endpoint security software (such as Cortex XDR) event logs to determine if javaw.exe or any agent binary was blocked or terminated as a false positive.
Verify whether the agent terminal or console session closed automatically after a user logged off or disconnected from RDP.
Open Task Manager and terminate any hung workflow-related processes (such as orphaned java.exe, stuck Python OCR scripts, crashed browser drivers, or unnecessary open application windows).
Restart the AutomationEdge agent service or process on the host machine.
If out-of-memory or high heap utilization caused the failure, increase the maximum Java heap memory allocation in the agent configuration and disable debug mode if active.

Apply persistent environment fixes: request security exception whitelist in XDR policy for javaw.exe if blocked, or coordinate with the IT/infrastructure team to adjust server policy so running tasks do not terminate on RDP disconnect.
Open the AutomationEdge portal and verify that the agent status updates from 'Unknown' to 'Running' and displays green heartbeat status.

7ebff7e7-66ad-465d-b40c-d1a66b3dd3f9.title: Excel Output Plugin Failure Due to Corrupted Output File
steps: Inspect the workflow execution logs to confirm the failure originates from the Excel Output plugin and identify the path of the target Excel file and the specific Java exception (such as NullPointerException or ZipException).
Move the corrupted Excel output file out of the target directory into a quarantine or backup location, or delete it if no backup is needed.
Re-run the failed workflow to generate a fresh Excel output file.
Verify that the workflow run completed successfully and that the generated Excel output file opens correctly without corruption warnings.
Escalate to the engineering or platform team for root-cause investigation if file corruption recurs intermittently across multiple workflow runs.

a1e012cb-0c75-46ec-86ea-bc0cc9c7dc8b.title: Workflow Execution Failure Due to GUI Plugin Version Mismatch
steps: Check and compare the installed GUI Plugin version in the Process Studio authoring environment against the GUI Plugin version on the target execution agent.
Determine if the deployment environment has a lower GUI Plugin version than the authoring environment (such as an agent on pre-4.7 while workflow was edited in 4.7).
Upgrade the GUI Plugin on the target deployment environment agent to match the version used in Process Studio (at least version 4.7).
Re-deploy or open the workflow in the updated deployment environment and execute a test run to confirm GUI actions execute without corruption or initialization failure.

7de5f006-5f4a-4bcc-8fdc-9021b593f645.title: AutomationEdge IDAM API Integration Information and Support
steps: Identify the specific AutomationEdge IDAM API endpoints, authentication requirements, and data exchange formats required by the requester.
Retrieve the current AutomationEdge IDAM API documentation, endpoint URLs, and required connection parameters, then deliver them securely to the requester.
Check whether the target system requires an AutomationEdge plugin update or connector upgrade to support the API integration.
Validate with the requesting team that API calls connect successfully and that authentication completes without errors.

bd0d6a45-9691-4fef-842e-9ad37f84288c.title: Manual Provisioning of Specific Automation Browser Drivers/Extensions
steps: Determine the AutomationEdge deployment type (On-premise vs T3 Instance) and confirm the required browser type and exact version (e.g., ChromeDriver 148, EdgeDriver 148, or Microsoft Edge web extension).

Access the Support portal at https://support.automationedge.com/portal/en/kb/automationedge, select the EPD link under 'Links to better reach section', log in with EPD credentials, accept the agreement, and navigate to the platform downloads section to retrieve the target driver or plugin package.
Inspect the downloaded driver package to verify that the internal folder structure, file names, and archive format match the GUI Automation Plugin specifications before initiating deployment.

Check instance deployment type: if T3 Cloud Instance, trigger the plugin sync interface; if On-premise, log into the instance as sysadmin, navigate to sysadmin > File Management > Select GUI Automation Plugin, and upload the driver package.

If the sysadmin upload button is disabled in the web interface or an offline extension package is required, provide the verified offline driver/extension package directly to the customer and log an internal ticket for backend deployment assistance.

c1ebbaac-9eb2-4fa2-9688-6658679fc491.title: Remediating Agent Instability and Workflow Failures from Java and ActiveMQ Misconfiguration
steps: Inspect running system processes for duplicate OpenJDK instances and verify whether the ActiveMQ service is currently running.
Check the system PATH and environment variables to ensure the Java runtime is recognized correctly by the operating system and agent service.
Back up existing configuration files including activemq.xml, wrapper.conf, and agent startup scripts before making changes.
Stop the agent service, terminate all lingering duplicate OpenJDK processes, and remove obsolete agent startup configurations.
Fix the Java environment paths in the system configuration, then update <ActiveMQ_Install_Dir>\bin\win64\wrapper.conf to set wrapper.java.maxmemory=2048.
Open activemq.xml and configure queue limits: <policyEntry queue=">" producerFlowControl="true" memoryLimit="200mb" maxPageSize="2000"/>
Purge stuck messages from saturated ActiveMQ queues and update any stale database records holding stalled workflow locks.
Start the ActiveMQ service, restart application services, and start the agent service.
Submit a test workflow and verify that the agent receives and executes tasks without triggering queue backlogs or extra OpenJDK processes.

817b4409-3d37-4949-bd10-863ab9157432.title: Chatbot Incomplete Data Retrieval and Message Truncation
steps: Inspect the chatbot response pipeline to determine if the truncation occurs during structured/tabular data extraction in the Knowledge Management system or downstream at the channel delivery layer (such as WhatsApp message size limits).

Apply a workaround for channel message limits by configuring response pagination, splitting large tabular output into smaller messages, or summarizing output before dispatching to the messaging client.
Re-index or restructure the tabular data source in the Knowledge Management system so table parsers can extract complete rows and lists.
Test the target query and obtain confirmation from the reporting user that the complete list and full message body are now delivered correctly.

c640dbd1-f0b5-4b60-ad6d-99f2c963e6bf.title: Post-Upgrade Bot Process Failure Due to Plugin Incompatibility
steps: Check your current AutomationEdge server version and consult the 'Plugin Reference Guide' under the Resource tab on the AutomationEdge portal to determine the matching plugin release version for your platform.
Log in to the AutomationEdge portal with sysadmin credentials and upload the compatible plugin JAR files matching your platform version.
Review failing bot execution logs and agent logs to identify which specific steps or plugin entry points in the workflows are failing.
Open the affected bot process workflows in Process Studio, update the modified plugin steps with the new step parameters, and republish the bot processes to the AutomationEdge portal.
Trigger a test run of the modified bot processes on the assigned agents and confirm normal execution to completion.

85e3d947-d2d5-47cb-ad61-09eb56085686.title: API Usage & Documentation Information Request
steps: Review the request ticket to identify the target internal API (for example, Credential Vault API or Data Source API) and the specific usage details or parameters requested.
Locate and retrieve the relevant API reference documentation, schema definitions, and example payloads for the requested functionality.
Provide the requester with the API specifications, sample requests/responses, and any required integration guidance to resolve their query.

d6d51dfa-053a-430b-a08a-c8b6308a8a59.title: Application File Upload Size Limit Misconfiguration
steps: Inspect the ae.properties file located in the configuration directory (such as AE_HOME/conf/ae.properties) and verify the current values for ae.file.upload.size.limit.in.mb, spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size, and spring.servlet.multipart.max-request-size. Check whether these properties were erroneously placed in application.properties instead of ae.properties.
Create a backup copy of the ae.properties file before making any edits.

Add or update the following properties in the ae.properties file with the target size limits in megabytes:

ae.file.upload.size.limit.in.mb=<Required_Value>
spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size=<Required_Value>MB
spring.servlet.multipart.max-request-size=<Required_Value>MB

Ensure spring.servlet.multipart.max-request-size is set to a higher value than spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size (recommended 50 MB higher). Remove any duplicate spring.servlet.multipart definitions from application.properties if present.
Log in to the AutomationEdge portal, navigate to the file upload section, and upload a file close to the configured size limit.

923aa83c-ebf0-4c4e-9e93-5c137bf4fab8.title: O365 Send Mail Plugin Protocol Information Gap
steps: Review the user inquiry to identify the specific plugin implementation or authentication details needed (such as Microsoft Graph API protocol, Microsoft Entra ID Tenant ID, Client ID, or Client Secret).

Provide the technical specification: clarify that the Office 365 Send Mail plugin communicates via the Microsoft Graph API using OAuth 2.0 / Microsoft Entra ID authentication, requiring Tenant ID, Client ID (Application ID), and Client Secret or Refresh Token.
Confirm with the user that the provided specifications allow them to complete the plugin configuration and perform a test email send.

96629026-578e-47af-a965-2abedf9e5e73.title: Automation Failure Due to Unexpected UI Popup
steps: Identify the action triggering the popup (such as clicking the 'Go' button) and verify whether the popup leaves the parent screen inactive.
Record and insert required automation operations inside the popup window to interact with or dismiss the popup.
Record and insert automation operations to regain focus on the main window and resume execution after the popup is closed.
Run an end-to-end test of the updated automation script across the triggering action, the popup handling, and downstream actions.

da345261-913e-45f9-b0f2-d48719bdbfff.title: GUI Automation Plugin Failure Due to Incorrect or Incompatible JAR Version
steps: Inspect the Process Studio and Agent logs to identify whether the failure is caused by a javassist bytecode parsing exception (e.g., 'invalid constant type: 19 at 4') or a plugin version mismatch (such as a workflow requiring GUI Plugin 4.6 or 4.7).
Take a backup copy of the existing javassist JAR file and any existing GUI Automation plugin JAR files located in the Process Studio or Agent lib directory to a secure temporary directory.

Replace the incompatible or corrupted JAR file in the Process Studio or Agent lib directory with the supported version (for javassist sync errors, deploy the latest compatible javassist JAR; for version mismatch issues, deploy the matching GUI Automation complete JAR such as version 4.6).
Restart Process Studio and the AutomationEdge Agent service to load the updated JAR dependencies.
Trigger a synchronization of the Web GUI / GUI Automation plugin from Process Studio.
Open the affected workflow in Process Studio and execute a test run to confirm that the GUI Automation plugin opens and executes without errors.

9bd2023d-b07f-4b34-916b-1673f206a44f.title: API Authentication Failure Due to Expired or Invalid Tokens
steps: Inspect the failing API request headers and response body to identify the exact HTTP status code and error description (e.g., HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 400 Bad Request with error 'invalid_grant').
When receiving HTTP 401 Unauthorized due to an expired access token, issue a token refresh request using the refresh token endpoint, or generate a new access token via client credentials.
When receiving HTTP 400 Bad Request with 'invalid_grant' during token exchange, re-initiate the user authorization flow to obtain a fresh, unconsumed authorization code.

If the error occurs within a packaged integration or connector (such as the ManageEngine plugin) failing to refresh tokens automatically, deploy the updated plugin JAR version containing token lifecycle fixes.
Perform a test API request with the newly issued token or through the updated integration plugin to verify successful authentication.

dd39c4cd-040c-421b-b7f8-8cbce76106dc.title: Workflow Processing Bottleneck and Queue Saturation Recovery
steps: Inspect the message broker queue depth, active memory utilization, and agent polling status to verify whether messages are accepted but stalled without delivery.

Check scheduler thread pool utilization and identify any single-threaded agent tasks running for extended durations (e.g., exceeding normal runtimes or approaching 45 minutes) that consume high host memory (>90%).
Purge stuck messages from the saturated ActiveMQ message queue.
Update any stale database entries associated with unassigned or stuck workflow requests to reset or cancel them.
Restart the ActiveMQ broker service and the dependent workflow application services.

Verify the broker memory configuration rule: ensure that Per-Queue Memory × Number of Queues ≤ Total Broker Memory. For systems with high load, adjust the JVM Heap between 2 GB – 4 GB (Broker Memory set to ~70% of heap, e.g., 2800 MB for 4 GB heap) and distribute per-queue memory accordingly.
Verify that agents resume polling, new workflow requests are delivered promptly, and queue backlogs remain clear under load.

a0df7f8b-2bd1-4f4c-b625-318d5069174b.title: DocEdge Installation Failure Due to AE Version Mismatch
steps: Check the currently installed AutomationEdge version on the Linux server and compare it against the target DocEdge version compatibility requirements.
Upgrade AutomationEdge to version 8.4.0 on the Linux server.
Verify that AutomationEdge 8.4.0 services are running properly, then retry the DocEdge installation or upgrade.

e721881f-dfd8-437a-9ae3-3026c6e9ff1d.title: Configuring the Workflow Restart Validity Period in AutomationEdge
steps: Determine the required restart retention window in days and check the current setting for ae.workflow.failed.retry.days in the AutomationEdge configuration (default is 7 days).

Set the property ae.workflow.failed.retry.days to the desired number of days in the AutomationEdge configuration file. Test and validate this change in a UAT environment before applying to Production.
Restart the AutomationEdge service to apply the modified configuration property.
Attempt to restart a failed workflow request that falls within the newly configured retention window.

a6e44405-7e44-4361-86bf-88afbd929da2.title: Apache ActiveMQ Vulnerability Remediation
steps: Stop the Apache ActiveMQ service and take a full backup of the installation directory, including the configuration directory (conf/) and the active message store (data/).
Upgrade the Apache ActiveMQ instance to the patched release or replace the flagged vulnerable dependency JAR files with secure versions in the library path.

Start the Apache ActiveMQ service, verify the process is active, check activemq.log for clean startup with no initialization exceptions, and run a dependency/file scan to confirm the vulnerable JAR is no longer present.

ac88a4fb-9313-4d31-9f16-e66173fe4c45.title: SMTP Connection Blocked by Antivirus
steps: Check the application and mail plugin logs for SMTP connection failure details and PKIS errors.
Open the local antivirus or endpoint protection console, review active firewall and mail shield rules, and configure an exception to allow outbound SMTP traffic for the application process and ports.
Trigger a test email or execute a mail send task from the application to verify the SMTP connection.
Verify that full antivirus protection remains enabled and active with only the necessary process or port exclusions applied.

fcb27a0a-3c72-4a03-98c5-54e8f53f343e.title: Intermittent Workflow Stalling or Incorrect Execution Troubleshooting Playbook
steps: Inspect the ActiveMQ broker queue depth and memory usage to determine if message delivery is stalled. Check if workflows are accumulating in the queue while agents poll without receiving assignments.

If ActiveMQ queue saturation has halted message delivery, purge stuck messages from the queue, clear stale database entries, update wrapper.java.maxmemory=2048 in <ActiveMQ_Install_Dir>\bin\win64\wrapper.conf, and restart the ActiveMQ and application services.

Inspect agent execution logs and process lists for hanging external tasks, unhandled exceptions in User Defined Java Class (UDJC) steps, or un-terminated sub-processes (such as 7-Zip or Selenium browser drivers).

Add mandatory execution timeouts to external script calls (e.g., archive extraction, command-line utilities) and wrap custom code steps (UDJC decryption, data formatting) in explicit try-catch error handling blocks to avoid thread deadlocks.
Check database connection logs and workflow execution logs for connection dropouts, query timeouts, or the specific error org.postgresql.core.v3.ConnectionFactoryImpl.enableSSL.

Update the PostgreSQL JDBC Connection String to explicitly specify the schema and disable SSL negotiation: jdbc:postgresql://<servername>/<database_name>?currentSchema=public&sslmode=disable, and configure appropriate query timeouts.
Verify workflow execution across multiple test runs to ensure workflows progress to completion without stalling or thread contention.

c554b0b9-14cb-4f98-9f97-a8a13ef5d72c.title: AI Studio VAPT Compliance Request Fulfillment
steps: Identify the exact version of AI Studio deployed by the customer (for example, AI Studio 3.4.0) and verify the specific security documentation requested.
Locate and retrieve the approved VAPT report and certificate corresponding to the confirmed AI Studio version from the internal security compliance repository.
Verify that an active Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) or customer data sharing agreement is in place before releasing confidential security audit documentation.
Send the VAPT report to the customer via the authorized support ticketing channel and resolve the request.

c78f9dbd-40e0-4ec2-8996-0b64f9d7e22d.title: Workflow State Unclear Due to Pending Customer Action
steps: Inspect the workflow execution logs and transaction history to identify the last completed state and verify that no internal errors are blocking progression.
Contact the customer with specific details about the stalled workflow state and request confirmation of their pending actions or schedule.
Place the incident ticket status on hold pending customer response and document the required actions.

ccd1376e-5d64-477b-946f-527686dbf9d6.title: Agent Workflow Failure Post-Plugin Update Due to Plugin Bug
steps: Verify that the exact same plugin version is deployed and active across both Process Studio and the target Agent environment.

Inspect the Process Studio and Agent logs for library corruption or bytecode parsing errors, such as 'java.io.IOException: invalid constant type' or 'Error while accessing JAR file: JAR might be corrupted' pointing to javassist or plugin JARs.
Back up the existing javassist JAR file from the Process Studio/Agent lib directory to a secure backup folder before making any file modifications.
Copy the latest javassist JAR file into the Process Studio/Agent lib directory, replace the existing JAR file, restart Process Studio, and perform the plugin synchronization again.
Execute the workflow on the Agent to verify end-to-end execution with the updated libraries.

If the workflow continues to fail on the Agent despite version alignment and library updates (e.g., handling variables in specific plugin fields like delay values), document the reproducible steps and escalate to engineering for an official plugin fix in the upcoming release.

d19964ce-5984-4a29-bbb5-11bf12c82259.title: URL 'Not Secure' Status Despite SSL Configuration
steps: Inspect the SSL certificate presented to external client browsers by examining the certificate details (issuer, subject alternative names, validity dates, and chain of trust).
Check if an external load balancer, reverse proxy, or firewall is terminating SSL/TLS traffic in front of the Nginx server and presenting a different certificate than the origin.

If the certificate is self-signed, invalid, or issued by an untrusted Certificate Authority (CA), request a valid, CA-signed certificate and full chain bundle from the customer or certificate management team.

If the Nginx SSL configuration is verified as correct and the issue is confirmed to reside in client-side trust stores or external network devices outside application control, provide technical findings to the customer team for closure.

d1fe7fc0-fe1d-44c1-b3eb-41e9d310a605.title: RDP Session State Impacting Automation Workflows
steps: Check if the UI automation is executing within a disconnected or unfocused RDP session and whether it is attaching to an already-running Chrome instance.
Reconfigure the automation workflow to launch a fresh Chrome instance per run with focus emulation instead of attaching to an existing browser process.
Keep the RDP session active and connected during workflow execution as an immediate workaround if launching fresh browser instances is not viable.
Run a test automation cycle to verify that 'Set Value' and 'Click' actions complete successfully without user intervention.

d826e870-3e43-4667-b413-cd2e0a32d540.title: API 400 Bad Request Due to Incorrect Usage or Payload
steps: Inspect the raw API request payload, headers, and query parameters generated by the client or portal.
Compare the captured request schema against the API reference specification to identify missing mandatory fields, invalid data formats, or invalid environment parameters.
Update the client request payload or portal configuration with the correct parameter values, format, and required headers.
Re-execute the API request or retry the creation action from the portal interface.

e1ac8ec2-61cc-4584-985e-455a9c94d6ac.title: Operational Challenges During Workflow Updates
steps: Determine the inquiry type by checking whether the ticket is a request for procedural assistance with deploying a workflow or an incident regarding process delays during a deployment.
Provide procedural guidance to the user and perform or assist with applying the verified workflow update to the production environment.
Inspect active job queues and execution logs to determine if running processes are stalling, experiencing locks, or if the reported delay was transient.

If process delays cannot be reproduced and workflow execution proceeds normally, confirm resolution with the client and close the ticket; if process stalls persist, escalate with execution logs to engineering.

e8d88aa8-d209-4564-a5e5-03fe65f64c3d.title: Endpoint Security Software Blocking Application Agent Startup
steps: Check the endpoint security software logs and alerts (e.g., Cortex XDR console or local agent logs) to identify whether the application agent or its child processes (such as javaw.exe) are being blocked or quarantined.
Inspect the blocked binary (e.g., javaw.exe) to verify its version, file path, and digital signature status.
Engage the endpoint security administration team with the documented binary details, file paths, and block logs to request an exception, policy update, or hash allowlisting in the security console.
Start the application agent service and verify that the process initializes completely without being terminated by endpoint security.

f404fc23-d442-4aac-900c-e080dc472617.title: User Account and Software License Management
steps: Identify the request type (new account creation, dormant account reactivation, or hardware license transfer) and identify the target user identity and application requirements.

Validate the user account state in the identity provider. If creating a new user, provision the account with appropriate baseline groups; if the account is dormant, remove the disable flag and restore active status.
Allocate or reassign the requested software license. For hardware replacements, revoke the license assignment from the old hardware or user profile before assigning it to the new endpoint.
Verify that the user can authenticate and launch the licensed application without license or activation errors.

f5ca046f-3ee8-48f4-8f39-c07e2421cf51.title: New Feature Planning and Guidance
steps: Review the requested feature specifications, identifying specific target integrations such as Azure OpenAI for policy search or ARC plugins for email retrieval.
Determine subscription models, authentication mechanisms, and API access requirements for third-party or client-managed integrations.
Provide technical implementation guidance, outlining integration patterns, component boundaries, and configuration requirements for the engineering team.

f8622c17-316d-4f2c-bc58-0f4a385c5e84.title: Messaging Queue Overload Affecting Schedulers
steps: Inspect the ActiveMQ broker memory usage and queue message counts to identify saturated queues.
Purge stuck messages from the saturated ActiveMQ queue.
Update any stale database entries associated with unassigned workflow requests.

Update the queue memory policy in activemq.xml to apply safe limits and enable producer flow control: <policyEntry queue=">" producerFlowControl="true" memoryLimit="200mb" maxPageSize="2000"/>. Ensure that Per-Queue Memory × Number of Queues ≤ Broker Memory.
Restart the ActiveMQ broker service and all dependent application scheduler services.
Verify that AE Schedulers deliver queued workflow requests and that polling agents successfully receive work.

0dbada03-034f-4c6a-b0d0-93a54d9bd20e.title: RPA Agent RDP Session Blocked by Unexpected UI Popup
steps: Log in to the RPA bot host via console or administrative session and identify the unexpected UI popup blocking the session.
Dismiss or handle the popup by selecting the appropriate button (such as Close, OK, or Remind Me Later) to clear the active screen.
Verify that the RPA Agent connects to the active RDP session and confirm that automated processes resume execution.
Identify the application that generated the popup and configure system policies or application preferences to disable automated popups, update alerts, and startup dialogs.

002da021-f87b-4173-b28b-3ded031dec41.title: ActiveMQ Service Unresponsive Despite Running
steps: Verify the ActiveMQ service status and confirm whether requests are accumulating in the queue while agents poll without receiving work.
Purge stuck messages from the ActiveMQ queue and update any stale database records associated with the unassigned requests.
Restart the ActiveMQ service and dependent application services to restore message delivery.
Submit a test request and verify that agents successfully pick up and execute workflow tasks from the queue.
To prevent recurrence under high workload, open <ActiveMQ_Install_Dir>\bin\win64\wrapper.conf, set wrapper.java.maxmemory=2048, and restart the ActiveMQ service.

0d221c82-2cf5-495e-a722-522873a47f33.title: Middleware Service Startup/Stability Issues Post-Maintenance
steps: Inspect the ActiveMQ and Tomcat startup logs to identify the exact point of failure: check for Java execution permission denials, KahaDB file lock errors, port binding conflicts (such as shutdown port 8005), or broker connection issues.
If ActiveMQ cannot start because OS patching restricted access to Java, restore execute and read permissions for the service user across the entire Java installation directory.

If ActiveMQ fails to acquire a lock on the shared KahaDB location due to a lingering process or duplicate instance, terminate the stale ActiveMQ process or restart the host server to release the shared file lock.
If Tomcat fails to start because port 8005 is occupied by another process, edit the Tomcat server configuration to assign an unused port for the shutdown port, such as changing port 8005 to 8006.

If ActiveMQ connection parameters need tuning or updating, configure the broker failover URL in the ae.properties file using the format activemq.broker.url=failover:(tcp://<machine1-IP/Hostname>:<port>,tcp://<machine2-IP/Hostname>:<port>) and restart the AutomationEdge Tomcat services.
Verify that all services start successfully and monitor the ActiveMQ and application logs for reconnect warnings or broker connectivity issues.

142617ee-cd98-48dd-8c1a-3d745c8d8a4f.title: Resolving Workflow Failures Due to Missing Dynamic Folders
steps: Inspect the failing workflow step logs (such as the Excel Writer step) to identify the missing target directory path and verify at what point file creation fails.
Add or update the Modified JavaScript Value (MJSV) step prior to the file output step to validate whether the target folder exists before calling folder creation utilities.

In the Modified JavaScript Value step, call createFolder() to dynamically generate the required directory when it does not exist, and pass the resolved directory path to the downstream writer step (such as Excel Writer).
Execute the workflow and verify that the target directory is created if missing, that no 'Folder Already Exists' error is raised on repeated runs, and that output files are written successfully.

e3b053bb-bfc5-4c55-819f-28086fb3466a.title: New Component Adoption Blocked by Customer Security Review
steps: Obtain the formal security questionnaire and itemized list of compliance concerns from the customer infosec team.
Prepare and submit detailed technical answers and architectural documentation addressing each infosec query.
Follow up with the customer point of contact to confirm receipt and verify if security clearance is granted or further clarification is needed.

4a88d1e6-21b9-4e1c-9db5-aa110e4c72eb.title: Plugin Incompatibility with Custom Database Object Types
steps: Inspect the stored procedure signature and identify the parameter types causing the plugin execution failure, checking specifically for custom collection or record types like weo_rec_strings30_list.
Bypass the database plugin by implementing the stored procedure call directly in application code (such as Java) using native database connectivity drivers that support custom object mapping.
Execute a test call with the custom object payload using the newly implemented direct application code and verify the stored procedure output.

373750cc-779b-4ae3-b5bb-d3c7e5e3f2d3.title: Customer Missing Operational Notifications
steps: Check if the customer contact email is currently enrolled in the T4 user notification list.
Add the customer contact email to the T4 user notification list.
Send a confirmation response to the customer stating that they have been added to the notification list, then close the ticket.

207407ab-6288-4a7d-a6e3-a4fe06c44ea4.title: Web GUI Workflow Browser Instantiation Failure
steps: Identify the installed AutomationEdge version (7.x or 8.x) and verify if the workflow error log displays 'Can not instantiate browser due to compatibility issue'.
Update the Web GUI plugin file: install web-gui-4.2.jar for AutomationEdge 8.x, or install web-gui-3.24.jar for AutomationEdge 7.x.
For Process Studio execution, open the process-studio.bat file in a text editor and append the JVM flag -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true to the startup configuration.

For Agent execution, add the JVM flag -DignoreDeprecatedExperimentalOptions=true based on the platform version: for AutomationEdge 8.x, open the AE UI, navigate to the Agents tab, select Edit Agent, and add the parameter; for AutomationEdge 7.x, navigate to the Agent installation directory, open the bin folder, edit startup.bat, and add the flag.
Restart the Agent or Process Studio instance and re-execute the Web GUI workflow to verify that the browser launches and the workflow completes successfully.

65dd1912-d832-44d6-bf4b-eac1e32ce615.title: Resolving Advanced REST Client Parameter Conflicts and Malformed Requests in AutomationEdge
steps: Inspect the AutomationEdge execution log and locate the failed REST step. Check whether the failure reports 'EXTRA_PARAM_FOUND', an 'Illegal character in path' error, or a malformed request URL.

Review the parameter definitions in the Advanced REST Client step to check if any parameter key matches its assigned value with only case or exact character similarity (for example, key 'entity' and value 'Entity').

Modify the conflicting parameter value to use a distinct string or variable name (for example, change the value from 'Entity' to 'Entityvalue' or map to a distinct workflow variable) so the plugin does not misidentify the value as a duplicate key definition.

Open the workflow and configure the Generate Rows step to declare all request parameters separately: define individual fields for base URL, query fields (q), payload fields, and authorization tokens rather than concatenating them into a single raw URL string.
Execute the workflow within AutomationEdge and verify that the Advanced REST Client step finishes with a success status code and valid server payload response.

f7d9578e-ea14-46c4-9a40-200b21ceb08b.title: GUI Plugin Variable Inoperability in Max Timeout Field Post-Upgrade
steps: Inspect the installed version of AutomationEdge, Process Studio, and the GUI Plugin across both the development environment and all execution Agents.
Open the failing workflow in Process Studio and inspect the Max Timeout configuration field in the affected GUI plugin step (such as 'Set Value') to confirm variable syntax is used.
Back up the existing GUI plugin JAR files from both Process Studio and Agent plugin directories to an external backup folder outside the active classpath.

Deploy the official Plugins 4.8 release (or vendor-provided hotfix JAR) into the plugin directories of both Process Studio and all Agent instances. Completely remove older, duplicate, or backup JAR files from the active plugin folders to avoid classloader conflicts.
Restart Process Studio and the Agent service, then run a test execution of the workflow containing variables in the Max Timeout field.

a3b7fdad-2bbb-4b0e-9168-767fa46b4e8b.title: Customer Issue Diagnosis Hindered by Insufficient Evidence
steps: Inspect the customer-provided screenshots and log attachments to determine whether software component versions, error codes, and full system context are legible.
Request that the customer provide high-resolution screenshots, direct text copy of error output, or diagnostic log files covering the affected components.
If the customer requests ticket closure due to inability to obtain clear evidence, document the specific missing details in the ticket notes and close the ticket per customer request.

1d615cbb-7282-442b-8124-973844f2049e.title: Automation Edge Version Upgrade & Licensing Management
steps: Open CMD on the Automation Edge host server and execute the command getmac to retrieve the current physical MAC address.
Cross-verify the output MAC address with the MAC address recorded in the ae_license database table and the uploaded license file.
If a MAC address mismatch is identified, contact the customer IT team to determine why the network interface or MAC address changed and request that they revert it to the previous MAC address.

If the MAC address rollback is not possible or an upgrade invalidates existing licensing, submit a request to the license team to issue an updated license or temporary trial license matching the host details.
